Title: Playing Maggie... The Iron Lady
Description: Pip Utton is a Fringe favourite. He is recognised as one of the world’s leading solo performers and writers for his spellbinding portrayals of Hitler, Bacon, Dickens, Chaplin, Churchill and the Hunchback. His performances have garnered praise and many awards internationally. Playing Maggie won the Stage Special Award 2015, the FringeReview.co.uk Outstanding Theatre Award 2015 and the Valery Kazhanov Award 2016, presented at the Fujairah International Arts Festival by the International Theatre Institute. ‘A remarkable and original show’ (Guardian). ‘Landslide satisfaction’ (Daily Telegraph). ‘Evocative, provocative… fascinating hour’ (TheatreGuideLondon.co.uk).

Title: Fluff - A Story of Lost Toys
Description: In a world of odd size boxes, night-lights and little wooden beds, lives the slightly quirky Gingham family.  Welcome to the mad, mod world of the Ginghams, a cheerful trio who travel to rescue lost toys. Fluff was under the couch, Squibbly in the gutter and Disco Frog caught in a ceiling fan. But don't fret - in this comedic, off-the-wall story, with its humorous projections, these toys are discovered and recovered by the kindly plaid-patterned family.  Told with originality, warmth and an extraordinary combination of vocal sounds, movement, music and intriguing sampling of audience members, this refreshing and have a story to tell.

This fast-paced hour of family fun includes haunted backpacks, ninja grans, vomiting puppets, alien attacks, toilet-paper cannons and an actual 6D movie filmed every show. Burns’ key poems and songs are performed to a cracking live musical accompaniment, along with discussion, context, and English subtitles. A sell-out at Fringe 2014, TradFest Edinburgh 2014 and Burnsfest 2015 and 2016, this is the show about Burns that Burns would want to see! Includes poems To a Mouse, Holy Willie’s Prayer, Tam O’Shanter, and songs You’re Welcome Willie Stewart, Green Grow the Rashes, Ae Fond Kiss, A Man's A Man and Auld Lang Syne.

Title: Grandad Died
Description: ‘You have papers, you have food delivered to you twice weekly... all this talk of leaving, who do you think you are?’ Brian and Aaron are about to leave here to go there. They await the arrival of their friend Mary and contemplate both the society in which they live, and whether they should try to leave. What is happening over the hill? Does anyone ever make it back? Grandad Died is an absurdist comedy about two men contemplating the society in which they live and their role within it. Aaron wears orange, Brian wears a potato sack.

Explore and learn with Fraxi in her ever-changing forest home. Title: Company
Description: At the age of 25, Bobbi should be finding the one. When her friends aren't fighting or lying to their soulmates they worry about their poor baby, Bobbi. She's all alone. To her, commitment is unthinkable; constantly sharing, caring, compromising would be insufferable. But every day she finds it harder to justify the single life she used to enjoy. Sondheim’s masterpiece about New York’s most eligible bachelor is remixed for the 21st century. The first concept musical is transformed into a story of modern loneliness, independence and self-discovery. Regardless of who we love, don’t we all still need company?

Through original cabaret songs, we hear Nils’ inspiring story full of heart and, surprisingly, humour. Taking us from an island in the tropics through 35 surgeries, amputation and tough rehabilitation, we learn how this one-legged man redefined himself, managed to cohabit with his disability and eventually to rise again. An entertaining show from an internationally trained musical artist, full of charm, honest observations and personal wit creating a must see, heart-warming and enlightening production.

Told through Jane's eyes, this autobiographical novel shocked the Victorians, and Charlotte Brontë's gothic subversion of fairy tale romance is now distilled for the stage (under its full title) by writer/director Elton Townend-Jones. Title: Bedtime Balancing Act
Teaser: Treat yourself to a good nights sleep by building your very own mini mobile!
Description:
We all know that getting to sleep at night can be very tricky. In connection with Dermatological Distractors, this workshop is a fun and interactive look at sleep and what helps us get to sleep. Come along and share your favourite bedtime story, and get stuck-in making a mini mobile from bold, colourful shapes and wire. With a little bit of time and practice, learn how to balance your mini mobile creation so that it hovers above your head, then take it home and hang it up to help you get to sleep at night! 

If you can't seem to find the land of nod at night, then this is the event for you.

This is a free event (drop-in) and all children must be accompanied by an adult.

Title: A Serious Game (Den allvarsamma leken)
Description: A tale of forbidden love set against the backdrop of Stockholm at the beginning of the 20th century, Lone Scherfig’s astute adaptation of Hjalmar Söderberg’s 1912 novel is a striking costume drama directed with real style by Pernilla August. It follows the love affair between Arvid (Sverrir Gudnason) and Lydia (Karin Franz Korlof), unable to marry because both are too poor, but still drawn to each other when older and wealthier. Despite their marriage to other partners they cannot resist each other, and drama lurks around a melodramatic corner. [PG]

Title: Alison Gopnik & Sue Palmer
Subtitle: The Children are Our Future

Description: Two specialists offer some radical thinking. In The Gardener and the Carpenter, developmental psychologist Alison Gopnik argues that parenting has become a multi-billion dollar industry and childcare has been transformed into a controlling and goal-oriented system. Education expert Sue Palmer, in Upstart, states the case for raising the school starting age to 7 because starting at age 4 is an accident of economics, not what’s best for the child. Chaired by Sarfraz Manzoor.

Title: Chris Dugdale – Full Circle
Description: You decide the ending. I will try and bring it Full Circle. Twelve royal performances, astonishing magic and mind control. 'What a pleasure to have met you and be amazed by your magic' (Jimmy Page). 'The best I've seen, brilliant' (Sir Richard Branson). 'This guy is amazing' (Simon Cowell). 'The most unbelievable ending of any trick ever' (ITV). As seen on NBC, The CW, ITV, ITV News, BBC One and yes, Blue Peter! Fifth appearance at the festival! This time it's personal... 7204071521010. Don't read these two words! Foreheads. Pets.

'Olaf Falafel is an idiot, and wouldn’t have it any other way' (Steve Bennett, Chortle.co.uk). ‘Skilfully delivered absurdist musings’ (ThreeWeeks). ‘Olaf Falafel is like a chocolate digestive – very moreish’ (Bruce Dessau, BeyondTheJoke.co.uk).

Fringe fun with great food and world class tutoring on Scotland's national drink. What more could you want at 9.15pm every evening, Monday to Friday, during the Fringe? Description: Lynne Jassem brings her moving solo show From Como to Homo to Edinburgh. In it she tells the story of a 10-year-old juggling her career on live TV in 1957 with the demands of her stage mother, a former Rockette, and a burgeoning awareness of her gender dysphoria. She tells her tale through tap-dancing, mime, physical comedy and song.

The protagonist of this tale is the curious house on Winchester Road, where the various inhabitants report unexplainable occurrences. Suspend your disbelief and follow an investigation that spirals beyond rationality. In the search for answers, witnesses relive their encounters; presences emerge and the fragile lines between normal and paranormal blur exponentially.

Description: Described as Scotland's ‘very own Tori Amos’ (Sunday Herald) and ‘a heady cocktail of Carole King and Regina Spektor’ (SpiralEarth.co.uk), Kim’s live performances have been noted for their intimacy and intensity. Celebrate the launch of her third solo album, Stories Untold, and hear songs from this alongside favourites from her previously acclaimed albums, performed on grand piano, acoustic guitar and voice. ‘Moving, literate, allusive and expressively sung’ ***** (Scotland on Sunday). ‘Inspired empathy... an artist clearly at the top of her game' ***** (FringeReview.co.uk). ‘Unusually impressive... an achingly honest voice’ **** (BroadwayBaby.com). ‘Superb’ **** (Daily Record).

Outside their comfort zone and coming to grips with their inner beast, the Latino lover, the pushover, the best buddy and others enter a quiet battle for man’s right to be himself. Teaser: During its years of empire, British colonisers seized land, property and goods from across the globe. Some of our cherished visitor attractions now proudly display cultural artefacts acquired by means that often amounted to theft. In Keeping Their...
Description: During its years of empire, British colonisers seized land, property and goods from across the globe. In Keeping Their Marbles, cultural sociologist Tiffany Jenkins explores the arguments for repatriation and sets out the controversial case for artefacts to stay where they are.

Description: A captivating period drama about a strained relationship between father and son, Jason Connery’s enthralling film is set against the fascinating backdrop of the early days of professional golf: when golf balls had to be painted, when backspin on a chip shot was practically unheard of and when it wasn’t unusual for fights to break out when betting got too intense. Scottish acting legend Peter Mullan is perfectly cast as the ordered and loyal Old Tom Morris, the man who helped set up the Open Championship and went on to win it four times. He would become greenkeeper at the Royal and Ancient Club at St Andrews, where he established a club-making shop overlooking the 18th green, and where he hoped his son Tommy would follow in his respectful footsteps. Young Tommy (Jack Lowden, BBC’s War & Peace) has plans of his own, and sets out to become the ‘dashing young man of golf’, challenging traditions, drawing spectators and becoming golf’s first touring pro. This beautifully directed film is an uplifting, amusing and dramatic story of two men united by the love of a sport. The film also features an impressive performance by Ophelia Lovibond as Tommy’s wife Meg, and makes great use of some spectacular Scottish locations. Director Jason Connery commented: “It is a story that is truly close to my heart as I grew up with my father on a golf course and I have a home an hour from St Andrews. It is an extraordinary and intimate tale of love and family at the beginning of the great game of golf.” [PG]

Description:

'Joe Davies has true funny bones, a glorious loon' (John Kearns). 'Just look at his face. Of course he's funny' (Rob Beckett).

Freckles is not to be missed!

Title: Tales of a Grandson
Description: Where do you begin to tell the story of Scotland? With the myths, the legends and the battles? Or by building a castle in your granny's back green?  Tales of a Grandson is one man’s re-telling of Scotland's history - but this is no straight and dusty history lesson, this story is told by Andy Cannon, formerly of Wee Stories and one of Scotland’s finest story-tellers.  Andy takes us on a time travelling adventure with his grandparents through Scotland’s past to piece together the myriad of Kings, Queens, friends and foes that make up our nation's story (and unearths just why our mountains are so small on the way!).   Accompanying Andy and adding to the Tales is composer and musician Wendy Weatherby.
Artist: Andy Cannon, Wendy Weatherby and Red Bridge Arts

Part monologue, part stand-up comedy and a lot of the kind of guitar-playing that moved Ed Ward of National Public Radio to call John 'one of the great guitarists of our time.' It's a funny, poignant and in the end a story of personal transformation.

The arrival of Arthur Clennam and a pocket watch with the words Do Not Forget written inside symbolises a new beginning for the Dorrit family and the uncovering of family secrets. Title: The Rose and Crown
Description: In turns comic, moving and spine-chilling, this one-act play is a rarely seen masterpiece by the author of Time and the Conways and An Inspector Calls. In the late 1940s Britain has won the war but victory is forgotten as food, clothing and much else is still rationed. Homes are cold, cities dreary and the future seems bleak. In a London pub a group of drinkers – men and women, young and old – find plenty to complain about in their lives. Then a stranger enters and makes an unusual request.

Title: Lunch
Description: Luke Courtier presents Lunch, a high-octane series of musical comedy vignettes asking that vital question: well what is it that really happens at Lunch, narratively speaking? From the fashionable perils of adequate dog size, to an ill fortune horrific death in Knightsbridge, the woes of the largely forgotten Thomas Duke of Clarence and the doomed travails of a goose called David and a duck called Susan. This is a veritable treasure chest of song, mirth, searing relevance and that distinct fleeting victory one feels after satisfyingly grasping the very last Saucisson-Sec from the charcuterie aisle of the Fulham Waitrose.

Title: Confetti
Description: Cal believes he’s diagnosed with a sickening love for Lliope, believing she is his dream girl. He manifests Lliope in his mind to help somehow sedate his obsessions. When the true Lliope presents herself, she challenges him to a deep and dark understanding of the powers of infatuation and desire. From the anxious dreamscape of Cal’s imagination, his obsessions wrestle her ruthlessness. With themes of desire, escape, ideologies of love, and the world of the artist, Sublevel Theater Group will present a wild play that poetically examines the unsuspecting consequences of model love stained by desire.

Title: Tales of Don Roberto
Description: Writer Jamie Jauncey grew up with stories from the extraordinary life of his great-grand-uncle, Robert Cunninghame Graham, politician, author, horseman and adventurer. But who was “Don Roberto” really, and what was it like to have such a figure as part of the family backdrop? Experience afresh one of Scotland’s most gallant adventurers in art, life and politics.

Title: Pop-Up Science: Nest Building
Teaser: Get hands-on to find out why and how birds build nests
Description: Get hands-on to find out why and how birds build nests. Explore the pieces of art and architecture that are influenced by bird nests. Examine nests from local and exotic birds, match the bird to the nest that it built and build a nest of your own to take home or leave in our special museum trees.

Title: Intergalactic Nemesis: Twin Infinity – A Live Action Graphic Novel
Description: The smash hit from America crash lands into Edinburgh in a UK premiere. When Pulitzer Prize-winning reporter Molly Sloan’s fiancé doesn’t show up to the altar, she discovers more than her wedding (the fate of the globe, perhaps?) hangs in the balance. Three actors, one Foley artist, a pianist, and over a thousand comic book panels tell a story like no other. Comics meet radio drama in this hilarious, one-of-a-kind, nerd-tastic spectacle for the kid in everyone. ‘If you haven’t seen it yet… what are you waiting for?’ (Austin Chronicle).

Title: Paul McCaffrey: Fresh Hell
Description: Star of Impractical Jokers (BBC Three), Russell Howard’s Good News (BBC Three), and Stand Up Central (Comedy Central), Paul returns with a brand new stand-up show. ‘A brilliantly entertaining hour full of laughs, beautifully delivered. It is almost impossible to dislike him, some of them leave the gig thinking they may have a new best mate. He has a warmth and vulnerability. There are no gags, no puns, no clunky links, every story, every deviation feels honest, unexaggerated and heartfelt’ (Chortle.co.uk). ‘A total natural, his storytelling is utterly unique, never anything less than gut-bustingly hilarious’ (GQ).

This outstanding group perform a highly original mixture of jazz and world music, crafting lyrical melodies around infectious grooves. Featuring tender balladeering, straight-ahead modern jazz, drum'n'bass and Brazilian baiao and choro, the ensemble's performances have attracted much acclaim. Expect highly accomplished musicianship, modern jazz with a keen respect for the tradition, deftly-crafted, yet powerful. ‘Assured and inventive’ (Scotsman). ‘Strikingly good’ (LondonJazzNews.com). ‘A classy and well-crafted debut’ (BBC Radio 3). Made in Scotland winner 2014.

Author Michael Horowitz (Burn Notice, Prison Break) crafted these steamy masterpieces under his nom-de-porn Philip S. Wilson while working at such a cable network in the early 2000s. Now he's bringing all the tawdry, tempting and titillating action directly to you. Prepare yourself for a rollicking good time as, like our narrator repeatedly reminds us, 'hot sex ensues!'

The ICCA UK 2016 champions and CARA award-winning a cappella group, The Techtonics, were founded to help sociopathic male science students at Imperial College escape the library and discover life after labs. Four American tours later, they return to the Fringe with a show combining singing of the highest standard, comedy and classy choreography. As for the button, well, hopefully it will have been tamed (a bit) by the show, but please… don’t push the button!

Uninterested in the life his family expect him to lead, Jack becomes further drawn into the darker secrets of this alternative circle. A beautifully shot, supremely enjoyable drama, this debut from director Chris Foggin features engaging performances from young stars including Will Poulter and Cara Delevingne. [15]

Description: Scotland's fresh new opera company present a unique production of Charpentier's Descent Of Orpheus to the Underworld in an exciting Scots language translation. Roll up! Roll up! Come and see the weird and wonderful characters of the circus bring the legend to life as never before. Charpentier's score is brimming with beauty, drama and heartfelt emotion, performed by some of Scotland's rising stars.

Title: Molhados&Secos – Wet and Dry
Description: An almost word-free physical and visual performance from Brazilian company ParaladosanjoS. A poignant, poetic and sometimes comically absurd reflection on human fragility in the face of nature, inspired by the real and reimagined stories of people who have suffered the onslaught of natural disasters. Four distinct scenes directed by four different directors of international renown explore the human capacity to overcome obstacles and survive extreme situations. The show has toured extensively in South America: this is their UK premiere. ‘At times dramatic, at times comic, always visually enchanting’ (TotalTheatre.co.uk).

Title: Feel-Link
Description: Airida Gudaite and Laurynas Žakevicius represent a new generation of Lithuanian dancers and choreographers. In this piece they bring a fresh approach to a timeless topic: a pair of dancers explore the feelings and insights evoked by a couple’s experience of love past, present and future. A free urban dance style utilising the full capability of the body breathes an expressive vitality into reflections on the love they have felt and that which they still seek to feel. Set to a reinterpretation of Nina Simone’s Feelings, Feel-Link is a captivating performance for anyone who has ever been in love.

The scars of the Lebanese civil war haunt this introspective mystery story, which is given heart and soul thanks to Farahani’s charismatic central performance. [PG]

Description: Agnes Török is a Swedish spoken word performer living and working in Edinburgh. Her projects include shows such as If You’re Happy and You Know It - Take This Survey and a debut spoken word album Poetry // Resistance. Chimwemwe Undi was raised in southern Africa, of Chewa heritage, and is now a spoken word poet living in Winnipeg, Canada. Speaking powerfully of the immigrant experience, she explores what it means to call a place home.

Title: Ofgagged
Description: Sketch Club 7 (six schoolboys and a blow-up doll) return to the Fringe after a triumph last year (‘terrifyingly brilliant’ BroadwayBaby.com). Yet this year something is wrong, there’s been political incorrectness in the group and Ofgag, the comedy regulator, must inspect the show. Whilst rebel fighters consider the merits of bombing the death star, and Captain Comedy saves the day, the Ofgag inspector does his best to take over the show, in a tale of revenge, betrayal and so-called lols. This young dynamic group pulls it off again with a marvellously constructed and hilariously witty show. **** (Wandsworth Radio).

Description: Go with your intuition and join us for a rare opportunity to explore paranormal mysteries with the Koestler Parapsychology Unit. Skeptics and believers welcome.

Title: Jess Smith

Description: Back in 1982, as she watched her father’s life ebbing away, Jess Smith promised him that she would write a history of Scottish Travellers, setting the record straight about a group of people so often discriminated against. Title: Where Do Ideas Come From?
Description:
In partnership with the Wellcome Trust, join a panel of novelists, screenwriters and neuroscience researchers to consider the creative process of generating ideas. How does an idea happen? What is inspiration? How different is writing a story from remembering, or dreaming? Bring your own enquiring mind, and every question you ever wanted answering about the magic - and science - of ideas. [U]
The panel will be moderated by story editor Kate Leys.
Wellcome Panel Biographies

CHRISTOPHER BROOKMYRE
He is a writer and director, known for Bedlam (2014), Quite Ugly One Morning (2004) and Scotland on Screen (2009). Christopher is the author of eighteen published novels to-date, the latest being Dead Girl Walking.

RACHEL TUNNARD
Rachel is a writer director and editor. Her short film EMOTIONAL FUSEBOX was nominated for a BAFTA and a BIFA. It also won the audience award at the British Shorts Film Festival, Berlin and the Jury Prize for Best Fiction at the This Is England Film Festival, Rouen.
Her first feature, ADULT LIFE SKILLS, won the Nora Ephron Prize at Tribeca Film Festival (2016). It premieres at Edinburgh Film Festival in June 2016 and is released in the UK on June 24th. Rachel has a second feature in development with Film 4 and a TV project with Channel 4.

DR SUE FLETCHER WATSON
Sue is a developmental psychologist, holding the post of Chancellor’s Fellow at the University of Edinburgh. She is an associate of the Patrick Wild Centre for research into autism, fragile X syndrome and intellectual disabilities and of The Salvesen Mindroom Centre to understand and resolve learning difficulties.

DR DANIEL GLASER
Dr Daniel Glaser is a neuroscientist who has worked for many years promoting public engagement with science. He is Director of Science Gallery London at King’s College London, a new space where art and science collide to be constructed opposite the Shard. Previously he was Head of Engaging Science at Wellcome Trust, commissioning and funding public engagement and arts projects.

In the late 1990s, a collection of musicians from Chemikal Underground Records hired a bus and headed off on a road trip to a town in rural France to play a one-off gig. Now they are headed back to relive the experience.
From Mogwai to Franz Ferdinand, The Delgados to RM Hubbert, Chemikal Underground defines the independent record scene in Scotland from the mid 90s until present day. Lost in France, in exploring a small moment in its history, defines what has made the label and its acts so adored by fans around the world.

Mike Garry has toured with John Cooper Clarke, had a number one single with St Anthony, An Ode to Anthony H Wilson in August 2015 and works with artists including Philip Glass, New Order and The Charlatans.

Title: Betty Blue (37°2 le matin)
Description: Crucially harnessing the wild, rebellious energy of his then unknown leading lady, Beatrice Dalle, to spectacular effect, and perfectly pairing her with the wonderful Jean-Hugues Anglade (Subway, Nikita), Beineix raises the ‘Cinema du look’ temperature, slowly blurring passionate romance into hard drama and ultimately, bleak tragedy against a cynically bright, pastel coloured backdrop. Adapted from a novel by Philippe Djian, Beineix’s intense, fractured love story became an international success, and went on to represent France in the Best Foreign Language Film section at the 1987 Academy Awards. [18]

Title: Discretion Guaranteed
Description: How do women protect themselves in the digital world? Discretion Guaranteed explores the world of bloggers, female gamers and sex workers and their never-ending battle against the onslaught of abuse. A fast-paced, highly physical and decisively funny feminist piece that doesn’t shy away from hitting the mark.
Warnings: Strong language used at times

Title: Regrouping
Description: First screened at EIFF in 1976, Borden’s multi-layered film within a film is the highlight of this year’s retrospective focus on the 1970s. It follows the activities of a women’s group, whose political ideals are unraveled and questioned throughout the process of collaboration. The film’s self-reflexive techniques keep the viewer guessing about the relationship between the real and the staged, dismantling the objective foundations of the documentary form. A powerful and rarely seen classic of feminist filmmaking. [15]

Title: The Bookbinder
Description: They say you can get lost in a good book...  The Bookbinder  is a story of mystery, intrigue and charm. Peculiar things happen when a boy leaves home to make his fortune and finds himself learning the crafts of an apprentice bookbinder. In true storytelling style he is warned that he should not do anything that cannot be undone.  With the arrival of a mysterious customer and an unusual book in need of repair, an atmospheric epic fable begins.  A handkerchief, a missing page and a gap in the world is wonderfully woven around the ramifications of the price of cutting corners. A delicious dark walk towards danger, The Bookbinder is told with a wink, shadow-play, pop-up book paper art, puppetry and exquisite music.

Description: A sparkling band of genre-minded directors – including Kevin Smith (Yoga Hosers), Gary Shore and Nicholas McCarthy – each take inspiration from a different holiday to craft a grim and scary tale, guaranteed to make you think differently about holiday seasons. An unflinching look at the unravelling of one woman's life, Fabric exposes the shifting roles and expectations of women in today's society and asks how, if ever, they can be fulfilled. This powerful new play is written by Abi Zakarian, directed by Tom O'Brien and stars West End actress Nancy Sullivan. You can never catch up with yourself once that first thread is pulled…

Flesh is a duet of volatile and fleeting realities that seduces and mesmerizes.

Title: Bringing Death Back to Life
Description: Dying is a universal human activity, and it shows no sign of abating. Despite the impact of non-smoking campaigns and the value of various screening and early diagnosis initiatives, death will still be 100% fatal for every single one of us. Given we cannot evade it, is it time to face up to death? Should we be planning our own death the way we plan our wedding? Or is there no point planning for something inevitable (and terrifying)? Scott Murray, a leading palliative care researcher, asks when, where and how would you like to die?

This area of Blackwell’s is now a suspected crime scene, open to you, our Science Festival detectives. During the investigation, your job will be to establish murderer, motive and weapon. Join us to examine the crime scene, exploring rare blood disorders and learning how blood stains can be used to solve crimes.

Title: Edinburgh's Christmas
Description: Edinburgh's Christmas is a spectacular, six-week season of festive entertainment in the heart of the city. Taking place across multiple locations, the festival features a host of shows, as well as ice skating, markets and rides, including the Big Wheel and the 60-metre Star Flyer, with breathtaking views over the city. Free event include the return of the Street of Light in a new location on West George Street, and the big Christmas lights switch-on on 20 November. With millions of visitors every year, the festival is a fantastic Christmas celebration, and great fun for the whole family!

St Andrew Square features the Spiegeltent, where our shows take place, the Scottish Market, the helter skelter, one of our two fantastic carousels, a brand new ice rink and bars serving something to warm you up! Title: Three Nights With John
Description: In six years of bible storytelling, Yorick has built a reputation for delivering John's Gospel with a gripping performance storytelling style that is authentic and accessible. Revealing an honesty and directness in the text, he delivers it word for word and verse for verse, using no props, no costume and no special effects – just voice, face and movement. It is powerful, quick, witty, intense, riveting, real, refreshing and totally captivating. Yorick brings John's Gospel to life in a remarkable way, with a singularly unique voice that is not to be missed!

It features the effects of Bernie Sanders, dates ending up in rivers, toasters at parties, and the result of a video gaming tax relief break. It has everything that they’ve learnt in life. Title: Middle Age Came Quick!
Description: How does it feel and what do you do about it when old age catches up with you 10 years before you even suspect it's chasing you? When everywhere you look, you see the people around you getting older, and every celebrity you ever loved dying? Time flies whether you are having fun or not, so those years where you didn't really do what you wanted come back to fill you with loss, and guilt. A funny show (I hope), where I want audience experience as much as my own.

Description: Much has been written about the Russian Revolution, but Helen Rappaport’s new account, Caught in the Revolution, is told through the eyes of foreign nationals who witnessed events as they unfolded. Title: The Gin Whore Tour
Description: Take a sip of sin and tonic! You'll enjoy four of the finest gins during this slightly naughty one-woman show. Delve into historical tales of hooch and harlots to celebrate the modern gin renaissance.
Warnings: Adult themes. Alcohol tastings are included.
Venue description: Situated in the heart of Edinburgh’s West End, lies the Devils Cut our boutique style basement which offers a unique, quirky and stylish space with a ‘1920s speakeasy’ vibe. Devils Cut is known as the hidden gem of the West End, which in it self’s boasts a beautiful restaurant and bar with live performances every weekend!

Title: Amnesty International Imprisoned Writers Series
Subtitle: Diaries of Child Refugees
Teaser: The image of the lifeless body of a toddler swept ashore provoked an outcry about the death of refugees fleeing for their lives. Amnesty International's research shows that children remain the most vulnerable of refugees, facing violence, exploitation...
Description: The image of the lifeless body of a toddler swept ashore provoked an outcry about the death of refugees fleeing for their lives. Amnesty International's research shows that children remain the most vulnerable of refugees, facing violence, exploitation and sexual harrassment. Today, authors reading the stories written by child refugees include Emily Dodd, Jenny Downham, Cecilia Ekbäck and Sean Taylor.

Title: EVENT CANCELLED - Nature's TARDIS
Teaser: Discover how translocation can provide endangered species with a second chance.
Description: Time travel to restore extinct species is pure science fiction, but we can successfully bring back locally extinct species, as Scotland’s sea eagles have shown. Translocation can provide endangered species with a second chance, but only if we understand the reasons for their decline. Botanist and TV naturalist Sally Eaton will lead a discussion with Dr Sarah Robinson from the Royal Zoological Society of Scotland, Prof Chris Thomas from the University of York and Andrew Bauer from the National Farmers Union Scotland to explore the science and potential impact of translocation.

Title: John Muir: Rhapsody in Green
Description: Directed by Patrick Sandford. A declaration of love for the wilderness based on the writings of the Scottish mountaineer and environmentalist, performed by Mike Maran with a soundtrack of glaciers, huskies and Native American song.
Venue description: Festival Fringe productions in The Little Theatre 'beyond the treasure house of salamis, cheeses, balsamic vinegars and olive oils' ([i]Sunday Times[/i]). 'If anything makes a London-based gourmet jealous of the Scots, it is Valvona & Crolla' ([i]Financial Times[/i]).
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site, Some areas not reachable by lift or level access, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, On street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. Venue accessible by wheelchair user who can move on to chairlift. Plenty able-bodied help to assist

Title: Absence of Separation
Description: This new play is a bleak Beckettian comedy drama punctuated with physical theatre, spoken word, clowning and live songs. It tells the story and delves deep in to the minds of the two protagonists, ready to either redefine themselves or give up on life altogether. Delving in to existential philosophy, they argue about the surreal absurdity of life, fight for their beliefs, question everything, dissect their dreams, give a squirrel a parking ticket and almost lose their minds. The play touches on Vedanta Hinduism, Zen Buddhism, spirituality, contemporary society, depression, consciousness, psychology, dreams, addiction and fairy tales.
Venue description: Fringe venue 333

Title: Totally Wired: Trigger Warning!
Description: Presenting Trigger Warning! Ireland's oldest and finest comedy duo (aged in the barrel of life) take a light-hearted look at the dark side of life, love and comedy. Through jokes, tropes, songs and stories! They will let your laughter decide which side of the (of)fence you are on. Spoiler alert, there will not be any pun control laws! You have been warned.
Warnings: All Seating is unreserved. Late comers may not be admitted. Parental Guidance.
Venue description: Stand 5 and Stand 6 are located at The Place – a luxury four-star boutique townhouse hotel, situated in a stunning A-listed Georgian terrace in the very heart of Edinburgh's New Town. Stand 5 & 6 offer comfort, space, a roof terrace bar and complimentary WiFi. The venue also boosts a stylish restaurant and opulent cocktail bar. Catch another sensational comedy line-up from The Stand family here!

Title: The View from Castle Rock
Subtitle: World Première Performance
Teaser: With Stellar Quines Theatre Company, the Book Festival presents a vibrant production of Alice Munro’s stories, taken from the Nobel Prize-winning author’s collection The View from Castle Rock, which imagines the extraordinary experiences of...
Description: With Stellar Quines Theatre Company, the Book Festival presents a vibrant production of Alice Munro’s stories, taken from the Nobel Prize-winning author’s collection The View from Castle Rock, which imagines the extraordinary experiences of Munro’s Scottish ancestors who sailed from Leith Docks in 1818 in the hope of a better life in Canada. Acclaimed director Marilyn Imrie and multi award-winning playwright Linda McLean have created, in this word-for-word adaptation from Munro’s text, a powerful drama about the 19th century Scottish migrant experience. Daily performances at artSpace@StMarks.

Title: Briony Redman: Secret Show
Description: Shh, it's a surprise. A wrapped parcel of comedy, sketches and storytelling. Some secrets will be told, others will be kept. Seriously, to tell you more would be considered spoilers. There will also be a very special guest star! I've said too much. Debut solo comedy show from one half of Surname & Surname: 'Inventive, scrappy, proper Fringe fun' (Times). 'A sketch show worthy of selling out' **** (ThreeWeeks). 'Universal charm and wit' **** (EdFestMag.com). From the pen and mind that brought you Farce Noir: The Big Sheep – 'Cracking script... Joyously daft' **** (List).
Warnings: Some Strong Language
Venue description: Soak up the legendary atmosphere at the Pleasance Courtyard, considered by many to be the heart of the Fringe. With every entertainment under the sun in seventeen venues, come take in a show, enjoy a drink and stay for the day. There's even the Kidzone for the little-ones! ‘The centre of the cultural universe' (Scotsman).

Title: Ross Hepburn is Beetlejuice'd
Description: Most seven-year-olds don’t pick a ghost as a role model. But Ross Hepburn wasn’t like most seven-year-olds. Discover the story behind his strange and unusual choice of hero in a show that explains why sometimes only the undead can help you live life to the full.
Venue description: The Banshee Labyrinth is a teeming pub that is said to be Scotland's most haunted pub. Regular comedy nights, karaoke and live music will keep you entertained until the wee small hours. Three performance spaces, three bars, one open from 12.30-05:00. 18+ only. www.thebansheelabyrinth.com
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site

Title: Trainspotting
Description: It’s difficult to imagine a world without Danny Boyle’s 1996 smash hit. A film that has captured generations of fans across the globe and catapulted its cast to mainstream acclaim, still regularly features 20 years later in top ten lists everywhere. As if our own 70th anniversary and the film’s 20th birthday weren’t reason enough to screen this Oscar®-nominated bombshell, what better way to celebrate the hotly anticipated sequel than another chance to catch the original classic on the big screen? [18]

Title: Shakespeare Shorts – Hamlet
Description: Hamlet’s got the hump. His Uncle Claudius has bumped off his dad and married his mum, who’s a bit too fond of "ginger beer". Girlfriend Ophelia won’t listen to a word he says and his best mate, Horatio, keeps seeing ghosts. No wonder Rosencrantz and Guildenstern are confused. Mysteries, murders and magical music in this intriguing take on Shakespeare’s longest play, specially adapted for a young audience. 'Fun, frolics and lots of noise' (Peeblesshire News). 'Accessible Shakespeare at its best' (Southern Reporter).
Venue description: Located right in the middle of it all on the Royal Mile and part of our 7 theatre Royal Mile hub we present two spaces offering an array of new and established work, from theatre to musicals, dance, music and physical work, a real feast for all . Bar partners Beetlejuice make the Courtyard bar a funky festival option for all. Show info: www.thespaceuk.com.
Venue accessibility: Full venue site is accessible, Lift level access to all areas, Wheelchair accessible toilet, Reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas

Title: Don’t know what to believe? Ask for Evidence
Teaser: You don’t need to be an expert to question misleading claims about science and evidence
Description: Every day, we hear claims about what is good for our health or bad for the environment and how to improve education, cut crime and treat disease. But how do we know what to believe? Join a panel of speakers from Sense About Science, Research The Headlines, the Nappy Science Gang and The Young Academy of Scotland as they share stories from allotment growers, powerlifters, personal trainers and others who stood up for science and asked for evidence.

Title: Adelaide Fringe Information Session
Description: Adelaide Fringe is Australia’s largest open-access festival, with over 1,000 events across every art form in over 300 venues. Meet the Adelaide Fringe team and previous Fringe artists and get first-hand tips on presenting your work in Adelaide. Hear about potential Australian tour circuits (Perth –  Adelaide – Melbourne) and dedicated programmes, like Honey Pot, that are in place to help you get the most out of your Adelaide Fringe experience.
Venue description: Fringe Central is a resource developed specifically for Fringe participants. A hub for professional and creative development opportunities and home to our Arts Industry, Media and Venues and Companies offices, you will find support and advice as well as a programme of over 100 free events all designed to help you make the most out of your Fringe experience.

Title: The Maiden's Toy
Description: An ambitious director will leave no stone unturned in her production of a fiendishly difficult and disturbing play. The Maiden's Toy features a fast-moving account of the weeks leading up to the unveiling of her new production and focuses on the director's increasingly twisted relationship with her young leading male. New writing exploring the pursuit of perfection and the boundaries that must be crossed to achieve it.
Venue description: Located right in the middle of the Mile, seconds from the Fringe stages, a real fringe hub, three theatres offer a diverse programme of new and established work, from theatre to improv, spoken word, music, comedy, monologue, sketch and spoken word, a global feast for all. Description: Multi award-winning Australian comedian Tessa Waters is back with a new hour of stupidity. Dance, clown, sketch and gurning combine in this ridiculous genre busting show that has notoriously ruined pants across the globe. Tessa is a Gaulier-trained dynamo and professional idiot, whose multi award-winning physical comedy WOMANz (2015 Edinburgh Fringe) broke records at Melbourne Fringe Festival in 2014 for being the first show ever to win three awards and went onto tour around Australia and the UK to widespread acclaim.

Title: Noiseless and Patient
Description: Prince Edward Island, Canada, 1883 – home to the young Lucy Maud Montgomery, creator of Anne of Green Gables, and to four young spinsters of Scottish, Irish and English descent. They unravel their disparate stories of love, betrayal and hope as they spin and sew their young friend's wedding dress, looking towards uncertain futures in a pioneering land of mixed opportunities.
Venue description: theSpaceUK presents this state of the art venue. Located next door to theSpace @ Surgeons Hall the venue makes up part of our 7 strong theatre hub located right at the heart of the modern fringe on Nicholson St and Hill Square. Title: Tim Moore
Subtitle: Pedalling Two-Wheeled Adventures
Teaser: This popular travel writer and author of the bestselling French Revolutions has been dubbed ‘Bill Bryson on two wheels’. Since that first bestseller he’s got back on his bike for other long-distance adventures including a captivating journey...
Description: This popular travel writer and author of the bestselling French Revolutions has been dubbed ‘Bill Bryson on two wheels’. Since that first bestseller he’s got back on his bike for other long-distance adventures including a captivating journey around Italy on an aged bike. As he prepares for the publication of a new book this autumn, Tim Moore joins us to talk about long-distance odysseys and to give a taste of his new project.

Title: Hey Fat Roland! Forty Minutes of Idiot
Description: Spoken word behemoth Fat Roland mixes deadpan comedy and surreal stories with wonderfully odd illustrations. Imagine Johnny Vegas devouring Stewart Lee. On a depressed rollercoaster. Driven by a buffalo. Fats runs Bad Language in Manchester (best UK spoken word night, Saboteur Awards 2015) and is a columnist for Electronic Sound. This mini-show to support his new podcast Hey Fat Roland (which he’ll probably forget to mention) is a follow-up to his debut Fringe show, Kraftwerk Badger Spaceship, which BroadwayBaby.com called: ‘often hilarious... superbly executed... a seriously excellent piece of music-based comedy’.
Venue description: Located at the junction of Princes Street and Leith Street, The Newsroom is right in the heart of Edinburgh with free Fringe shows daily from 11:00-02:00. A recently refurbished, modern and stylish bar.

Title: Downs With Love
Description: Elizabeth has Downs. She lives a very independent life with help from her support worker, Tracy. Elizabeth has fallen for a guy, but the trouble is, he has fallen for Tracy. A challenging look at love and how society views relationships. Devised and written by the company. Based on real life experiences from one of the cast members who has Downs.

Description: The Bluebelles are returning to the Edinburgh Festival Fringe with their second show! Following last year’s five-star debut, this jazzy, adorable, all-female a cappella sensation from the University of Exeter are back to wow the Fringe again. Founded in 2013, this group has now competed in the Voice Festival UK and ICCA, singing everything from The Chordettes to Beyoncé. With a dollop of vintage cute and a whole lot of smiles, The Bluebelles bring you a cappella as you've never heard it before. Think the Andrews Sisters but with a modern twist and bright red lipstick.
Venue description: theSpaceUK present another high calibre venue.  A highbrow alternative to traditional Fringe venues boasting the most comfortable seats in town. Wonderfully located in our 7 theatre central Hub adjacent to SpaceTriplex and theSpace @ Surgeons Hall. A fabulous programme including music, theatre, a-capella, comedy, stand-up and percussion. Our very own gin bar in the courtyard adjacent makes this a must for all. For more information: www.thespaceuk.com.

Title: Eric's Tales of the Sea – A Submariner's Yarn
Description: Award-winning show. True-life submariner and gifted raconteur, Eric, gives an insider’s view of life aboard a nuclear submarine. This show is not to be missed – it is truly unique. Eric will keep you mesmerised hanging on his every word. With a selection of incredible images, he takes us through his experiences, which at times leave the audience scared to breathe in case they miss something. Heart-warming, real-life personal stories of danger, suspense and true love underwater. #madeinadelaide
Venue: Just the Tonic at The Caves

Title: The Big Stiffy
Description: Bob's dead. I know he loved you so much. Please come to the funeral to pay your respects. Karl's providing complimentary crudités (with dips), chopped to perfection by an angle grinder, plus fruit teas and apple crumble. There will be song, mirth and erotic hoovering. Please wear black and a smile. Karl Sparx – the man born in a coal mine – brings his relentlessly foolish brand of comedy to Edinburgh for the first time!
Venue description: Step away from the herd and enjoy the best programme at the Festival in this haven of calm and comfort just along from the Cowgate. Featuring shows of all genres from around the world, a trendy bar, posh loos and ... glorious air-conditioning.

Title: Sound + Vision: About a Boy
Description:
Sound + Vision in partership with Summerhall and Nothing Ever Happens Here (18+)

A two day festival in the courtyard of Summerhall celebrating film and music. Each day, warm up with a luminous array of great live music, before settling down for a special movie screening as darkness sets in... Bring a blanket and make a night of it.

Your ticket gets you access to the courtyard for the Saturday of the festival and access to all live music and the film screening. 

Live music line-up includes:
Badly Drawn Boy
Lovely, laid back, indie rock - the sort of stuff you might play on a Sunday morning while you walk down the street pretending you’re in a movie. The perfect musical accompaniment for a cup of tea in the sun, and the genius behind the soundtrack for About a Boy.

Admiral Fallow
Beautifully delicate songs with some stomp thrown in for good measure. This adorable band bring unadulterated joy to the ears of audiences across the world with their lyrical genius and unique take on Scottish folk music.
 

Randolph’s Leap
Upbeat downbeats to bop your head to – this band are very loveable. There’s quite a lot of them and their sound reflects this: a veritable smorgasbord of instruments and sounds that will undoubtedly wipe a grin on your face.


Teen Canteen
Forget The Spice Girls – this is grrrl power at its finest. This cherry-cola kissed sticky-harmony indie-pop band from Glasgow is something very special. The sort of music you can’t help but shake it all about to.

Followed by a screening of About a Boy  
Chris Weitz, Paul Weitz / UK / 2002 / 101 min
Adapted from the best-selling novel by Nick Hornby, in which a cynical, immature man is taught how to act like a grown-up by a little boy.
Bars and concessions available on-site. Non-seated event, Summerhall will rent out blankets/cushions on the day or feel free to bring your own!

Timings TBC, line-up subject to change.

Title: Something in My Shoe
Description: Meet Reginald, the bravest piece of rope in show business. Discover the perils of rising-finger illness. Thrill to the exploits of Rupert, rabbit escapologist. Join in the collective creation of a magic spell, and find out what on earth is in Ian’s shoe. 'With his childlike imagination and intuitive rapport with the audience, Saville's magic really captures the children – low-key, apparently simple tricks which they can't quite get to the bottom of, and wonderful joining in' (Scotsman). 'If you've never seen Ian in action you've missed a real treat' (Michael Rosen, writer and broadcaster).
Venue description: Theatre Arts Exchange presents theatre that is collaborative, innovative and ambitious from the ground up. From the creative community behind one of London’s most exciting Theatre Arts programmes, Middlesex University is proud to present an eclectic programme of new and established artists at a unique Edinburgh venue here at Gayfield Creative Spaces, a stone’s throw from the Playhouse.

Title: It's a Kinda Magic!
Description: London Cabaret Award-winners Duo Bogof have been making magic since before they were married, and they’re still making magic... long after their divorce!  Equipped with their trusty video camera, a few magic props and the belief that anything is possible, Duo Bogof transport you into their strange and wonderful world. Is the giant white rabbit merely a figment of Mr Bogof’s imagination? Where exactly does Mrs Bogof go when she vanishes from the magic box? With very special guests the winners of Baghdad's Got Talent (La Soiree).
Warnings: Contains some nudity and bad language.

In the evening the venue transforms into a great party space with live DJs and a late licence. Check out our Rocky Horror Night and our Karaoke Sundays... and £2.50 Jagerbombs seven days/week and £3.95 cocktails Monday – Wednesday.

Title: Beyond Price
Description: Highlights from those shows that couldn’t make it to this Festival. Klaff will commemorate anniversaries. Yes, we’ll see Jack as fornicating pandas, dubbed Carry On characters, a verse-speaking Mandela and tap-dancing robots. But there’s also visceral material here. We’ll discover what today’s theatre makers plan and value, what issues of the day concern them and what plays governments ban and keep from us. A rounding-off of Summerhall’s season and a celebration of the live art of the theatre, replete with almost illegal dollops of fun.
Venue description: Uniquely within Edinburgh's former Royal (Dick) Veterinary College, Summerhall presents high quality, engaging, challenging and exhilarating theatre, music, dance, visual arts for people of all ages. Our busy bar restaurant and cafe offers a wonderful selection of food and drink; the courtyard an epicentre of al fresco bars and street food. Not all of our shows are listed here. The entire programme of performance and visual arts is at www.summerhall.co.uk

http://www.summerhall.co.uk/about/accessibility/. Physical, poetic, technically demanding and emotionally complex, don’t miss this rising choreographer and her striking company of dancers in a riveting theatrical experience. ‘Emerald’s troupe is a real Fringe find’ ****(Scotsman). ****(Times). ****(List). ****(BroadwayBaby.com). ****(ThreeWeeks).

Title: Scotland's Democracy Trail
Description: Democracy is a hot topic in Scotland. In 2014's independence referendum, thousands of people in Scotland even got enthusiastic about it. Take the gentle uphill path to the top of Calton Hill to hear a 500-year-old story of democracy in Scotland, much of it almost forgotten. Using the fabulous views of the city, the tour will show you the clues that live on in Edinburgh's landscape. We then take a downhill stroll to the Scottish Parliament to bring the story right up to date. Approximately two hours, walking on pavements and good tracks. Some steps and slopes.
Warnings: Approximately two hours, walking on pavements and good tracks. Some steps and slopes. Finishing outside Scottish Parliament.

Title: Panicky Tack
Description: Panicky Tack bring you musical comedy, but not as you (or they) know it. All of the songs are craftily created on the spot! The two-piece London band bring their mind-blowing, side-splitting, toe-tapping show to Edinburgh for the first time. Once the sessions are up for good, they’ll be spat right back out again, but whilst they’re here, they are not alone: you’re in there with them.

From early delta blues to modern artists such as Jack White and Seasick Steve, Blues! plays the songs and tells the stories of the artists that have defined today’s music. The show features a 12-piece incarnation of acclaimed Edinburgh rhythm and blues band The Blueswater. 2012 Mervyn Stutter Spirit of the Fringe Award winner. ‘Terrific set of blues songs performed with zest and wit. Great night out’ (Ian Rankin). ***** (BroadwayBaby.com). ***** (ThreeWeeks).

Title: Claudia Hammond
Subtitle: The Best Things in Life are Free
Teaser: When acid house band KLF set fire to £1 million, there was outrage. Would people have been as angry if they'd squandered their money on booze? In her new book, Mind Over Money, BBC Radio 4’s voice of psychology, Claudia Hammond, explores our strange...
Description: When acid house band KLF set fire to £1 million, there was outrage. Would people have been as angry if they'd squandered their money on booze? In her new book, Mind Over Money, BBC Radio 4’s voice of psychology, Claudia Hammond, explores our strange moral relationship with money. She reveals not only the power it holds over us, but also some tools for making better decisions about the ways we use it.

Title: Lady Rizo: Multiplied
Description: New York City's iconoclastic, multi award-winning cabaret superstar returns – with child. Backed by a choice trio, Rizo rips apart carefully chosen pop songs and her own stirring originals. An entertainment machine even at eight months post-partum, her soulful vocals and titillating humour will leave you breathless in her gloved palm. Just don't inhale the baby powder! 'A powerhouse set of pipes and personality galore' ***** (Times). 'If you only see one cabaret show this year, see Lady Rizo... soulful, uproarious, slightly scary and utterly irresistible' ***** (Time Out).
Venue description: Assembly Checkpoint is the Fringe's premier venue for cabaret, music and more. The venue is located inside an old church and exudes warmth and charm. There is a bar inside the upstairs venue and further drinking and dining options downstairs.

Title: Panti: High Heels in Low Places
Description: The Queen of Ireland Panti invites you into her gender-discombobulating, stiletto shaped world, exposing stories behind the make-up – from performance giant to accidental activist – to reveal the national f*cking treasure she is today. In 2014, Panti landed herself in a legal shitstorm, dubbed Pantigate. Her speech about homophobia went viral, was broadcast worldwide, remixed by Pet Shop Boys, caused a parliamentary meltdown and fed into Ireland’s marriage equality referendum success. Hilarious and poignant, Panti traces her journey from small-town boy kicking against traditions to towering plastique woman in false lashes making history.
Warnings:
Adult themes
Strong language
Some audience interaction

Subtitle: Scottish Arcadias
Teaser: Nature and ideas intersect in inspiring ways. Linn Botanic Gardens is the subject of Another Green World, a beautiful, elegiac book created by novelist Philip Hoare and artist Alison Turnbull. At Stonypath in the Pentlands, artist Ian Hamilton Finlay...
Description: Nature and ideas intersect in inspiring ways. Linn Botanic Gardens is the subject of Another Green World, a beautiful, elegiac book created by novelist Philip Hoare and artist Alison Turnbull. At Stonypath in the Pentlands, artist Ian Hamilton Finlay created Little Sparta, a garden with stone-carved typographic artworks. Magnus Linklater, chairman of the Little Sparta Trust, discusses the garden and its enigmatic creator.

Title: The Shot Heard 'Round the World
Description: Written, directed and composed by three 20-year-old students, this is a brand new musical exploring the story of a man who effectively changed the course of history. It is loosely based on the life of Gavrilo Princip, the young revolutionary who delivered the fatal blow assassinating Archduke Franz Ferdinand. The musical explores how he became caught up in the movement and how his choice ultimately catapulted the world into the Great War: perhaps the greatest tragedy the world has ever seen. It is a story of passion, love and sacrifice.

Title: Airswimming
Description: 'A feelgood comedy set in the most unlikely of places' (Guardian). Critically acclaimed Weird Sisters Theatre Company present this uplifting story about friendship, fantasy and freedom. In 1924: Persephone Baker is planning her coming-out ball at the Dorchester when she finds herself abandoned at St Dymphna’s Hospital for the Criminally Insane, with only 'unhinged cigar smoking monomaniac transsexual' Dora Kitson to keep her company. Forgotten for 50 years, they create a surreal fantasy life involving Doris Day and a host of epaulette-wearing heroines to escape the drudgery and isolation of their existence.
Venue description: Step away from the herd and enjoy the best programme at the Festival in this haven of calm and comfort just along from the Cowgate. Featuring shows of all genres from around the world, a trendy bar, posh loos and ... glorious air-conditioning.

Title: Nev: Guts
Description: Strong tummies are required for Nev's (Chunks co-daddy, ‘ever versatile’ (Skinny) ‘comedian’ (National)) latest show. A tapeworm's fever dream on the politics of bleeding, vomiting, pissing, shitting and Greek gods of the DWP.
Venue description: Decorated in a dark and eerie gothic style with skeletons and other macabre items. Two bars offer food, beers, wines, spirits and themed cocktails - with performances of free Fringe festival comedy shows every day from 12:00-01:00.

Title: Hot Dub Time Machine
Description: Fringe's best party ever is back! Hot Dub Time Machine returns for its fifth year. The ultimate late night party. This time it's the biggest rave in Fringe history, at the massive, amazing Edinburgh Corn Exchange! Dance through pop music history from the Beatles to Beyoncé in a turntable driven, epic, audiovisual party experience unlike any other. Tom Loud's five-star, late night party is always sold out; it has the best music, the best people and the most dancing in town. Accept no imitations: be a time traveller at the best party ever!
Warnings: Strictly over 18s only - ID will be checked on arrival.
Venue description: The Edinburgh Corn Exchange has a rich history of live music events and has played host to many of the festival’s most memorable concerts during the last 16 years. As Edinburgh’s most flexible and multi-use venue we are always excited to see what the festival will bring us and 2016 is guaranteed to be no different. Join us and 2500 other revelers, it’s time to make new memories.

Title: Elevated
Description: Sam, Catherine and David get into the elevator together to leave work, each in a world of their own. When the doors open though, there is simply nothing there. Nothing at all. And they cannot get out. Their world disintegrated, their belief systems shattered, the three desperately seek an escape as the looming threat of physical and mental collapse hangs constantly over them.

Title: The Great Gatsby
Description: In 1922, New York reaches boiling point: parties are longer, morals are looser, liquor is stronger and jazz is hotter. When impressionable Nick Carraway arrives to seek his fortune, he is drawn into the decadent, hedonistic world of America’s elite. But when tragedy strikes, he is forced to decide whether money matters more than his morality. Following a sell-out run at the Nottingham New Theatre, this ‘terrific production’ **** (TheReviewsHub.com) has a ‘wonderfully unique and enthralling concept’ (Impact) guaranteed to bring to life one of the greatest novels ever written.
Venue description: Royal Terrace is special. It is a hidden gem – it’s '...one of the most charming venues at the Fringe...' so Lyn Gardner said and we like to think it is too.

Subtitle: Scotland, 1900-2015

Description: No Gods and Precious Few Heroes is former SNP politician Christopher Harvie’s history of 20th century Scotland. When its third edition was published in 1998 it was described as ‘a masterly synthesis of the most important…developments in Scotland’s recent past.’ Now, Harvie has updated his classic for a defining era of Scottish history. He discusses recent events in Scotland with former Labour politician, Tam Dalyell.

Title: Joe Fairbrother's Power Hour
Description: Power yourself up with a cult Edinburgh favourite. Join Joe for a fun-filled hour that's part stand-up, part film and part chat. Essentially, it's Spielberg meets Kilroy. But without the unsavoury politics of Kilroy. 'Hilarious. Fairbrother has talent in abundance' ***** (BroadwayBaby.com). 'Delightful' (List). 'Very funny' (RemoteGoat.com).

Description: Alexander McCall Smith is a cornerstone of Edinburgh literary life and a global publishing sensation. Today he gives a sneak preview of a new No 1 Ladies title, Precious and Grace, launches the latest volume in 44 Scotland Street, the world’s longest running serial novel, and offers up an hilarious standalone novel – My Italian Bulldozer. Irresistibly entertaining, McCall Smith is a jewel in the Book Festival’s crown.

Title: The White Crow
Description: Adolph Eichmann, the Nazi war criminal, was kidnapped in Argentina by the Israeli secret service, and brought to Jerusalem to stand trial for crimes against humanity, the trial of the century, as it would forever be known. A psychologist, Dr Baum, is sent in to break the great criminal. When given the opportunity to confront a notorious Nazi psychopath, we discover that the world of victims and executioners is not the world we expected, and that we ourselves are only one decision away from ‘the banality of evil’, as Hannah Arendt famously described it.

Wonderman is a unique gig-theatre take on Roald Dahl's short stories for adults, combining a sizzling hot score of original live music, macabre characters, soaring imaginings and thrilling twists and turns, all injected with a wicked sense of dark humour. A celebration of the wonder of one of Britain's best-loved storytellers for his centenary year. Prepare to expect the unexpected. 'Exciting, unmissable new theatre' ***** (Stage).

Title: Ahmed al-Malik, Lucy Popescu & Ben Rawlence with Bidisha
Subtitle: Asylum Found
Teaser: Bidisha continues her study of migration. Sudan-born writer Ahmed al-Malik fled to the Netherlands in 1989 after his novella was seized by the regime it criticised, from where he writes about Khartoum's recent history. Writer and critic Lucy Popescu...
Description: Bidisha continues her study of migration. Sudan-born writer Ahmed al-Malik fled to the Netherlands in 1989 after his novella was seized by the regime it criticised, from where he writes about Khartoum's recent history. Writer and critic Lucy Popescu discusses her refugee work and her powerful anthology of fiction and non-fiction, A Country of Refuge. With City of Thorns, Ben Rawlence offers an insight into the world’s largest refugee camp, Dadaab in Kenya, a place he spent four years getting to know.

Title: Rob Auton: The Sleep Show
Description: This show is about sleep. It is suitable for those who have slept. Following on from 2012's The Yellow Show, 2013's The Sky Show, 2014's The Face Show, 2015's The Water Show, award-winning writer and performer Rob Auton returns with 2016's The Sleep Show. ‘Just sad’ (Vanessa Feltz). ‘We need him’ (Scotsman). ‘Entirely compelling to watch’ (Daniel Kitson). ‘A genuine original. Poetical, philosophical, humane, completely charming and funny to boot.’ (Guardian). ‘Like watching a kid caught in the stage lights of his first Nativity’ (Venue.co.uk).
Venue description: The Banshee Labyrinth is a teeming pub that is said to be Scotland's most haunted pub. Regular comedy nights, karaoke and live music will keep you entertained until the wee small hours. Three performance spaces, three bars, one open from 12.30-05:00. 18+ only. www.thebansheelabyrinth.com
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site

Title: Don't Panic
Description: Jim Bayes took his show Pure Jim to Hull and Leicester festivals and following great feedback is now subjecting it to Edinburgh. Stylish comedy as Jim turns his self-esteem issues on the world around him while trying to get fitter and ditch the car. Jake Donaldson returns to Edinburgh and again brings his brand of humour. Everyone sees the world differently, and Jake sees it even more differently than most! Hilarity aplenty as he unravels the mysteries of his mind in this stand-up show about perception and mental health.
Venue description: Located right on the Royal Mile, The White Horse has been reborn in the last two years as a stylish bar, cafe and bistro right in the centre of Edinburgh. With great value lunches, followed by free shows from late afternoon until the end of the night.

Title: TG McEwan – Promises
Description: Promises is McEwan's seventh album. From Edinburgh, Tom grew up in Maryland and developed a Celtic Americana approach to 12-string, blues harp and songwriting. He stormed the 1980s college circuit. After playing the Bluebird open mic in Nashville, he launched the weekly Edinburgh Songwriters Showcase, before fronting the frenzied Captain Swing Ceilidh Band. Neurosurgery curtailed music for years, but, after winning Let’s Get Lyrical, he produced a book of 200 songs, re-released his back catalogue, and returned to gigging. And now, Promises, which explores the commitments we all make and sometimes break. Welcome back, Tom! tgmcewan.wordpress.com
Venue description: Acoustic Music Centre @ St Bride's is approx 5 - 10 minutes' walk from the important Haymarket road and rail interchange.

Title: Jamie MacDonald: High Vis
Description: The white stick waving blind bombshell is fast becoming a household name. Outrageous and fun Jamie expertly mines the world for comedy gems like beautiful Spanish disabled toilets and the fad month of Gaypril. This year it’s all about sticking out in this must see show. ‘One of the funniest Scots on the circuit’ **** (Sunday Herald). ‘Compelling anecdotes’ *** (Scotsman). ‘A fresh perspective’ **** (FringeGuru.com). ‘New, exciting and downright hilarious’ **** (Edinburgh Festivals). ‘A new meaning to observational humour’ **** (BroadwayBaby.com).

The Studios have some of the best audience facilities on the Fringe. All five Studios have comfortable modern seating, and the modern indoor Studios Bar has plenty of sofas, a much used piano and serves freshly prepared hot and cold meals.

Title: Me, Me, Me
Description: Life is hard, three comedians insist. But which has it just that little bit worse? A one-upping extravaganza of self-indulgent complaining and unapologetic oversharing. This show is navel-gazing in its purest form. They set out to hold up a mirror to the audience but spent the night staring into that mirror themselves. Good wholesome fun but don’t bring your family – this is not about you. It’s about us and we're creating art.
Artist: Ryan Bridge, Olga Koch, Charlie Ringe
Venue description: Situated on the bustling city centre street, at the foot of Edinburgh Castle sandwiched between the stylish West-end district and the ever popular Bruntsfield. Title: Martin Ford
Subtitle: The Robots are Coming
Teaser: For years, technology has been putting workers out of jobs. But in award-winning new book, The Rise of the Robots, Martin Ford charts a technological revolution that has profound social implications. The Silicon Valley-based entrepreneur argues that we...
Description: For years, technology has been putting workers out of jobs. But in award-winning new book, The Rise of the Robots, Martin Ford charts a technological revolution that has profound social implications. The Silicon Valley-based entrepreneur argues that we must make fundamental decisions to ensure technology benefits all, or we risk making white collar jobs obsolete and an implosion of the capitalist economy. He talks to James Runcie.

Title: Lindsey Fraser on Walk Two Moons
Subtitle: Reading Workshop
Teaser: In our workshop today, literary agent Lindsey Fraser explores Walk Two Moons by Sharon Creech. Winner of numerous awards including the Newbery Medal, this moving novel expertly weaves together two tales to create a story of love, loss and the complexity...
Description: In our workshop today, literary agent Lindsey Fraser explores Walk Two Moons by Sharon Creech. Winner of numerous awards including the Newbery Medal, this moving novel expertly weaves together two tales to create a story of love, loss and the complexity of human emotion. Expect an open discussion from the start: you can either read the book ahead of the event or be inspired to pick it up afterwards.

Title: Rory O'Keeffe: Monoglot
Description: Affable young funny man Rory O'Keeffe doesn't know any foreign languages. This apparently makes him a monoglot, which may or may not be a word. Join the 'Intelligent youngster' (Time Out) for his debut, as he tries to learn a new tongue, explores why we never say what we mean, and asks whether men and women really do speak different languages (spoiler alert: they don't). 'Comedy for a post-recession graduate generation' **** (Fest). 'Utterly hilarious' ***** (ThreeWeeks). 'His amicable charm and vigour makes for a highly enjoyable performance... a tightly composed and expertly delivered romp' **** (EdFringeReview.com).
Venue description: Soak up the legendary atmosphere at the Pleasance Courtyard, considered by many to be the heart of the Fringe. With every entertainment under the sun in seventeen venues, come take in a show, enjoy a drink and stay for the day. There's even the Kidzone for the little-ones! ‘The centre of the cultural universe' (Scotsman).

Title: Dominique Pinon: In Person
Description: Key roles in Alien: Resurrection and Amélie thrust Dominique Pinon into the international spotlight, but he was already an established name in his native France in the 1980s, when he worked with auteurs Jean-Jacques Beineix and Jean-Pierre Jeunet on such modern classics as Diva, Betty Blue and Delicatessen. He is currently gracing our screens as Master Raymond in the smash hit show Outlander. With several of his films featured in this years special ‘Cinema du look’ retrospective, we are especially honoured to welcome Dominique to EIFF to discuss his long and fascinating career. [U]

Title: Australia: A Whinging Poms Guide
Description: The funny side of Australia. British comedy veteran Dan Willis moved to Australia four years ago. Now he's got a bag of jokes, experiences and hangovers to share. ‘Unpretentious, informal, belly laughs-a-minute stand-up’ **** (ThreeWeeks). ‘Sharp wit and comic timing, never fails to entertain’ **** (List).
Venue description:
Part of The Liquid Room and offering 4 fantastic separate stage rooms and beer garden music bar. The venue can be accessed from Victoria Street. Title: Kader Abdolah
Subtitle: The Life of Muhammad
Teaser: Having fled Iran to escape the Ayatollah and Islamic fundamentalism, novelist Kader Abdolah settled in the Netherlands. From that safe distance he began enquiring into the true meanings of the Qur’an, and is now an acclaimed author. In The Messenger:...
Description: Having fled Iran to escape the Ayatollah and Islamic fundamentalism, novelist Kader Abdolah settled in the Netherlands. From that safe distance he began enquiring into the true meanings of the Qur’an, and is now an acclaimed author. In The Messenger: A Tale Retold, he portrays the Prophet and his followers in distinctly human ways, thus underlining Abdolah’s main desire: to build bridges between east and west.

Title: Menagerie of Microbes: Exhibitors Talk
Teaser: Join the Menagerie of Microbes team of artists and scientists for a day of interdisciplinary workshops, talks and discussions exploring the mechanisms, histories and future potential of simple yet complex life forms
Description:
Join the Menagerie of Microbes team of artists and scientists for a day of interdisciplinary workshops, talks and discussions exploring the mechanisms, histories and future potential of simple yet complex life forms. Beginning with an hour of free artist talks, the day will conclude with a 5 hour paid workshop. The workshop includes creating textiles with microbial dyes with Anna Dumitriu, a micro-geography field study with Simon Park, and testing the intelligence of slime mould with Heather Barnett.

Menagerie of Microbes Talks: 11-12, Anatomy Lecture Theatre (free)

Menagerie of Microbes Workshop: 1-6pm, ASCUS Lab (£30)

Title: Chris Packham
Subtitle: My Love for a Kestrel
Teaser: As the presenter of BBC's Springwatch, Chris Packham has become one of the nation’s favourite naturalists. But Packham was far from popular as a child: in his brave and lyrical memoir, Fingers in the Sparkle Jar, he recalls life as a solitary child,...
Description: As the presenter of BBC's Springwatch, Chris Packham has become one of the nation’s favourite naturalists. But Packham was far from popular as a child: in his brave and lyrical memoir, Fingers in the Sparkle Jar, he recalls life as a solitary child, comfortable only with a menagerie of insects. Then, in an act that would change his life, he took a young kestrel from its nest… He talks to Ruth Wishart.

Title: Expensive Shit
Description: 'The country change, the city change, the people dem think they change, but I tell you dem shit the same. Dem all dey run from it the same.' One toilet attendant. Two sets of toilets. One night. Worlds apart. The story of a nightclub toilet attendant, working in the toilets of a fictional club based on the Shimmy Club in Glasgow. Her conflicted journey spliced with flashbacks to the toilets of the Shrine nightclub in Lagos, Nigeria, where her younger self dreams of becoming a dancer in the revolutionary band of the late Nigerian musician, Fela Kuti. www.madeinscotlandshowcase.com
Warnings: Strong language

[18]

Humans have become a force on a par with earth-shattering asteroids and planet-cloaking volcanoes, and our planet is said to be crossing a geological boundary into the Anthropocene, or Age of Man. Gaia looks at how humanity’s changes are reshaping our living planet and explores how we might engineer Earth for our future.

Title: Allan Little's Big Debate
Subtitle: The End of the Transatlantic Era?
Teaser: Bruised by prolonged conflicts in the Middle East and encouraged by voters to return to isolationism, the US has begun to withdraw from the transatlantic role it adopted in 1945. It's a retreat that looks set to continue, but what does this mean for the...
Description: Bruised by prolonged conflicts in the Middle East and encouraged by voters to return to isolationism, the US has begun to withdraw from the transatlantic role it adopted in 1945. It's a retreat that looks set to continue, but what does this mean for the future of NATO and security in Europe? Will China take the chance to step in as the world's policeman? Allan Little brings together former leader of the Liberal Democratic Party Menzies Campbell, London bureau chief for the New York Times Steve Erlanger, and American journalist and author Lionel Shriver to debate this year’s hot topic.

Title: Come Down the Mile
Description: Walk the historic and dramatic Royal Mile with poet Ken Cockburn, weaving through narrow closes, open squares and secret gardens to discover how this city has been inspiring writers for 500 years. Edinburgh is a UNESCO City of Literature and has the only purpose-built poetry library in the world. Poetry has been its heartbeat for centuries – the medieval makars of the Scottish court, Robert Fergusson whose work inspired Burns, Robert Louis Stevenson who had a love-hate relationship with his home city, and the many poets who live and write in the city today.
Warnings: Walking involved – and please dress for the weather.
Venue description: Tours begin and end by the Scottish Poetry Library, the only purpose-built poetry library in the world, opened in 1999 and recently extended, housing a collection of Scottish and international poetry.

Born in 1875, poised to inherit the Empire, he instead burned brightly, briefly and transvestitely; blowing his family's godlike wealth putting on diamond-studded plays starring him (to which nobody came). When he died, his family burnt every record of his life, and carried on as though he'd never been. A hilarious, ripped up new extravaganza by Seiriol Davies (Caroline Horton & Co's Mess) about being too weird for the world.

Title: Go home and sit still: the Scottish Women's Hospitals in the First World War
Teaser: A fascinating talk about the Edinburgh-born pioneer Dr Elsie Inglis.
Description: A fascinating talk about the Edinburgh-born pioneer Dr Elsie Inglis. In 1914 she offered the War Office a female staffed hospital unit and was told to ‘go home and sit still’. She didn’t. Instead, Dr Inglis established the Scottish Women’s Hospitals. Christine Short tells the story of this remarkable women who braved deprivation, disease and war to provide a high standard of nursing care during the First World War.
Genre tags: Science and Culture,Health & Diseases,History of Science

Before he is released from hospital we meet Ives, a magnet for trouble and Ray’s delusional and paranoid friend. We follow Ray on his meandering journey through the grasp of his overworked brother Pete, who watches him slowly fall in love with tough skinned, brave but damaged Laura.
