Title: The End
Description: In yet another vanity-free performance (his second for director Guillaume Nicloux after last year’s Valley of Love), the immensely watchable French acting icon stars as an unnamed man (simply credited as l’homme) with a shotgun and a dog, who sets off on a habitual rabbit-hunting trip to the local woods. But before long, the dog runs off, he’s lost, his phone stops working and his gun, disappears. An encounter with an unpleasant youth and a naked woman reveal more questions than answers… [PG]

Title: Alastair Savage, Alone With History
Description: 2016 sees the release of Alastair's long-awaited fourth album and his first completely unaccompanied fiddle recording. Captured in the magnificent setting of Crathie Kirk next to Balmoral Castle, Alastair brings the first concert performances of the album to this year's festival. Featured highlights include Alastair's own Scenes from Gow in tribute to the lives of Niel and Nathaniel Gow, as well as Rabbie Burns. The music of James Scott Skinner is also included in recognition of Skinner's connection to Royal Deeside. A Scottish fiddle journey exploring the entrancing beauty of melody, ancient and modern.
Venue description: The Sir Arthur Conan Doyle Centre is situated on Palmerston Place, just a stone throw away from Haymarket Station. Set in a beautiful Victorian Townhouse, the Centre boasts rich historical features and was created to provide for the physical, emotional and spiritual well-being of society and community needs in Edinburgh.

Hosted by DJ Ace, one of the UK's leading radio DJs with a daily show on BBC Radio 1xtra, Damon the Barber, whose clients include not only celebrities but also the every day heroes of the community, Femi Oyeniran, professional actor and law graduate and, finally, Little Man A comedian who has amassed a large following on and off the comedy circuit.

Title: Paul Thorne: This Month's Apocalypse
Description: Throughout history, every generation has thought they would witness the end of the world. They were wrong. We will! Paul Thorne returns to Edinburgh with a sideways look at modern evil. From bigots and bankers and the seven deadly sins to the fifth Horseman of the Apocalypse and the three fundamentalist teddy bears. ‘...a must-see comedian’ (Guardian). ‘...Thorne makes working an audience look effortless’ (Stage). ‘Paul Thorne’s satirical songs, with his own guitar accompaniment, a waspish, sweary pleasure‘ (Telegraph). paulthorne.co.uk @pthornecomedian
Warnings: All seating is unreserved and latecomers may not be admitted.

Title: Journeys
Description: Journeys is a fast-paced, physical comedy that romps along through a series of farcical stories, each ridiculous and occasionally poignant. A soldier, an artist, an actress and a housewife, each running from the past embark on a journey across a war-torn landscape, experiencing misfortune, mishaps and mayhem, whilst forging new and loving relationships.

Subtitle: New Kids on the Block
Teaser: Two smart novels feature loners who arrive in town - with unexpected consequences. Devil Take the Hindmost won Martin Cathcart Froden the Dundee International Book Prize for its thrilling depiction of a young man who stumbles into a world of velodrome...
Description: Two smart novels feature loners who arrive in town - with unexpected consequences. Devil Take the Hindmost won Martin Cathcart Froden the Dundee International Book Prize for its thrilling depiction of a young man who stumbles into a world of velodrome racing in the 1920s. Meanwhile in David Sanger’s first novel, All Their Minds in Tandem, a mysterious man in an 1870s community in West Virginia starts entering the minds of the townsfolk.

Title: Julia Donaldson & Friends
Teaser: Festival favourite Julia Donaldson is joined by The Gruffalo illustrator Axel Scheffler and friends for a highly interactive and hugely entertaining event of live drawing, songs and rhymes. Also joining the party is writer James Robertson with his Scots...
Description: Festival favourite Julia Donaldson is joined by The Gruffalo illustrator Axel Scheffler and friends for a highly interactive and hugely entertaining event of live drawing, songs and rhymes. Also joining the party is writer James Robertson with his Scots translation of Julia's much-loved book, The Reiver Rat.

Title: Aquapella: Mash-Up, Mix and Blend
Description: Since their Edinburgh debut last year, vocal sensations Aquapella from the University of Bath have toured, won highest-placed UK mixed a cappella group at ICCA, and were a Voice Festival UK finalist. Bringing home awards for outstanding choreography and arrangements, Aquapella certainly know the recipe for success: mash-up, mix and blend. Their secret ingredient – a spoonful of sass, a pinch of humour and cheesy dance moves to taste. ‘The group seem to have limitless energy… Entertaining, occasionally moving, always accessible and uplifting… Catch them if you can – you won't regret it’ (FringeReview.com).

Title: Depresstival, Tim Loud: Antifolks
Description: Two antifolk-Punk musicians, Depresstival and Tim Loud, bring their melodic, musical whinge fest to Bob's BlundaBus. Depresstival is a caustic, witty and eloquently miserable antifolk musician and vaguely viral YouTuber – facebook.com/depresstival. Tim Loud is a gut-bustin', foot-stompin', 12-string driven country/blues antifolk musician from Leeds. His songs take a sardonic and self-deprecating look at life as a tour-heavy DIY punk musician – timloud.bandcamp.com. Find them both on a bus in the heart of the Fringe… www.pay-what-you-want.info

Description: You Wouldn't Want to Be in the Great Fire of London is a 45 minute, 100 miles per hour show for kids! Two storytellers will transport the children back to 1666 smoggy, grotty London, where the most famous fire in history began! Come with us on an adventure ride of the imagination, come laugh with us, sing with us and help us save London! This production is adapted from the children's book You Wouldn't Want to Be in the Great Fire of London published by The Salariya Book Company.
Venue description: The Sir Arthur Conan Doyle Centre is situated on Palmerston Place, just a stone throw away from Haymarket Station. Set in a beautiful Victorian Townhouse, the Centre boasts rich historical features and was created to provide for the physical, emotional and spiritual well-being of society and community needs in Edinburgh.

Title: All Aboard the Marriage Hearse
Description: Sean and Amy are your typical cohabiting, Catholic/Jewish, thirty-something couple living in Manhattan. After four years together, Amy wants to get married but Sean doesn't believe in the institution. The game is on! Tonight the pair will settle the marriage question once and for all. Sean will try to talk her out of it. Amy will try to talk him into it. Will they breakup? Will they climb aboard the Marriage Hearse? Don't miss this internationally acclaimed romantic comedy by Matt Morillo and the team behind The Inventor and the Escort and Angry Young Women.

For avid fans it's a must, and if you've never read the book or seen the film, this is your ticket to a ride you won't soon forget. ***** (Edinburgh Evening News). ***** (ThreeWeeks). ***** (AllEdinburghTheatre.com). ***** (ThePublicReviews.com). ***** (ScotsGay).

Description: Agnew returns with his sequel to 2012's Tales of The Sauna, moving out the steam room into the living room. The consequences of gay sex going Abigail's Party. Hailed as a master storyteller, his 2016 offering is a snapshot of hardcore, working-class gay life touching on mental health, sexual health and general misadventure. The former Scottish Comedian of the Year's language and imagery is bold and brash – the stories deeply personal. 'Electrifying' (Guardian). 'Unmissable' (Chortle.co.uk). Title: Fraser Doherty
Subtitle: The 48-Hour Start-Up
Teaser: Aged just 14, Edinburgh-based Fraser Doherty began making 100% fruit jam in his gran’s kitchen and successfully sold it to Waitrose. 13 years on, SuperJam is an international brand. Keen to inspire other young people to take the plunge and start their...
Description: Aged just 14, Edinburgh-based Fraser Doherty began making 100% fruit jam in his gran’s kitchen and successfully sold it to Waitrose. 13 years on, SuperJam is an international brand. Keen to inspire other young people to take the plunge and start their own business, he recently took part in an experiment, attempting to create a profitable business from scratch in 48 hours. In this event, he shares his successes and mistakes.

Title: Dido and Aeneas
Description: Coro 16 return to the fringe with Henry Purcell’s short operatic masterpiece. In this semi-staged concert performance, the small ensemble and strings will be directed from the harpsichord by Neil Metcalfe. Dido – Carole Clarke, Aeneas – Richard Coleman. 'A flawless and accomplished musical performance' (Three Weeks).
Venue: St Andrew's and St George's West, George St

Title: Denton and Me
Description: 1944: Fastidious diarist Denton Welch writes with astonishing honesty about his obsession for reckless land boy Eric. 2011: A young writer is given the diaries by a family friend and discovers echoes of his own life within. This multi-layered, stunningly designed show weaves together writer/performer Sam Rowe’s autobiography with the writing of Denton Welch (1915-1948), a fascinating figure in queer and literary history, and favourite of Alan Bennett, William S Burroughs and John Waters. A powerful, moving and humorous production, in collaboration with Scotland’s most exciting theatrical talent. Directed by Nicholas Bone. **** (Herald). www.madeinscotlandshowcase.com
Artist: Sam Rowe and Macrobert Arts Centre in association with Showroom

Description: Mediterraneo is bringing Africa, Cuba and southern Italy to Summerhall for a huge festival edition of their world music concert. A night of Italian pizzica, Zimbabwean jit-jive and Afrobeat tangled with Cuban salsa. Three bands – 20 musicians; complete with big brass, furious tambourines, wild guitars and dance moves from three continents. Pizzica, tarantella and tammuriata exponents The Badwills are joined by Zimbabwe legend Rise Kagona (ex Bhundu Boys) and his mighty jit-jive band, with seven-piece Afrobeat, Caribbean and Cuban rhythm aficionados Poción de Fe to top off.

Title: CeilidhKids at the Fringe – Free
Description: Family workshop suitable for children aged 3-7 years with parents or carers. We involve everyone: skip, clap and march together to traditional Scottish music. Enjoy discovering very simple (often simplified) dances that you might find at a ceilidh or Scottish country dance, celebrating the social aspects of dancing with a partner. CeilidhKids is all about fun for all generations. Hugely popular with local families, now it's your turn.
Warnings: All children should be accompanied by an adult willing to join in. One adult can dance with two children.

Title: A Working Title
Description: It's about living in the city in a generation of renters, Tinder swipers, never-left-the-nesters, budget shoppers, internshipers, over-the-recommended-daily-allowance-drinkers, minimum wage workers, sofa surfers and daydreamers. It's about how disappointed your spotty 16-year-old self would be by their future life, dominated by Netflix, no money and sharing a shower with eight strangers. It's about turning 25 and not having your shit together. It's about people. Six people, and the little snippets that make up a day in their lives. Explored with a jaunty live soundtrack, poetry, dancing and silly voices.

Among other things, this year we meet some celebrity obsessed mythical beasts, learn what really upsets professional wrestlers and find out what theatrical props talk about during filming breaks. Eccentric, energetic and a whole lot of fun, it's the perfect way to start a day at the Fringe.

Title: JOAN
Description: Put your drinks down and your hands together, all the way from Domremy in France (via Soho and 600 years) it's JOAN! An earthy story of courage, conviction, hope, survival and love, this is Joan of Arc – the world's first drag king? Packed with guts, heart (and some well placed couscous), JOAN fuses lyrical new writing with drag king cabaret. Performed by Drag Idol Champion LoUis CYfer. Written and directed by Lucy J Skilbeck. 'Emotional ballast and cross-dressing that looks like sorcery' (Guardian) on JOAN. 'Theatre that flies in the face of conventionality' **** (Stage) on Milk Presents.

Title: Paul Harrison’s Trio Mágico Play the Music of Gismonti
Description: The music of Egberto Gismonti is like a microcosm of his native Brazil – diverse, joyful and unique. Award-winning jazz pianist Paul Harrison, bassist Mario Lima Caribe and drummer Stu Brown have a special rapport from years of performing together in Scotland and internationally. In this new band they bring fresh life to great compositions that deserve to be heard more widely. Rhythms that will (literally) move you, melodies that you'll find yourself singing for a long time afterwards and a musical experience that will stay with you.

In this dark comedy, a conversation takes place in an afterlife where nothing is as it seems and the whole of forever is happening at the same time. Just don't annoy the one person in charge of it all...

Title: The Lounge
Description: A dangerously unstable farce about growing old. 97 years go by in a flash. An afternoon lasts an eternity. In a care home lounge somewhere off the A1, 97 year old Marsha Hewitt begins the last day of her life. But she cannot go quietly. As the radiators burn and Jeremy Kyle blares, rivalries, relatives and murderous impulses jostle for space on the Axminster carpet. By teatime, a riot is brewing. The award-winning Inspector Sands (A High Street Odyssey, If That’s All There Is, Hysteria) shine a light on how we cope, or fail to cope, with ageing.
Warnings: The age guidance is recommended based on the subject matter and possible use of bad language

Description: When lonely teenager Ada creates her own robot pal, named O.K.A.Y. (Outstandingly Knowledgable Android Youth), she has no idea the trouble it will cause. Strange things start happening to her classmates and O.K.A.Y. seems to be showing signs of self awareness. Is it responsible? With your help, Ada must decide whether to destroy her best friend or risk her classmates lives. At what point does a robot deserve the same rights as a human? If it is self aware, is it wrong to kill it?

Title: Jenni Fagan on The White Bird Passes
Subtitle: Reading Workshop
Teaser: Scottish writer Jenni Fagan explores Jessie Kesson’s The White Bird Passes. Using her own childhood as inspiration, Kesson has written a charming and haunting account of the poverty of a young girl in the 1920s, passing from the city streets into a...
Description: Scottish writer Jenni Fagan explores Jessie Kesson’s The White Bird Passes. Using her own childhood as inspiration, Kesson has written a charming and haunting account of the poverty of a young girl in the 1920s, passing from the city streets into a troubled life in an orphanage in Scotland. Expect an open discussion from the start: you can either read the book ahead of the event or be inspired to pick it up afterwards.

Title: Liam Withnail: True Defective
Description: Sobriety's a joke. With sell-out shows at the Adelaide, Glasgow, Brighton and Leicester comedy festivals, Liam Withnail now unveils his hotly-tipped debut hour. A hilarious journey from menace to society to total sobriety. Is life still fun? Can he still operate? Is loving booze akin to mental illness? Or is all this a bit much? As featured on: BBC Radio 4, STV and live at T in the Park. For drinkers and thinkers alike, True Defective is a guaranteed laugh. ‘Good, anarchic fun’ (Scotsman). ‘Slick, fast paced banter’ (Skinny). ‘Outrageously hilarious’ (Advertiser, Adelaide).

As the truth comes in and out of focus, we witness a vital human struggle for power in the face of the unknown. This production from Lucille Lortel and New York Innovative Theatre award-winning Rising Phoenix Repertory grapples with Pinter’s dark and mercurial text to question how art can reckon with atrocity. Title: Ubu Faust
Description: Ubu assumes the role of Faust in this raucous, rapid-fire puppet comedy. Inspired by the plays of Alfred Jarry, the legends of Faust, and the traditions of Punch and Judy, Ubu Faust is a satirical exploration of a most grotesque and unlikable man and the lengths to which he'll go to satisfy his many hungers. Well, two. Two hungers. He really only has the two. Contains boorish villainy, laughable special effects, gratuitous wordplay, and puppet sexuality. Minimal audience participation. Only one bit. Well, three. Three bits. But they're simple. And relatively painless.

Teaser: Global food production will have to double by 2050 to feed our ever-growing population - join our panel of experts to explore how we can feed the world.

The screams and scratching you have been hearing are getting closer now and you're about to turn and flee when the doors ahead of you burst open. A tall, gaunt figure approaches and urges you to follow, but warns that you do so at your own risk... Do you dare enter Wychwood House, the asylum that supposedly closed its doors in 1916? Being stationed in remote and dangerous corners of the world he lived many different lives, juggling the dedication to his writing with the ties of a tumultuous marriage and the loyalty to his pilot friends. Yet what was essential for Saint-Exupéry? 'One sees clearly only with the heart. What is essential is invisible to the eye.'

Title: Trevor Royle
Subtitle: Culloden: A Very European Battle
Teaser: Associate Editor of the Sunday Herald and highly respected military historian Trevor Royle has completed a timely reappraisal of the last major battle to be fought on British soil, and one of the most controversial: Culloden. Far more significant than...
Description: Associate Editor of the Sunday Herald and highly respected military historian Trevor Royle has completed a timely reappraisal of the last major battle to be fought on British soil, and one of the most controversial: Culloden. Far more significant than simply a fight between the Scots and the English, Royle contends it represented the bedrock of the creation of the British Empire. Chaired by Sheena McDonald.

Title: Happy Together
Description: Everywhere you go you can see happy couples being happy together. Smiling profusely, laughing manically, grabbing, grinding, slurping furiously. Happy happy happy. It must be exhausting. Do you ever wonder what happens when the happy couple go home, away from the public eye? Do they unmask, unravel, drop the act? Happy Together goes behind closed doors and explores the theatricality of one couple's dysfunctional relationship. When the stage becomes a bed, the curtain a locked door and the audience a fly on the wall, what are the boundaries between performance and life at home?

They understand what the small battles are worth. Sure, we can all solve world peace, but what about slow walkers and public nose-picking? Bring these and other woes to this interactive stand-up show. Matt and Declan are the new face of anger, and it’s smiling benignly, with varying degrees of facial hair and success. Come see these two fierce Guardianistas articulate their scything, unremitting anger in vague, polite and entirely ineffectual way.

Working with young actor James Robert Rutherford on his second Fringe venture, the two bring an atmospheric, enigmatic and thought-provoking story to the stage.

Audiences keep coming back for more to ‘this serene little venue’ ([i]Scotsman[/i]).

Title: The Man Who Was Thursday
Karen Hobbs: Tumour Has It
Description: Join Karen for the honest and hilarious story of her cervical cancer extravaganza. In her debut show, she will share with you the gore and glory of getting a nasty surprise at 24, and why laughter is a lifesaver. Through comedy, storytelling and a poem to Svetlana the Tumour, you will spend 50 minutes with someone who has found a light at the end of her vaginal tunnel. Tumour Has It challenges the stigma of having a gynaecological disease, raises awareness, celebrates life and loudly tells cancer that it was barking up the wrong chuff.
Warnings: There is one moment of non-sexual nudity. There is strong language and adult themes.
Venue description: Situated at the heart of the festival, between George Square and Teviot Place, the Med Quad is where you can find venues Cow Barn, Ermintrude, Buttercup, Daisy and Clover, presenting theatre, musicals, comedy, cabaret and family shows early til late.

Title: The Wives of Others
Description: NYC, 1955. Angie and her friends are having a dinner party. Their Mafioso husbands are off on a job, but the real story is unfolding in Angie’s living room. Chronicling the violent and duplicitous events of one evening, The Wives of Others promises foul language, bloodshed, and a lot of spaghetti. With an all-female cast and original script from one of Cambridge’s most prolific playwrights, Tom Stuchfield, this is a brutally stylish, Tarantinoesque, pitch-black comedy unlike anything you’ve seen. ***** (Cambridge Student). Stuchfield’s And The Horse You Rode In On: ***** (TheTab.com) ***** (EdFringeReview.com).
Warnings: Explicit language and violence.

Title: Nicole Henriksen is Makin it Rain
Description: After sell-out shows and rave reviews across Australia, alternative comedian Nicole Henriksen brings her award nominated, unflinching and cheeky theatre debut to Edinburgh. Makin' it Rain is a frank look behind the scenes of life as a high-class tease, as well as an examination of our society's relationship with sexuality, gender and image. It'll answer the questions you're too afraid to ask and have you thinking up some of your own. 'Dynamic and courageous' **** (TheatreGuide.com). 'Flawless' ****½ (Kyrztoff.com). 'Amazing' ***** (TheatreReviews.co.uk). Best Theatre nominee, Fringe World 2016.
Warnings: This show contains full frontal nudity, occasional course language, and loud music.

Title: Vladimir McTavish: Scotland In Sixty Minutes
Description: Vladimir McTavish turned 60 in 2016. For many, this is a time in life for sober reflection or for ticking off items from the bucket list. Instead, McTavish decided to take advantage of his free bus pass to embark on a three month tour of cities and small towns of Scotland, in search of the quirks that make up our nation’s psyche. A hilarious hour-long account of that trek from Gretna to Thurso and beyond in a quest to find the essential Scotland. ‘One of the finest acts on the Scottish comedy circuit’ (Guardian).
Warnings: All seating is unreserved and latecomers may not be admitted.

Title: Cal Flyn & Candace Savage
Subtitle: Settlers and Colonists: Uncomfortable Histories
Teaser: Once fêted as the heroic 'discoverer' of Gippsland in the wilderness of 1830s Australia, Cal Flyn's relative Angus McMillan was recently identified as the perpetrator of gruesome massacres of the Gunai people. Flyn's Thicker Than Water is a personal...
Description: Once fêted as the heroic 'discoverer' of Gippsland in the wilderness of 1830s Australia, Cal Flyn's relative Angus McMillan was recently identified as the perpetrator of gruesome massacres of the Gunai people. Flyn's Thicker Than Water is a personal account of this troubling story. A descendant of the ‘pioneers’ who settled in the Saskatchewan prairies, Candace Savage's A Geography of Blood retells the prairies story with help from First Nations people.

Title: After Magritte
Description: After Magritte is a rip-roaring comedy about ordinary people in a most bizarre situation: a senile woman obsessed with the tuba may or may not be the mother of anyone in the room; a neurotic police inspector may or may not have a search warrant for an unidentified tortoise; an argumentative couple may or may not have seen a man covered in shaving foam wearing the kit of West Bromwich Albion. Stoppard’s play is a sophisticated romp into the delightful absurdity of sixties suburbia, proving that splendid absurdity doesn’t just emerge from the mundane, but thrives on it.
Venue description: theSpaceUK presents this state of the art venue. Title: Nothing But the Poem on Love, Life and Death
Subtitle: Reading Workshop

Description: Join Georgi Gill from the Scottish Poetry Library for a discussion around a selection of poems that contain profound insights into human life. The workshop features poems by some of our Festival authors: Michel Faber, Hollie McNish and Louis de Bernières, all writers who challenge convention and the boundaries of the written page. No background knowledge is required and poems will be provided.

Title: Hayley Ellis: FOMO
Description: Hayley Ellis has Fear of Missing Out (FOMO to the kids). Join award-winning Ellis (tour support for Rob Delaney and regular contributor for BBC Two's Russell Howard’s Good News) for her follow-up hour to find out how neurotic we all really are. ‘Engaging’ (Scotsman). ‘Destined for comedy greatness’ (XFM). **** (Gigglebeats.co.uk). ‘Ellis made everybody laugh’ (Independent). ‘An engaging and quick witted performer’ (Fest). ‘Hayley Ellis is fast becoming Manchester’s funniest female’ (Steve Wright, BBC Radio 2). As featured in the top Fringe jokes of all time in the Scotsman and the Independent.

Description: One of Ireland’s top comedians is back in Edinburgh. After a couple of years away, Neil returns with show packed with more hilarious tall tales. Includes tips on how to survive a bobsled ride and how to pretend you’re enjoying a trip in an astronaut training centrifuge. ‘If you've yet to see Delamere live, make this the year… simply put, he is a master’ ***** (Scotsman). ‘One mean, lean, comedy killing-machine’ ***** (Herald).

Singing for the love of his people, his country and culture, Archie’s songs go to the heart of the Australian story. Archie is an extraordinarily gifted Australian artist with a truly visionary talent. His voice springs from the broken heart of a broken nation, which only makes his message of hope and love more powerful.

Trouble comes when Ken wants to go straight after his girlfriend’s pregnancy but Kazu decides to keep on selling without their boss’s approval. The winner of the Japanese Cinema Splash best film at the Tokyo Film Festival, it is a great example of new Japanese indie cinema. [15]

When Flinn is in the middle of his school play his old nemesis, Mr T the T-Rex, appears and kidnaps his friends forcing them to hunt for the Magic Cutlass: a sword that grants any wish! Title: Mr. Right
Dr Phil's NHS Revolution
Description: Laugh, love, shout and reclaim our NHS. Ditch the market, cherish the carers, fund the frontline, avoid the harm, kill the fear, tell the truth, use the evidence, inspire, collaborate, recover, die gently. Are you in? Guest appearances from inspirational Glasgow GP, writer and broadcaster Dr Margaret McCartney. Phil Hammond is an NHS doctor working in chronic fatigue, an investigative journalist for Private Eye, a BBC presenter, comic and author of 'Staying Alive, How to Get the Best from the NHS’. 'If Dr Phil were a medicine, you should swig him by the litre' (The Times).

Title: Ayman Jarjour Classical Guitar
Description: Ayman Jarjour is an internationally renowned Syrian classical guitarist and graduate of The Juilliard School in New York. He performed solo and with orchestra in Syria, UK, Belgium, Spain, Lebanon, Egypt, Malta, Jordan, Germany, Taiwan, Tunisia, Sudan, USA and Turkey. In February 2016, a reviewer described him as 'Wearing his remarkable virtuosity with the utmost modesty, Ayman Jarjour was a beguiling and impeccably-mannered guide through his world of subtle imagination and colours, and left his listeners charmed and extremely contented'. Ayman recorded a CD of his solo programme at Carnegie Hall, New York.
Venue description: Situated in the heart of vibrant Stockbridge, ten minutes walk from city centre.  Stockbridge Church is an attractive Grade-A Georgian listed building. The Sanctuary is a magnificent space which has a flexible stage with the potential of using risers. They have recorded three albums for the Berlin-based Karaoke Kalk label, two (Standards Volume II and III) of mainly original material and one (the NJTOS's Xmas Album) of well-known carols. They have shared the same bill with names as diverse as Teenage Fanclub, James Blackshaw and Steve Beresford; collaborated with artists including ShugoTokumaru and Benni Hemm Hemm.

Dundonian author Jim Crumley’s new book is a beautifully-wrought study of what happens when moody and majestic Autumn descends on Britain, while Stephen Moss has spent a year in the dramatic and wild landscapes of the Highlands.

Title: Acting With Archetypes
Description: Part of the Fringe Central Events Programme, specifically for Fringe participants. This workshop offers an opportunity to experience some of the unique work of the Royal Conservatoire of Scotland’s MA in Classical and Contemporary Text programme. This original practice, emerging from Programme Coordinator Dr Marc Silberschatz’s directorial, research and teaching experience, will offer an exciting tool by which participants can engage with archetypal images, characters and situations. The session will prove valuable for those interested in both text based and devised theatre.
Warnings: You may be asked to show your Fringe Participant pass on entry.
Venue description: Fringe Central is a resource developed specifically for Fringe participants. A hub for professional and creative development opportunities and home to our Arts Industry, Media and Venues and Companies offices, you will find support and advice as well as a programme of over 100 free events all designed to help you make the most out of your Fringe experience.

Description: He’s currently CEO of the New York Times but before that he was Director General of the BBC. There, Mark Thompson oversaw the broadcasting behemoth during a time of turbulence and change. In his fearless broadside Enough Said, Thompson explains why the internet and an age of rolling news has singularly failed to lead to better democracy. Political language must change, he will argue today in conversation with Sarfraz Manzoor.

Followed by an exploration of how the arts can express, reflect, contest and shape the wider culture and how this can help navigate a cultural shift. Followed by an open discussion for practitioners about how we might better use the arts/culture in our practice.

Description: How does life work? How does nature produce the right number of zebras and lions on the African savanna, or fish in the ocean? How do our bodies produce the right numbers of cells? Join award-winning biologist and author of The Serengeti Rules, Sean B Carroll to hear the stories of the pioneering scientists who sought the answers to simple yet profoundly important questions and learn how their discoveries matter for our health and the health of our planet.

Description: The best undiscovered songwriter of his generation? Born to celebrity parents when Elvis topped the charts, immediately given away to strangers. He grew up with the King on repeat on the Dansette. He was always going to be Elvis – until he heard The Beatles, and Lennon. Oozing natural musical talent, he first performed aged seven and hasn’t looked back. Elvis gave him rock’n’roll, John gave him rhyme'n'revolution. It’s all there in his own songs. Nigel, son Solomon and the Free Radicles play his thought-provoking originals and covers that reek of rock, rage and rebellion.

Title: String
Description: ‘The string is the thing’ – in the centre of the stage there is a giant sculpture. Is it art? Is it a metaphor for the internet? Exploring the nature of communication itself, the characters follow the winding threads of the internet, only to become increasingly entangled in its ever-evolving web of words and images. The string (and the play) obeys no rules. This ‘original and thought provoking’ (Cherwell) piece is the debut of Oxford University student Lauren Jackson.
Venue description: Greenside @ Nicolson Square is set in the heart of town, seconds from the BBC@Potterow, the internationally renowned Festival Theatre, the flashing lights of Bristo Square and the hustle and bustle of the Royal Mile. We’re bringing our desire for creating great spaces and passion for service to the heart of the festival.

Description: Warning: This show contains ninjas, not magic. After a standing room only season in 2015, Javier Jarquin returns with award-winning show Card Ninja. Watch, as he turns ordinary playing cards into weapons, as he battles through tests of unfathomable precision, speed and power, in a unique, unforgettable and hilarious performance. Following his journey from mild-mannered card player to silent assassin, Card Ninja contains upbeat humour, impressive stunts and smooth audience interaction for anyone who's ever wanted to be a little bit ninja. 'Jarquin is seriously talented' (Stage).
Venue description: Come and graze in George Square! Food, drink, two fantastic venues and of course, an upside down purple cow. If you're looking for Udderbelly or Wee Coo, this is the place to be. We also have buzzing bars open til very late!

Warnings: Strong language

Description: Great selection of collectable vinyl! LPs 12" and 7" singles and a gaggle of 78s. Quality selection of CDs and DVDs, including an extensive range of classical CDs. Covering every type of music from the 50s, 60s, 70s, 80s, 90s, 00s to present day. Rock'n'roll, blues, jazz, beat, psychedelic, progressive and heavy rock, classical, country, punk, indies, folk, Scottish and more. The stock will be changing daily over the five days, including a large range of clearance vinyl at bargain prices and displays of expensive, rare vinyl. A must for music lovers of all ages!

Title: Shaggers (Free Festival)
Description: Following sell-out shows in Adelaide, Melbourne, Darwin, Singapore, Germany and all over the UK, the hugely popular and hilarious show returns for its ninth successive year at the Edinburgh Festival Fringe. A variety of performers of all genders, nationalities and sexual orientation come together to tell their best material based around that most noble of all pursuits, shagging! ‘Excellent’ ***** (Audience review, Edinburgh Festival Fringe). ‘The best way to close a night at the festival’ ***** (HeraldSun.com.au, Melbourne International Comedy Festival). ‘Utterly hilarious’ ****1/2 (TheWest.com.au, Perth Fringe World).

Description: Learn to re-mix and create music using a MaKey MaKey and anything that conducts electricity. A MaKey MaKey is an invention kit that turns everyday objects into touchpads and you'll experiment with things including fruit, veg, pots, pans and even your friends! This workshop brings science and music together in a fun and active learning experience that must not be missed!

Title: Fern Brady: Male Comedienne
Description: Following a surprise sell-out run for last year's critically acclaimed debut People Are Idiots, Fern returns with a new show about gender, class and Catholicism. As seen on BBC Three's Britain's Biggest Sexists, Channel 4’s 8 Out of 10 Cats and Stewart Lee's Alternative Comedy Experience. 'Top five young comedians to watch' (Telegraph). 'Appealingly acidic... a great comic sensibility with moments of sparkling verve' (Guardian). 'Bold, whip-smart and unabashedly honest' (Herald). 'Brilliantly on point savvy seething' (List). 'Last year she was promising, this year she’s kicking down the door to the big time' (GiggleBeats.co.uk).

Description: Edinburgh's very own Scottish BAFTA-winning and triple BAFTA-nominated comedian returns to the festival following four consecutive sell-out runs. As seen/heard on Drunk History (Comedy Central), Love Island (ITV2) and The Dog Ate My Homework (CBBC).

With every entertainment under the sun in seventeen venues, come take in a show, enjoy a drink and stay for the day. There's even the Kidzone for the little-ones! ‘The centre of the cultural universe' (Scotsman).

Title: Juliet Meyers: This Flipping Rescue Dog Has Ruined My Life
Description: Juliet (writer on Sarah Millican Television Programme and 8 out of 10 Cats) and her dog have issues. This is a show about unconditional love, anxiety, peeing on things and being a wolf. Contains stand-up, stories, a bit of tenderness (mostly caused by bruising when the dog chased a squirrel), and possibly the actual dog as he doesn’t like being left. 'Devilish… on the edge' **** (Scotsman). ‘Laugh-out-loud show that resonates’ **** (Chortle.co.uk). ‘Quirky and original’ **** (BroadwayBaby.com). ‘Smart... very funny!’ (Independent). Panellist on Breaking The News (BBC Scotland).
Venue description: A stylish and intimate bar, formally known as the Meadow Bar, and now Edinburgh's first social enterprise pub. With a cosy, friendly and welcoming atmosphere, great food and drink, and free Fringe shows through the day, this is a great sociable place for the socially responsible.

Title: Nosferatu's Shadow
Description: Who was Max Schreck, the man behind the monster? Why is he solely remembered for the only horror film he made during a career encompassing 800 parts and 50 films? How did he continue working through the rise of Hitler and the Nazis? What compromises did he have to make? He was a dreamer, a loner, a nature lover, a mystic, a hugely versatile and consistently lauded actor. He performed Shakespeare, Schiller, Moliere and Brecht. He was an expert in expressionism and naturalism. But, who was Max Schreck? To find out, we must liberate him from Nosferatu's Shadow.
Venue description: Step away from the herd and enjoy the best programme at the Festival in this haven of calm and comfort just along from the Cowgate. Featuring shows of all genres from around the world, a trendy bar, posh loos and ... glorious air-conditioning.

Title: Captured
Description: 'One day you and I will just be a pile of photos gathering dust. My eyes captured, but yours staring back.' In a basement flat by the sea, past and present collide in a cascade of forgotten images and a whirlpool of repressed words. Captured is the story of Isaac and Sophie, of photographer and subject, of perception and reality. A raw, politically charged, and poignant two-hander, Captured uses mesmerising projection in this turbulent reunion of past lovers. 'A shining example of upcoming artistic talent within the theatre, and a must-see for any fringe theatre lover' (AYoungerTheatre.co.uk).
Warnings: Partial projected nudity

Description: BBC Radio 4‘s multi award-winner Viv Groskop presents Be More Margo, the follow-up to her sold-out five-star 2015 debut. Title: We're All Mad in Here
Description: We’re All Mad in Here follows the story of Alasdair Carroll, a young gay man living in Edinburgh who comes across an elusive drag club called Curious Appetites. One night, Alasdair follows one of the performers who is running late for work and finds himself amongst a host of familiar characters like you’ve never seen them before. This is a contemporary adaptation of Alice in Wonderland, 150 years since it was first published. This play is about finding your identity and expressing yourself. Expect lip-syncing, big costumes.
Warnings: Adult themes, strong language

Title: The Childhood of a Leader
Description: Set against the backdrop of the 1919 Paris peace conference that led to the Treaty of Versailles, US actor Brady Corbet’s directorial debut is a tautly drawn drama that juxtaposes the rise of fascism in context of an apparently angelic young boy’s tantrums and power struggles with his parents and carers in a large country house. Robert Pattinson has a series of telling cameos, though at the heart of the film is 10 year-old Tom Sweet as the manipulative boy Prescott, tussling with his parents, played by Berenice Bejo and Liam Cunningham. Great design and a memorable soundtrack by Scott Walker. [12A]

Title: The Kagools
Description: Fresh from their hit Australian tour, UK silent comedy duo, The Kagools, return to Edinburgh Fringe. Expect the usual award-winning combination of physical comedy and interactive film as your weatherproofed guides take you on a brand new adventure. This unique show is spontaneous, anarchic fun for everyone! Buxton Fringe Best Family Show 2015. ‘Brimming with wit and imagination... surely one of the outright funniest pieces of the entire festival’ ***** (TVBomb.co.uk). ‘A brilliant show’ ***** (MumbleComedy.net). ‘Beautifully executed. Perfect viewing for all ages and nationalities’ **** (Chortle.co.uk). ‘Pure genius... Clever and entertaining... Comedy gold... Side-splittingly hilarious **** (BroadwayBaby.com).

Title: 'Flatpack' in Fountainbridge
Teaser: Learn about architecture for the people, by the people in this event looking at Wikihouse.
Description: WikiHouse is an open source system that is making amateurs feel empowered to experiment with architecture. It makes it possible for anyone to design, share, download and ‘print’ houses that can reduce waste, be low-cost, and suited to local needs. Find out the story behind this remarkable movement with WikiHouse co-founder Alastair Parvin and Akiko Kobayash from FCI who built the first UK community WikiHouse in Fountainbridge, Edinburgh over 3 days last October.

Title: Get Stuck into Science with the Royal Society
Teaser: Join us where science and reading collide, and take part in exciting drop-in activities inspired by the shortlisted books for the Royal Society Young People’s Book Prize. Get stuck into surprising science, arts and crafts and help us decide which book...

Title: The Funny Brothers
Description: A ‘garden variety’ *** (Easingwold Advertiser) show with plenty of variety, and not much garden. Unlike anything ever before, the Funny Brothers are bringing you all the different types of funny and some new ones, taking inspiration from Morecambe and Wise, French and Saunders, and even Dick and Dom. A four-star comedy duo from the hilarity hotbed of Easingwold, the Funny Brothers will blow your minds and then put them safely back together, without breaching the Occupational Works Act of 1974. Rhys, our technician, is also First Aid trained, just in case anyone’s allergic to funny...

Title: Andrés Neuman
Subtitle: Journey into the Imagination
Teaser: According to Roberto Bolaño, ‘the literature of the 21st century will belong to Neuman’. There’s no better introduction to the work of this rising Argentinian star than How to Travel Without Seeing, a travelogue documenting his flying visits to...
Description: According to Roberto Bolaño, ‘the literature of the 21st century will belong to Neuman’. There’s no better introduction to the work of this rising Argentinian star than How to Travel Without Seeing, a travelogue documenting his flying visits to places across Latin America. The tour becomes a dazzling voyage into the mind of the traveller and a journey into the collective psyche of a Spanish-speaking world.

Title: Soddin’ Flodden
Description: 1513, Flodden Field: among the dead lay Scotland's most popular Stewart King and the flower of her nobility. Who was James IV, the charismatic monarch with a passion for women, alchemy, cannons and metal underwear? Were his 'three steps into England' just a mad-cap, ill-considered, naive adventure, destined to end in disaster? Or was he driven to it by the French, and having suffered relentless provocation by the arrogant Henry VIII? With creative and quirky storytelling interwoven with a witty selection of songs, Ideoms will attempt to dispel the resulting 500-year-old inferiority complex.
Venue description: Spotlites is one of the leading venues at Edfringe, with seven unique, beautiful theatres established at the heart of the Festival. Spotlites has a reputation for quality five and four star sell-outs, clean facilities and caring, helpful staff.

Title: There Was a Soldier...
Description: WWI stories, songs, poems, humour and visuals by performers aged 14-70. The outbreak of war, young men volunteered and pals enlisted together, including Hearts football team. Men sent to France where they find comradeship, hardship, horror, honour and bravery. At home, women worked in transport, farming, factories and munitions. Tales from wounded soldiers sent from Southampton by train to Edinburgh War Hospital, Bangour. Scottish War Hospitals, started by Elsie Inglis in foreign fields after being refused in Britain. ‘Local history at its best – performers live these songs – moving, uplifting, superb!’ (Fiona Hyslop, Culture Minister).
Venue description: Situated in the heart of vibrant Stockbridge, ten minutes walk from city centre.  Stockbridge Church is an attractive Grade-A Georgian listed building. The Sanctuary is a magnificent space which has a flexible stage with the potential of using risers. There is also a balcony with a splendid Church Organ and separate Halls which consist of a large octagonal space and smaller room divided by connecting door. Kitchen.

Join him in the stunning surroundings of the Dome, one of Edinburgh's most iconic and breathtaking buildings, as he orchestrates an awe-inspiring evening of mind reading and illusion. With a cocktail in hand, ascend the stairs, immerse your imagination, and experience wonders at dusk... Complete sell-out 2013-2015. 'The ultimate sparkling diamond of this year's Fringe' ***** (SGFringe.com). 'With formidable style, unbelievable talent and even recognition from David Blaine, Scott is not to be missed' ***** (WhatsOnStage.com). 'A festival experience like no other... unforgettable' ***** (BroadwayBaby.com).

You become the author and watch your very own murder mystery masterpiece unfold live on stage! Each night, Degrees of Error present an unplanned, unscripted and never before seen improvised comedy theatre show which promises to dazzle, enthral and delight. Will you work out whodunnit in time? Recommended by BBC Radio 2. ‘Unrestrained bursts of joy’ ***** (BristolTheatreReview.com). ‘By far the best improvised show that I have seen’ ***** (InterMissionBristol.co.uk). ***** (FringeReview.co.uk). **** (ThreeWeeks). **** (BroadwayBaby.com). **** (FringeGuru.com).

But the citizens have found a heroine: a crackshot sniper, with 100 kills to her name. And she appears indestructible. She’s the Angel of Kobane. Fringe First-winning Naylor’s last play, Echoes, transferred off-West End and Off-Broadway, won seven major international Fringe awards and received 26 four and five-star reviews included the Australian, Guardian, Scotsman, Sunday Mail, Sunday Times, and Times. ‘A hugely impressive play’ (Mark Lawson). Best Theatre, Adelaide 2016. Spirit of the Fringe, Edinburgh 2015.

Title: Mind Power and Magic

There is a myth that we use only 10% of our brains, and while this is not true, there is no doubt that a trained mind can perform tasks that ordinary people may find miraculous. In his 25th Fringe, Edinburgh magician Ian Kendall will be demonstrating feats of mental agility that will boggle the mind, bamboozle the brain and leave you wondering whether there are any practical applications for this particular skill set (spoiler alert: no, not really). Oh, and there will be magic tricks as well. ‘Sleight of hand king’ (Sunday Times).
'Highly entertaining' **** (Scotsman).

Ronnie became an alcoholic and ghost writer for real comics. Luckily, they’ve recently been invited to reunite for a high-profile comeback gig, but can they put the past behind them? Set at the exclusive 28 Queen Street, acclaimed illusionist Scott Silven hosts an exquisite evening of fine dining and whisky tasting interwoven with breathtaking illusion. The bespoke menu provided by James Freeman, whose cuisine has been awarded 10/10 by the Herald, accompanies Scott’s performance and makes for an extraordinary and unforgettable experience. 'Hugely impressive' ***** (STV). 'A must see!' (Herald). 'Scott dazzled, shocked and wowed in equal measure' ***** (Aeon.co). 'The ultimate sparkling diamond of the Fringe' ***** (SGFringe.com).

Code: Eduardo Galeano: Rescuing the Kidnapped Memory of Latin America
Title: Eduardo Galeano: Rescuing the Kidnapped Memory of Latin America
Description: Alastair Hulbert celebrates in words, images and music the great Uruguayan, Educardo Galeano, who died last year. “I am a writer,” Galeano explains in his wonderful trilogy, Memory of Fire, “who would like to contribute to the rescue of the kidnapped memory of Latin America, that despised and beloved land. I would like to talk to her, share her secrets, ask her of what difficult clays she was born, from what acts of love and violation she comes.”

Title: Juliet Barker
Subtitle: The Brontës in their Own Voices
Teaser: Setting new standards in literary biography, Juliet Barker’s The Brontës earned her a reputation as the foremost authority on Yorkshire’s literary family. To mark the bicentenary of Charlotte’s birth, Barker has produced The Brontës: A Life in...
Description: Setting new standards in literary biography, Juliet Barker’s The Brontës earned her a reputation as the foremost authority on Yorkshire’s literary family. To mark the bicentenary of Charlotte’s birth, Barker has produced The Brontës: A Life in Letters. Using selected correspondence written by Charlotte, Emily, Anne and their brother Branwell, a close-knit family is revealed, including elegiac tributes by Charlotte to her beloved siblings. This event is part of Both Sides of the Border, in association with Borderlines, Carlisle's Book Festival.

Description: Jean Rondeau has been stirring up the early music scene since winning the Bruges Harpsichord Competition. Celebrated for his often iconoclastic interpretations of standard repertoire, this young French artist already has two successful solo CDs to his credit. In dynamically charged live performances he aims to convince the world that the harpsichord is cool, yet this modernity is matched by his assured understanding of historical context. In Edinburgh Jean Rondeau will explore the transformative nature of Dance, as portrayed by JS Bach, Rameau and Royer. 'maturity, fabulous touch and originality' (France Musique).

Description: Live Act of the Year at the 2015 Scots Trad Music Awards, Rura are ‘one of the most exciting bands on the Scottish folk scene’ (Songlines). With their second album, 2015's Despite the Dark, Rura have reinforced their reputation as one of Scotland's most powerful folk-based bands. Their exquisitely rugged yet refined blend of fiddle, Highland pipes, whistle, flute, bodhran, guitar and voice has proven to be a resounding hit across the board. They are one of Scotland's most sought after acts. Catch them live and you will see why!
Venue description: The Queen's Hall is a 900-capacity music venue, situated on Clerk Street in the Southside of Edinburgh. Originally built in 1823 as Hope Park Chapel, it was converted to its current role in 1979. It now plays host to all types of live music, and presents approximately 200 performances every year.

Title: Molly Whuppie
Description: Molly and her mother and sister live by the seashore. A great winter descends and freezes the sea. At night, Molly spies the golden towers of a castle high on the mountain. She tiptoes off up the mountain to ask the King for food for the Winter Feast, little knowing there is a Giant in the forest or that to reach the King she must cross the Bridge of the One Hair! A highly entertaining adventure; Molly finds things are not what they seem and she is bolder and cleverer than she imagined! 'It's just a joy' (Herald).

Title: The Man Who Knows Everything
Description: What would you ask someone who knew absolutely everything in the whole wide world? What would a dinosaur watch on TV? Why isn’t cat food mouse flavoured? Who invented alphabet spaghetti? What’s the smelliest food? What will I be when I grow up? Join Ophelia as she meets The Man Who Knows Everything, who shares some of the best stories in the world including Aesop's fables, Brothers Grimm and many more. Performed by two comic performers with decades of experience in music, puppetry, comedy and illusions, this is an unforgettable hour to stimulate everyone’s imagination.

Title: Once...
Description: Multi award-winning physical theatre company Derevo bring their sold out hit (Fringe First, Herald Angel), a groundbreaking masterpiece of love, longing and laughter. On one rainy day, the lightning of love struck their hearts. The story starts rolling through laughter and tears, past the pessimistic Cupido, the elegant evil, past silly death to the unknown end... A fairy tale dedicated to the eternal child living in us all. 'Bravo, Derevo, for reminding us that it's better to be heartbroken than heartless' (Herald). 'Absolutely stunning... the best of the best' (Scotsman). 'A love song to your soul' (List).
Warnings: Strobe lighting for a few seconds. Partial nudity.
Venue description: Assembly George Square Theatre is perfectly located next to Assembly George Square Gardens and Studios for pre or post show drinks or food. Title: Playful Cities
Teaser: Join the experts to investigate why healthy play is important for the adult mind
Description: In the past play was rarely thought of as an activity for adults, however this is changing as science reveals how important it is for our minds. Joining us will be Verity McIntosh who produced Playable City Awards 2015; Donald Gow, Senior Zoo Keeper and expert in primate play at Edinburgh Zoo; Dr Amanda Seed, lecturer in psychology and neuroscience and Dr Tine Bech, play researcher and artist. The event will be hosted by Francesca Perry, social and community editor for Guardian Cities. During the event there will also be the chance for some play!

Title: 23, Please: The Sketch Show That Never Was
Description: 23 what? 23 pleases? 23 hours in a day? We know that the number 23 is crucial. We don’t know why. From the Cambridge Footlights; this sketch show hasn’t happened, isn’t happening and will not happen. But don’t let that stop you coming to see it. ‘23, Please combines sketch, mime, songs, and impressions for an hour of unadulterated hilarity' ***** (Varsity). ‘Varied, relatable and, most importantly of all, funny’ ****½ (TheTab.com). ‘Innovative and excellent’ ***** (CambridgeTheatreReview.com).
Warnings: Strong language, drug references, mild sexual references
Venue description: C nova, our popular seven-storey multiplex, is an unrivalled city centre hub. Features intimate studio theatres and fantastic found spaces. C nova's spaces are ideal for smaller-scale theatre, physical theatre, cabaret and comedy. C nova also houses installation spaces and immersive environments. C nova is part of the C venues curated programme taking place in over twenty performance spaces at multiple city-centre venues in our 26th year at the Fringe.

Title: Rob Biddulph: Odd Dog Out
Teaser: Following the success of his 2015 Waterstones Children's Book Prize-winning picture book Blown Away, Rob Biddulph returns with Odd Dog Out. Come and meet Rob, hear why he likes creating picture books with animal themes and watch him draw some of his...
Description: Following the success of his 2015 Waterstones Children's Book Prize-winning picture book Blown Away, Rob Biddulph returns with Odd Dog Out. Come and meet Rob, hear why he likes creating picture books with animal themes and watch him draw some of his best-loved characters. Tickets admit 1 child and 1 accompanying adult. Adult supervision recommended.

Title: Phil Nichol: Twenty
Description: Wow. Where does the time go? Double nominee and Edinburgh Comedy Award winner Phil Nichol celebrates his 20th year of solo comedy shows at the Fringe. To honour this milestone Phil presents his greatest hits of the last two decades. It'll be eye-popping, gut-wrenchingly funny! Did we mention that it's been 20 years? If you have seen him perform live then you will know that this is going to be one of his greatest all-time performances. It's been 20 years people! Do not miss this show. Book Early!
Warnings: Parental guidance
Artist: Brett Vincent for Get Comedy by arrangement with Glorious Management
Venue description: Assembly Checkpoint is the Fringe's premier venue for cabaret, music and more. The venue is located inside an old church and exudes warmth and charm. There is a bar inside the upstairs venue and further drinking and dining options downstairs.

Title: Celebrity Organ Recitals 2016 – 1
Description: Hear the glorious sounds of St Giles' famous Rieger organ. Franz Josef Stoiber plays Bach, Reger, Bruckner and Elgar, together with his own improvisations. A feast of musical colour in these historic surroundings.
Venue description: Founded in the 1120s, St Giles' was the church of John Knox during the Reformation and is renowned for its stained glass, Rieger organ and beautiful Thistle Chapel. Open daily. Free guided tours, concerts and shop. Donations welcome. For access and prices to the newly opened Roof and Tower Tours check website.

Title: Maggie's Plan
Description: A delightfully funny and cleverly interweaving story of mis-matched relationships, director Rebecca Miller’s film is a real pleasure, with the love triangle between Greta Gerwig (Maggie of the title), Ethan Hawke (a would-be novelist) and Julianne Moore (terrific as the intellectually intimidating Dane) wonderfully drawn out as they engage in witty banter and hilarious rants. With Bill Hader and Maya Rudolph also featuring, it amounts to a real rom-com pleasure. [12A]

Description: Freaky Family are back! Aki Remally, Jamie Graham and Allan Ferguson head this groundbreaking band traversing funk, jazz, hip hop beats and groove sensibility. A space funk odyssey.

Title: Anti-White PC Mangina Activate!
Description: Dick Coughlan thought he was a good guy. That was until he met the internet and soon found out he was actually an evil, ball-less, genocidal, race-traitorous bastard! Now, after seven years, even he doesn't know. This is his bizarre journey deep into the weirdest, darkest and funniest recesses of the interwebs. ‘Undeniably funny’ ****(BroadwayBaby.co.uk). ‘Passionate and hilarious’ (Paul Sinha). ‘The man is a killer’ (Reginald D. Hunter).
Venue description: Located right on the Royal Mile, The White Horse has been reborn in the last two years as a stylish bar, cafe and bistro right in the centre of Edinburgh. With great value lunches, followed by free shows from late afternoon until the end of the night.

Title: The Sounds of Science
Teaser: This extraordinary project reveals how humans have changed the world over the last 10,000 years through a timeline of science and engineering played live using nothing more than sound.
Description: Launching at the Science Festival, this extraordinary project reveals how humans have changed the world over the last 10,000 years through a timeline of science and engineering played live using nothing more than sound. Celebrated percussionist Dame Evelyn Glennie will perform the world premier of a groundbreaking 21-minute soundscape written by composer Jill Jarman and conceived by timeline specialist and world history author Christopher Lloyd and a discussion about the project will follow. With generous support from the Institution of Mechanical Engineers

Title: Dylan and Donovan: The Prophet, the Poet and the Sorcerer’s Apprentice
Description: Two musical icons from different sides of the world, and the fascinating story of their meeting, their rivalry and how their music shaped a generation. One of the few singers sanctioned by Dylan, international singer/songwriter Steve Foster from Adelaide revives the music and the simpler times from the 60s of peace, love and war! Interspersed with his own million seller hits, Steve takes you on a journey down memory lane when protest songs made a difference, and the world was Mellow and Yellow! Wonderful memories!

Venue description: C scala at the majestic Saint Stephen's Stockbridge hosts some of our biggest shows in a building with an impressive history. C scala is part of the C venues curated programme taking place in over twenty performance spaces at multiple city-centre venues in our 26th year at the Fringe.

Title: Neil Gaiman: Dream Dangerously
Description: The European premiere of the official documentary film on Neil Gaiman, one of the world's most beloved storytellers (Sandman, American Gods, Stardust, Coraline, Neverwhere, Dr Who) and winner of every major science fiction and fantasy award, including the Hugo, Nebula and Newberry. The screening will be followed by an in-person Q&A with Executive Producer Geoff Notkin, star of TV’s Meteorite Men and Neil Gaiman’s lifelong friend.

'We are all monkeys vying for status! A group of actors. Trying to do a play. Locked in a radio studio. Go tumbling down a black hole in this disturbingly wünderbar and terrifically bonkers twisted dark comedy.' (Bring your own banana!) Description: A completely improvised Shakespeare play inspired by audience suggestions. Bursting with comedy, love, tragedy, mistaken identity and everything between, this show will delight Shakespeare nerds and newbies alike. Back for a third year, the cast buckle on the Bard's britches to bring you the plays he never wrote. 'Shakespeare from the hip. Ingenious and very funny' (Will Gompertz, BBC Arts Editor). 'They pull a seemingly authentic Bard play out of thin air' Recommended (FringeReview.co.uk). 'Outstanding hour of theatre' **** (BroadwayBaby.com). 'Riotous fun' ***** (PlaysToSee.com). 'An impressive display of improv' **** (ThreeWeeks).

Description: One man. One hour. Three courses. Comedian George Egg is also a fanatical cook with an anarchic approach to making meals. In this absurd cocktail of stand-up comedy and striking innovation George prepares a three course meal using the equipment you’ll find in a hotel room. And you can taste it at the end. Just three chances to catch the total sell-out show from Edinburgh 2015. ‘A genius… he is the friendly face of anarchy, the anarchic face of food and the foodie face of comedy’ (Scotland on Sunday).

Title: Fin Taylor: Whitey McWhiteface
Description: Taylor the 'filth maestro' (Time Out) takes on the ickiest thing there is! Being white. Set 'potential for backfire' to maximum. Taylor follows up last year's show Stink, which the Scotsman called 'the punchiest, densest, most wide-ranging hour of stand-up at the Fringe', with an hour that's just about one thing. 'A brilliant analysis of white privilege... masterful stand-up' (Scotsman). 'Says Honky and Cracker more than Reg D Hunter in his prime' (List). This virtuoso band (fiddle, accordion, piano, bass and percussion), featuring some of Scotland's finest musicians, will also perform excerpts of their recently commissioned silent film score Salt for Svanetia. Title: The Dwelling Place
Description: Be transported into an abandoned cottage on the Outer Hebrides. Brothers Jamie and Lewis Wardrop invite you to experience their swirling surround multimedia performance, teasing out the jarring sense of absence and the loss of a profound island culture found in a humble island home. Striking live visuals, electronic sound and the words of the great highland poets. ‘…reminiscent of Boards of Canada and the Radiophonic Workshop, with the hallucinatory quality of a fever dream, and yet it has a gritty sense of defiance, of survival and keeping the spirit of Old Scotland alive.’ (AcrosstheArts.co.uk).
Venue description: Uniquely within Edinburgh's former Royal (Dick) Veterinary College, Summerhall presents high quality, engaging, challenging and exhilarating theatre, music, dance, visual arts for people of all ages. Our busy bar restaurant and cafe offers a wonderful selection of food and drink; the courtyard an epicentre of al fresco bars and street food. Not all of our shows are listed here. The entire programme of performance and visual arts is at www.summerhall.co.uk
Venue accessibility:

Our step free access is through the side entrance on Summerhall Square. The Royal Dick Bar and Restaurant is situated to your right as you come in (with a ramp at the rear of the bar) and there is a ramp directly ahead of you that leads to the Reception, Box Office, Shop and Café.

If you would like more information about the accessibility of particular shows, or if you wish to arrange a familiarisation tour of the venue prior to the festival, please do not hesitate to contact us by phone on 0845 874 3000 or by email on info@summerhall.co.uk

Title: Inspired by Nature
Teaser: Learn about how we can look to nature to invent elegant manufacturing solutions for a sustainable future.
Description: Nature has been perfecting solutions to problems since life began 4.1 billion years ago. The results of natural selection have already inspired our innovation and creativity. Now we need to look to nature again if we are to invent elegant manufacturing solutions for a sustainable future. Join Prof Thomas Speck from the Botanic Gardens of Freiburg and Dr Kalina Raskin from CEEBIOS (the first European Excellence Centre dedicated to Biomimicry) to discuss developments in biomimetics.

Title: Labels
Description: 'Powerful, important and funny' (Emma Thompson). The internationally acclaimed story of migration, family and prejudice returns to Edinburgh! Navigating a childhood in 90s England, a cacophony of right-wing rhetoric and a global refugee crisis, this honest, human tale of multicultural Britain is not to be missed. Expect paper planes, racist romances and lots of sticky labels! ***** (BroadwayBaby.com). ***** (ThreeWeeks). ***** (BritishTheatreGuide.info). Winner: Scotsman Fringe First Award and Holden Street Theatre’s Edinburgh Award, 2015. Winner: Best Theatre Award (Week 2) and Peace Foundation Award, Adelaide Fringe 2016. 'Terrific and really thoughtful' (Lyn Gardner, Guardian).
Warnings: Occasional strong language.

Title: Dersu Uzala
Description: Based on the memoirs of Vladimir Arsenievan, the early 20th century explorer who mapped much of the territory of the Russian Far East,   Akira Kurosawa’s Dersu Uzala tells the story of an unusual friendship between Arseniev (Yuri Solomin) and the nomadic tribal hunter for whom the film is named (Maksim Munzuk). The unspoiled vastness of the Siberian wilderness, so utterly unlike the modern Japanese landscape with its cultivated forests, offered a radically new canvas for Kurosawa. Always a powerful visual stylist with a flair for action, the director crafted some of his most striking imagery for this breathtaking drama. [U]

Title: Wearable Circuits

You’ll learn some basic electronics and how to design a circuit using LED lights, buzzers and switches and we’ll give you as much help as you need with the needlework. Bring along an item of clothing, soft toy, bag, flag, or banner (anything you can sew!) and we’ll provide the rest.

Title: Shappi Khorsandi
Subtitle: A Top Comedian Comes of Age
Teaser: UK-Iranian Shappi Khorsandi is a star of stand-up who has mined her comic talent to unearth a witty, sometimes shocking debut novel. Nina is Not OK is a coming-of-age drama about a young teenage girl battling her addictions: it’s a book that should...
Description: UK-Iranian Shappi Khorsandi is a star of stand-up who has mined her comic talent to unearth a witty, sometimes shocking debut novel. Nina is Not OK is a coming-of-age drama about a young teenage girl battling her addictions: it’s a book that should appeal to fans of Caitlin Moran. What tempted Khorsandi to shift from making people laugh in public to working on the grand scale of longform fiction?

Title: Lost Voice Guy: Disability for Dunces Volume Two
Description: Award-winning comedian Lost Voice Guy started off in a disabled Steps tribute band. They were called Ramps. That didn't work out though, so he's answering more of your stupid questions instead. Lost Voice Guy said: 'I’m often asked if I really can talk after my gigs, because obviously pretending to be disabled for the sake of entertainment is perfectly acceptable!? If I was going to do that, I’d pretend to be blind, then my guide dog could shit on everyone who didn’t laugh. So it's time I answered these bizarre questions.'
Warnings: All Seating is unreserved. Latecomers may not be admitted.

A much-anticipated follow-up to Pixar’s delightful 2003 hit Finding Nemo, this beautifully rendered sequel will enthrall, with fans young and old keen to catch up with the adventures of Dory and her undersea friends.
The film picks up six months after Finding Nemo, with warm-hearted amnesiac Dory (again wonderfully voiced by Ellen DeGeneres), suddenly recalling childhood memories specifically about the ‘jewel of Morro Bay’ in California. Accompanied by Nemo (Hayden Rolence) and Nemo’s father Marlin (Albert Brooks), she heads off to try and find her family, and they make their way to the Monterey Marine Life Institute. There they meet Hank (Ed O’Neill) a grumpy octopus who becomes their guide, beluga whale Bailey (Ty Burrell) and whale shark Destiny (Kaitlin Olson).
Director Andrew Stanton (Finding Nemo) is back guiding the film, with Angus MacLane on board as co-director and a wonderful voice cast that also features Diane Keaton, Eugene Levy, Willem Dafoe, Idris Elba and Dominic West.
The arrival of a new Pixar film is always a cause for excitement, and this sublime sequel makes for a delightful piece of aquatic animated entertainment. [U]

Title: Iphigenia in Tauris
Description: By JW von Goethe. Iphigenia, Diana’s priestess, has to immolate all foreigners entering the country. Her kindness leads King Thoas to suspend this barbarian custom. With no inheritor, Thoas wishes to marry her and, as she refuses, re-establishes human sacrifices. Orestes and his friend Pylades arrive in Tauris. As foreigners, they are destined to be sacrificed by Iphigenia... This classical play of amazing modernity talks about highly topical subjects such as gender equality, rejection of foreigners and triumph of humanity over barbarism. Iannis Xenakis’s Musik gives a fascinating dimension to Simone Rist’s timeless original staging.

Description: With Stellar Quines Theatre Company, the Book Festival presents a vibrant production of Alice Munro’s stories, taken from the Nobel Prize-winning author’s collection The View from Castle Rock, which imagines the extraordinary experiences of Munro’s Scottish ancestors who sailed from Leith Docks in 1818 in the hope of a better life in Canada. Acclaimed director Marilyn Imrie and multi award-winning playwright Linda McLean have created, in this word-for-word adaptation from Munro’s text, a powerful drama about the 19th century Scottish migrant experience. Daily performances at artSpace@StMarks.

Title: A Flag Without a Country
Description: Acclaimed director Bahman Ghobadi blends documentary with drama (in a similar fashion to his 2009 film Nobody Knows About Persian Cats), with real people placed into dramatised moments. This time round it is Kurdish pilot and engineer ‘Nariman the pilot’ and pop star/actress Helly Luv – he is setting up a pilot training scheme while she is planning a blissfully garish pop video. The two only acknowledge each other towards the end of the film, when the shadow of ISIS haunts the region and the Kurdish people. [12A]

Title: Audience as Producer: The Future of Content
Description: The past decade has seen technology democratise content, enabling audiences to access and shape content in unprecedented and innovative ways. Major news stories are now broken long before camera crews arrive on the scene. Live streaming technologies allow audiences to participate in events happening around the world in real time. Social media channels allow us to create and curate own our interactions and experiences. Audiences no longer want to be told what to experience, when and how. If anyone can be a producer, what’s the future of content?

Drawing on her own battles with depression and her Masters in Cognitive Therapy, Wax’s new witty, smart and accessible book, A Mindfulness Guide for the Frazzled, offers insight into why we need to understand ourselves better and arm ourselves with the ability to defeat debilitating stress-related illnesses. Drawing on stories ranging from six-toed cats to fish hips, werewolves and zombie genes, geneticist and author Kat Arney explores how DNA is packed, unpacked and read.

Rúnar Rúnarsson’s award-winning film is an impressively made delight. [PG]

Title: Undercover Refugee
Description: What happens when a 25-year-old Norwegian documentarist and Gaulier-trained actor travels through Europe undercover together with refugees? A show about white heroes, cool policemen and sexy Syrians. Karen Houge went to Lesbos and followed seven Syrian refugees from the beach and through Europa. A new society is formed around the trail; bloggers, journalists, mafia, policemen, refugees and volunteers, functioning together in an absurd system full of paradox. Karen Houge is an Gaulier trained actor, documentarist, stand-up performer and improviser. She describes the journey and the people we meet with depth and humour that takes us beyond tabloid perceptions.
Venue description: Cafe and health food store offering freshly prepared vegetarian, vegan, gluten-free, Scottish food and drink on the menu from 9am daily. During the Fringe we host a selection of PBH Free Fringe shows in our basement function room. No age restrictions.
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site

Title: Pop-Up Science: Dr Book
Teaser: Visit Dr Book where our book doctors will dispense advice and suggestions to cure all your reading ailments
Description: Stuck for something to read? Looking for new and exciting authors to explore? Then visit Dr Book where our book doctors will dispense advice and suggestions to cure all your reading ailments. You’ll even get your own reading prescription to take away with you. Consultations available for children and teens - no appointment necessary!

Title: Cycling from Land's End to John O'Groats With a Piano
Description: From street musician to concert artist and back again, the man who was Marvin Hanglider is celebrating his 60th birthday by becoming a fundraiser for Children in Need. A virtuoso pianist, raconteur, songwriter and multi-instrumentalist, Mike Hatchard presents a show that reflects on an extraordinarily diverse career, including forays into cartooning and comedy. His 2016 tour begins at the open air Minack Theatre in Land's End from where he plans to cycle about fourteen hundred miles performing at arts centres, village greens, even people's front rooms – and the Fringe.

Title: Hang
Description: Pinter-esque at times, Hang is set in the near future where the death penalty has returned to the UK, with a twist. Shot through with dark humour, it dramatises the inadequacy of words and the impossibility of saying or doing the right thing in extreme circumstances. It follows one woman's inner turmoil as she comes to a decision that she must live with forever.  She is guided by officials for whom squaring the procedural protocols and human empathy does not come easily. From Yellow Jacket Productions – a newly formed company of 2016 graduates from The Poor School.
Venue description: C nova, our popular seven-storey multiplex, is an unrivalled city centre hub. Features intimate studio theatres and fantastic found spaces. C nova's spaces are ideal for smaller-scale theatre, physical theatre, cabaret and comedy. C nova also houses installation spaces and immersive environments. C nova is part of the C venues curated programme taking place in over twenty performance spaces at multiple city-centre venues in our 26th year at the Fringe.

Title: The Young and the Wild Shorts
Description:
Ranging from the heart-wrenching to the surreal, this year’s collection of shorts from The Young and the Wild offer something a little different for young adult audiences. There’s the promise of kebab van rockets, the last Hong Kong egg laid in a dystopian world, and even gritty gang violence with a twist. These films pose real questions for the future from all over the world and their stories are sure to inspire and intrigue you. [15]
Code Red  Sabrina Doyle/USA/2016/15 min
Inspired by a true life story, Code Red has everything a coming-of-age film should offer - friendship, video games, and of course, periods.

Estate  Ronny Trocker/France, Belgium/2016/7 min
It all started with a photograph. Inspired by a single picture by Juan Medina, a story of the refugee crisis and the power of images unfolds.

Hux  Mageina Tovah/USA/2016/12 min
The end of the world. A girl on the autism spectrum. Mageina Tovah delivers a breathtaking and utterly convincing performance as well as her directorial debut.

A Night in Tokoriki (O noapte în Tokoriki)  Roxana Stroe/ Romania/2016/18 min
Who doesn't want to find out what a rural Romanian club night is like? There are certainly more donkey-drawn carts, and a possible romance...

Spoetnik  Noël Loozen/Netherlands/2015/11 min
What happens when a mysterious young motorbike rider starts working at a Spoetnik kebab van opposite a brothel? You've got 11 minutes to find out...

War  Nilesh Bell Gorsia/UK/2015/5 min
In the urban centres of Britain gang violence is a brutal and bloody reality for many. But is something sweeter around the corner for these sworn enemies?

A Well Spent Afternoon  Martin Turk/Slovenia, Croatia/2016/8 min
Exquisitely shot and full of childhood nostalgia, a simple walk home between father and son becomes a moral message about human compassion.

Title: Experimental: The Show that plays with your mind
Teaser: Prof Richard Wiseman returns to the Festival with Experimental, an interactive experience like no other!
Description: Prof Richard Wiseman returns to the Festival with Experimental. An interactive experience like no other as you take part in live mind-blowing psychology experiments that will make you laugh, scream and gasp. There’s no performer. It’s just you and the unknown. Devised and presented by Prof Richard Wiseman.

Title: Designing Fictional Worlds
Teaser: Come and delve into the virtual world!
Description: Come and delve into the virtual world! In this fascinating event we’ll look at how virtual worlds are designed and created, what paradigms the designers base them on, and the psychology of why so many people are drawn to them. Join our panel of experts, including award winning author Charles Stross and Emese Domahidi, researcher in social aspects of gaming, as they discuss the how fictional worlds can help us deal with the real world.

Title: The Inevitable Heartbreak of Gavin Plimsole
Description: Winners of Les Enfants Terribles Award 2016. If you had a finite number of heartbeats, how would you make each beat count? Gavin feels a flutter in his heart. Is it heartburn? Is it that girl across the room? Or is it a malformation of his heart – a sticky, red time bomb? Gavin is given a life-changing diagnosis. Hiding in his shed, he assesses his entire life. What has he done with those beats? Which has he thrown away? And how many did he lose when she broke his heart?
Venue description: The Pleasance Dome is at the very centre of the now famous Bristo Square, featuring the very best comedy and theatre in 5 venues all under one roof. With great bars and cafes, come soak up the legendary Pleasance atmosphere throughout the day and stay for the fun late in to the night. Open until 5am
