Title: The Improv Musical
Description: Back by popular demand, The Improv Musical is ready to hit the Edinburgh Festival Fringe for its third year! Catchy songs and hilarious storylines – completely improvised! The show is in your hands! ‘Knockabout farce’ **** (ThePublicReviews.com). ‘A fantastic feel for the comic touch.’ (BroadwayBaby.com). ‘A very good, fun show’ (EdFringeReview.com). ‘A total, rollicking hoot’ **** (AYoungerTheatre.com).

Title: Unbound
Subtitle: Liz Lochhead and the Hazey Janes
Teaser: Liz called. She said, ‘I’m working with The Hazey Janes. Together we are creating a celebration of the lyric impulse and the love of strange and new harmonies – I quite fancy doing an Unbound session; what do you think?’ Fresh from their recent...
Description: Liz called. She said, ‘I’m working with The Hazey Janes. Together we are creating a celebration of the lyric impulse and the love of strange and new harmonies – I quite fancy doing an Unbound session; what do you think?’ Fresh from their recent CD release The Light Comes Back, former Scots Makar Liz Lochhead and the much loved and lauded indie pop band The Hazey Janes, led by experimental jazz saxophonist Steve Kettley, give you a night of sensational sounds and sonnets. Over 18s only.

Title: A Comedy Tapas
Description: Chris O Neill serves up samples of ten different acts every day so you can pick your favourites. Cooked up to make your Fringe more easily digested and fun. A free taster containing mainly comedy and sometimes a sample of spoken word. Everyone gets a menu with a map to find their chosen acts. Get your Fringe off to a great start and see new acts every day.
Venue description: Opium alternative bar and nightclub is Edinburgh's longest running dedicated rock venue. Open seven days a week until 5am, Opium offers the very best in alternative entertainment. From rockaoke to live bands. During the Fringe we host a wide selection of top, 5 star PBH Free Fringe comedy. Over 18's only.
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site

Title: A Fool’s Paradise: 30 Shakespeare Scenes in 60 Minutes
Description: Six Actors. 60 minutes. 30 Shakespeare scenes. Can they do it? If not, someone gets a pie in the face. Seriously. We got the pies. You choose what to see next, play bingo for prizes and explore some of Shakespeare’s favourites, and lesser known pieces, too. You’ll laugh, you’ll cry, you’ll get chocolate tossed into the audience. Just the way Shakespeare intended.
Venue description: At the foot of the Royal Mile, Venue 13 has been bringing the best of emerging talent from the UK and the wider world to the Edinburgh Festival Fringe since 1996. With a real focus on theatre, but also contemporary dance and physical performance, Venue 13 prides itself on offering more than just simply fringe theatre. Audiences keep coming back for more to ‘this serene little venue’ ([i]Scotsman[/i]).

Title: Bach for Solo Violin
Description: The accomplished and acclaimed Hungarian-born violinist Tamas Fejes returns to the Edinburgh Festival Fringe to perform from his debut CD a selection of Sonatas and Partitas by JS Bach, including the might Chaconne, for unaccompanied violin. Audience comments: ‘I have listened to live recitals and recordings of Bach's Partitas/Sonatas by many violinists since the days of Heifetz. Tamas Fejes ranks among the best. It is an amazing experience to listen to him giving what appears to be an effortless performance – an experience of a lifetime, not to be missed.’
Venue description: Fringe venue number 60.

Title: Home Is Where the Harp Is
Description: Atmospheric songs, an eclectic range of instruments, beautiful harmonies and arrangements blended with Scottish, Irish and African traditions. Witches’ Brew (singers/songwriters Pauline Vallance and Clare Robertson) return to the Fringe for the third year. Let them entertain you with new songs, old songs and refreshing instrumentation. ‘Great musicality. Very interesting material’ (Danny Kyle, Open Stage judges at Celtic Connections Festival). Come and fall under their spell! paulinevallance.co.uk. clarerobertson-creative.co.uk

Title: Blue Rose Code
Description: ‘I feel like I've been forever a child of exile, a wanderer. These songs started to give me a context, a feeling, an understanding of where I come from, I am grateful’, says Blue Rose Code of his new trad project. Teaming up with three of the finest contemporary folk musicians: Ross Ainslie, Jarlath Henderson and Angus Lyon, for the first time Ross will be performing traditional songs as well as his own. 'It is extraordinary how these stories can live on beyond the hand that penned them, telling me about myself. It'll be a special show.’

Title: All the King’s Men: The 11 Tour
Description: Fresh from London, Boston, New York performances, returning to Edinburgh for a sixth year. The first British group ever to compete at the Boston Sings International A Cappella Festival. With five stars and an official sell-out in 2015, their all-vocal covers are a must-see. This year is the group’s seventh Edinburgh Fringe. This hit show includes music from Sam Smith to Tina Turner, and songs from ATKM’s current studio album, 11. Nominated for Contemporary A Cappella Recording Awards. ‘See these men take the Fringe by storm’ ***** (BroadwayBaby.com).
Venue address: Saint Stephen's Stockbridge, St Stephen Street/St Vincent Place
Venue description: C scala at the majestic Saint Stephen's Stockbridge hosts some of our biggest shows in a building with an impressive history. C scala is especially suited for circus, large scale physical and musical theatre, larger music and cabaret shows and international work. C scala is part of the C venues curated programme taking place in over twenty performance spaces at multiple city-centre venues in our 26th year at the Fringe.

Title: The Sanctuary
Description: Part of the Fringe Central Events Programme, for Fringe participants. Your opportunity to get away from the madding crowd to a calm, completely quiet space where you can just be for a while before going back out there. Providing a bit of peace in a comfortable environment, there is no need to book – just come in and relax. Brought to you by Equity and the Fringe Society as part of the ArtsMinds.co.uk initiative.
Warnings: You may be asked to show your Fringe Participant pass on entry.
Venue description: Fringe Central is a resource developed specifically for Fringe participants. A hub for professional and creative development opportunities and home to our Arts Industry, Media and Venues and Companies offices, you will find support and advice as well as a programme of over 100 free events all designed to help you make the most out of your Fringe experience.

Title: Sci-Fi Silliness with Matt Brown
Teaser: Author and presenter Matt Brown takes you on a time-travelling adventure with the latest book in his Compton Valance series, Revenge of the Fancy-Pants Time Pirate. When Compton leaves a sandwich to decompose (all in the name of science, of course...),...
Description: Author and presenter Matt Brown takes you on a time-travelling adventure with the latest book in his Compton Valance series, Revenge of the Fancy-Pants Time Pirate. When Compton leaves a sandwich to decompose (all in the name of science, of course...), he accidentally creates a time machine. Expect hilarity to ensue as Matt mixes sci-fi with lots of silliness.

Title: Other Voices Spoken Word Cabaret
Description: Welcome to our open-hearted open mic, where you can enjoy features from fantastic spoken word artists and different special guests daily, all with a sumptuous cabaret vibe. This show is dedicated to the words and voices less heard and hosted by PBH Spoken Word Artistic Director, Fay Roberts. ‘A showcase of spoken word at its best… Don’t miss this, it’s wonderful’ ***** (ThreeWeeks). ‘Other Voices is brilliant and, more than that, it’s important’ **** (SabotageReviews.com).
Venue description: The Banshee Labyrinth is a teeming pub that is said to be Scotland's most haunted pub. Regular comedy nights, karaoke and live music will keep you entertained until the wee small hours. Three performance spaces, three bars, one open from 12.30-05:00. 18+ only. www.thebansheelabyrinth.com
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site

Title: Performance Anxiety
Description: Award-winning comedians Benji Waterstones 'Distinctive worldview’ (Steve Bennett) and Jake Baker ‘Imaginative and original' (Kate Copstick), explore amongst other things: their neuroses, befriending Utterly Butterly customer services and using a Harry Potter book as a murder weapon.
Venue description: Edinburgh's premiere party venue and the free mega venue with six rooms of free shows running throughout the day and night, all located around a vibrant and buzzing courtyard. With a huge drinks selection, a wide menu, hog roast, and plenty of new surprises each year! Shows run from 09:00-02:00, with music and dancing trough until 5am, the venue is barely ever closed in August.

Title: Art Explorers
Teaser: Get inspired to make your own work of art as we explore the beauty of trees from the Garden
Description: Head along to the Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh for an afternoon of creative fun. Get inspired to make your own work of art as we explore the beauty of trees from the Garden using a wide range of colourful and tactile materials with Greengage Arts.

Title: Make your own Contact Speaker
Teaser: Get hands-on with science and sound by building your own contact speaker.
Description: Get hands-on with science and sound! Using a simple solder kit and a piezo transducer, learn how to create a contact speaker that can turn any surface into an amplifier. Test it against cardboard, plastics, fabrics and other surfaces and find out what materials work best for amplifying sound. At the end of the workshop you’ll get to take your contact speaker home!

Title: Danny McLoughlin: Phillip Was Right
Description: When Danny was 10 something bad happened, he was fine. He didn't think it was that bad. Now he's older, he's not fine as he's realised the bad thing was probably badder than he first thought.
Warnings: Buy a ticket in advance to guarantee entry or Pay What You Want at the venue.

Title: Can we address Fuel Poverty and respond to Climate Change?
Teaser: Join experts in fuel poverty and the energy industry to discuss whether Government action to address fuel poverty and action to implement Scottish Government climate change targets are compatible.
Description: Are the UK and Scottish Governments’ actions to address fuel poverty and implement climate change targets compatible? The Church of Scotland will report on this issue at the General Assembly in May. Join Sarah Boyack MSP, Elizabeth Leighton, Policy Advisor and secretariat at the Existing Homes Alliance Scotland, John Cunningham, Head of Energy Unit for Western Isles Council and Shona Stephen, Chief Executive, Queen’s Cross Housing Association, to explore the issues.

Title: Chocolate: Food of the Gods
Teaser: A special interactive evening investigating the past, present and future of chocolate.
Description: The seeds known to science as theobroma cacao (meaning ‘food of the gods’) have a long and fascinating history. In this special interactive evening, we will investigate the past, present and future of chocolate. Chocolate writer and Chief Executive of the Royal Academy of Culinary Arts Sara Jayne Stanes OBE is joined by Prof Paul Hadley, head of the Cocoa Project  at the University of Reading and master chocolatier Aneesh Poppat for a scientific feast for the senses not to be missed. Hosted by Susan Morrison.

Title: Locked In: The Distillery Escape
Description: The Locked In Escape game comes to the Fringe this year for the first time. Gather your team of clever people (between two and five players) and prepare to be mentally challenged. An interactive experience solving the mystery behind who is plotting the downfall of Pickering's Gin. Your team have an hour or less to find and solves clues... and most importantly save the gin. Go on, get Locked In, with only your mental agility to get yourself out. If you loved The Crystal Maze, this is for you.
Venue description: Uniquely within Edinburgh's former Royal (Dick) Veterinary College, Summerhall presents high quality, engaging, challenging and exhilarating theatre, music, dance, visual arts for people of all ages. Our busy bar restaurant and cafe offers a wonderful selection of food and drink; the courtyard an epicentre of al fresco bars and street food. Not all of our shows are listed here. The entire programme of performance and visual arts is at www.summerhall.co.uk
Venue accessibility:
We are committed to making your visit to Summerhall an enjoyable experience and we are working to make our venue as accessible as possible. The building is B-listed and is over one hundred years old and not all of our spaces are fully accessible. 

Our step free access is through the side entrance on Summerhall Square. The Royal Dick Bar and Restaurant is situated to your right as you come in (with a ramp at the rear of the bar) and there is a ramp directly ahead of you that leads to the Reception, Box Office, Shop and Café.
We have lift access to some of the First Floor spaces. Further information about individual spaces and shows can be obtained from the Box Office. If you would like more information about the accessibility of particular shows, or if you wish to arrange a familiarisation tour of the venue prior to the festival, please do not hesitate to contact us by phone on 0845 874 3000 or by email on info@summerhall.co.uk

Our staff are here to help and if there is anything you need assistance with please do not hesitate to ask.

http://www.summerhall.co.uk/about/accessibility/. Title: Wriggle Around the World
Description: Sell-out Edinburgh Festival Fringe 2015! Live concerts for babies and toddlers delivered by a professional violinist and cellist. An educational and interactive experience of classical music where wriggling is allowed, suitable for the whole family. The programme includes music with an international theme, a story about travelling and songs to join in with.
Venue description: Situated in the heart of vibrant Stockbridge, ten minutes walk from city centre.  Stockbridge Church is an attractive Grade-A Georgian listed building. The Sanctuary is a magnificent space which has a flexible stage with the potential of using risers. There is also a balcony with a splendid Church Organ and separate Halls which consist of a large octagonal space and smaller room divided by connecting door. Kitchen.

Title: Twice upon a Time (Kan ya Ma Kan... Marratayn)
Description: Director Niam Itani fled with her family from Beirut to Ghazzeh in 1989, seeking refuge from the Lebanese Civil War. Despite living in poverty, Itani describes her childhood years in Ghazzeh as ‘the best days of my life’, as families lived in solidarity. Connecting with Khalil, a young Syrian refugee in Ghazzeh in 2012, Itani has created a film of profound sensitivity, chronicling the effects of trauma past and present, and their shared hopes for the future. [PG]

Title: Loose Brie Filling My Tin, With Loose Brie, Phil and Martin
Description: From the team that brought you Winfamy, 'bizarre and brilliant' **** (EdFringeReview.com), 'a true pleasure' **** (ThreeWeeks). Phil and Martin have given up their jobs to perform comedy together. Have they made a huge mistake? Can they get along as flatmates? Will they last an hour as a double act, or will the whole thing fall apart? Find out the answers to all of these questions and more in an hour of car-crash comedy.
Artist: Loose Brie, Phil Lindsey, Martin Willis, Free Festival
Venue description: Located at the junction of Princes Street and Leith Street, The Newsroom is right in the heart of Edinburgh with free Fringe shows daily from 11:00-02:00. A recently refurbished, modern and stylish bar.

Title: Seymour Mace: Shit Title
Description: Here we go again. Not sure really. Maybe pretending I’m on a ship? Something out the window? And I’ve got a miniature Christmas village, can’t think what to do with that though. You’ve probably got more idea what I’ll be doing than me so if you think it’ll be brilliant then come along but if you think it’ll be shit then probably don’t bother. Thanks and that. ‘Made me completely lose myself to laughter’ ***** (Times). ‘Like a terrifying clown hiding under your bed’ (Skinny). **** (Fest). **** (List). **** (Chortle.co.uk). **** (Skinny). **** (Mirror). www.seymourmace.co.uk

Title: Strangers: A Magic Play
Description: In the same way that a musical blends theatre with music, Strangers: A Magic Play blends theatre with magic. A mind reader who is told other people’s thoughts by a voice in his head. A children’s entertainer whose private life interferes with his act. A waiter who dreams of making it big in the music industry. A homeless man struggling to survive. Four seemingly separate stories that all share one thing in common. They are interwoven with magic and illusion to create an audience experience unlike any other show in existence.

Title: Gary Little: A Little Bit of Personal
Description: After a successful 2015 Fringe, Gary is back with a brand new show. This time he tells stories of paranoia, hillwalking, prison pen pals and being known as the guy with the dogs! Gary has an incredibly warm, personable style. Combine this with his unflinching honesty and openness, and just a hint of vulnerability, and audiences everywhere fall in love with his easy charm. 'A master storyteller. Runs rings round his comedy peers' (Herald). 'Born Raconteur' **** (Scotsman). 'A f*cking riot' (Bill Burr). 'All you'll remember is how much you laughed' (Chortle.co.uk). www.biggarylittle.co.uk
Warnings: All Seating is unreserved. Latecomers may not be admitted.

Title: Afterhours Comedy: Amused Moose Comedy
Description: Laughter-packed, legendary and unmissable on Saturday nights. In an awesome new roost and totally shimmering plumage, Afterhours, the Fringe's tip-top comedy show, will delight you every time by showcasing the highest flying stand-ups around the Fringe. And we've plucked 2016's brightest fledglings from obscurity to charm you as they soar towards stardom. Hosted by Mark Dolan (Balls of Steel and Sky Movies), Afterhours features famously entertaining comedians, the same as at London's award-winning Amused Moose comedy venues. ‘Best late night comedy’ (List's top recommendation). ‘Awesome late night hilarity’ (ThreeWeeks). ‘Stellar!’ (Scotsman). Line-ups on amusedmoose.com/shows.
Venue description: theSpaceUK present another high calibre venue.  A highbrow alternative to traditional Fringe venues boasting the most comfortable seats in town. Title: Debate: Healthcare
Subtitle: Can Preventing Illness Save the NHS?
Teaser: Rather than focusing on cures for illness, could we alleviate the pressure on the NHS by finding a system based on improving health and wellbeing? Three experts discuss what’s needed to create positive narratives, particularly around palliative care....
Description: Rather than focusing on cures for illness, could we alleviate the pressure on the NHS by finding a system based on improving health and wellbeing? Three experts discuss what’s needed to create positive narratives, particularly around palliative care. Novelist, doctor and psychiatrist Joanna Cannon is joined by Jenny Downham, whose novels explore teenage illness and dementia, and Charlotte Clarke, Head of the School of Health in Social Science at Edinburgh University and specialist in elderly health. A special clinic will be held in the Imagination Lab after the event for anyone wishing to discuss specific issues.

Title: Guitar Multiverse
Description: As seen on BBC Four television and winner of the 2015 Adelaide Fringe Weekly Award for Best Music Show, Declan Zapala returns to the Edinburgh Festival Fringe with his fourth consecutive solo guitar show. Featuring a self-produced audiovisual performance of Steve Reich's 12-guitar part masterpiece Electric Counterpoint, as well as African influenced music by Gary Ryan and Declan's own stunning folk inspired percussive guitar pieces. A must-see for all music lovers. ‘One of the most exciting players on the acoustic guitar scene’ (Guitarist Magazine). ‘Breathtaking’ ***** (ThreeWeeks). ‘Fascinating’ ***** (EdinburghGuide.com). ‘Stunning’ ***** (TheClothesLine.com.au). ‘Immense’ **** (BroadwayBaby.com).

Venue description: C too, one of the first Fringe venues, features two spaces and a relaxed garden café in the heart of the city. Title: Seoul Station (Seoulyeok)
Description: Acclaimed South Korean animator Yeon Sang-ho (The King of Pigs) is a master telling a story about the dark side of the human condition. The story follows a man sleeping rough and a runaway young woman doing their ordinary best to deal with the truly horrific. The film ticks all of the right zombie genre boxes and is genuinely scary at times, but also astutely deals with the disposed as well as the undead. [15]

Romantic, earthy, sensual, playful, passionate, soulful and electric, Daniela Nardi and her Espresso Manifesto have been called all of these and more. Title: And They Played Shang-A-Lang
Description: Following a break after two years of sell-out shows, And They Played Shang-A-Lang is coming back! This is what life was like growing up in 70s Edinburgh, told through laughter, tears and 70s hit musical numbers. We follow Jim's life as he negotiates the stormy waters of adolescence. From school playground to school disco, we witness his life through his memories as he encounters love, death and the opposite sex. This production has it all. The strong cast brings his story to life with verve and energy that will leave you crying out for more.

Description: Somewhere between theatre and stand-up, The Mariuh Caring Career Agency will leave you with extra laughter lines to botox and will add some extra sparkle to your life. Laura Everett and Samantha Ng caricature some of the world's best known celebs to perform a unique and original comedy play. Based in the fantastical setting of The Mariuh Caring Career Agency, an altruistic venture that sees Mariah Carey, played by Samantha, helping less fortunate celebrities to fulfil their career goals. Kate Winslet, played by Laura, is the first and maybe last customer!

Title: First Lady
Description: This is a true story. In the early '90s in Chicago, I fell in love with a man who was running for president – in a dress. This man was Joan Jett Blakk, and he promised to ‘Lick Bush in ’92’. Joan, real name Terence, was an average man playing at being a superhero. HIV was ravaging the queer community and politicians were not doing anything. So Terence put on a dress to change all that. George Orange has been a theatre and circus maker for 25 years, and founder of Mary Bijou Cabaret.
Venue description: We are Scotland's first charity Recovery Cafe, run by people in recovery for people in recovery and public customers who want good value, good quality food in a relaxed space. Description: Two uplifting novels reflect on friendship, secrets and regret. Steeped in Donny Osmond and Babycham, Joanna Cannon’s The Trouble with Goats and Sheep chronicles a mysterious neighbourhood disappearance during England’s 1976 heatwave. South Africa-based Yewande Omotoso’s The Woman Next Door is a tale of two elderly Cape Town women – one black, one white – that brims with tenderness, shame and aching memories.

Title: Aladdin
Description: Battles? Magic? Princesses? We have it all! Come on down to Paradise Green this August and watch Aladdin! The traditional pantomime with a hint of Big Squirrel magic! A cast of six talented performers will take you through Widow Twankey’s Laundry, The Royal Gardens and even the Evil Egyptian Lair of Abanazar! Watch as Aladdin battles for his true love, Princess Yasmin, with the help of his dorky brother Wishee Washee and panto favourite Widow Twankey! Add in the Genie of the Lamp and we have a magic experience for all the family!

Title: The Female Question
Description: Over the 400 years in which he has been a beloved playwright William Shakespeare has only been able to see the problems that his work has caused. Living in a world where his characters are free to talk and express their views, he is faced with the issue of whether he failed them or not. With the help of his over enthusiastic and slightly arrogant younger self Shakespeare decides to finally talk on the biggest problem that he sees in his work... the women. And they aren't exactly happy.

Description: Bigoted misogynist or champion of freedom? Can John Knox, leader of the comprehensive Scottish reformation in the 16th century, still teach us anything today about democracy, equality and freedom from tyranny, or can he be written off as a bigoted religious extremist? In a new play by Jerry Averill in association with New Scottish Arts, John Knox takes you on a journey with the reformer ‘who feared the face of no man.’

Title: Mixing the World: The Power of Global Arts Projects
Description: Digital can bring the world together. At the British Council we have been working to create a friendly knowledge and understanding between the UK and the rest of the world for 80 years. As the world joins us online, we wanted to explore how we can continue to do this in the digital age. In this session, we’ll talk about how we have been doing this through projects including Five Films 4 Freedom – the world’s first online LGBT film festival – and Mix the City.

She joins Karrie Fransman, with Over Under Sideways Down, a comic book produced for Refugee Week that charts the true story of Ebrahim, a boy who fled from Iran aged 15. They discuss their work with Bidisha.

Title: Ash
Description: Based on a true story, Ash explores the life of George Crozier and his journey from his first to his last cigarette. Set against a backdrop of the tobacco industry’s ever-changing advertisements, this humorous and sensitive production uses object manipulation, movement and live music to explore the highs and lows of a lifelong love affair with smoking. Up until the last puff, it’s an addictive story of a Yorkshire community that aren’t planning to quit anytime soon. ‘The ensemble as a whole is connected and playful, and in performance there isn’t a weak link in the team’ **** (RemoteGoat.com).

Title: Russ Peers: Bad Gay?
Description: Is Russ Peers a bad gay? He's chunky, over 40, and knows more about pies than poppers. In his latest show Russ brings his biting wit to bear on society's expectations of what a gay man should be, how he should behave and who he should sleep with in what position. With cutting observations of the gay scene, society's "acceptable face" of gay, and his experiences in and out of the closet Russ looks at his big gay Northern life so far to find out if he really is any good at being gay.

So it’s no surprise that death isn’t like on TV either. But Malachy won’t let the pink disease kill the one thing he does have – hope. Every Day I Wake Up Hopeful is a darkly funny examination of a desperate attempt to take control of life before death does. ‘An absolutely engaging performer’ (Scotsman).

This theatrical vortex of recycled plays, Garbo’s Divine Woman and words from environmental prophets explores our devastating addiction to plastic consumerism. The landfill is closing and the choices are bad for the out of work garbage pickers: prostitution or drugs. Two options present themselves: a gold rush on the high seas recycling the Great Pacific garbage patch, or the unexpected opportunity a Garbo-loving filmmaker brings. This play is a prophecy, a prediction of the future. It's not sentimental, it's real.

Description:

Grand in every sense, Lawrence of Arabia is an example of an established director full of confidence and ambition. Nearly four hours long, several years in the making, and complete with an interval and its own overture, the film aims for greatness and achieves it. Peter O’Toole, then the new boy among international stars, gives a wonderfully charismatic performance as the enigmatic Lawrence. [PG}

Description: How have Scotland’s architectural projects over the past half century shaped the country’s identity? With a disastrous design and build scheme recently resulting in the closure of 17 Edinburgh schools, could it be that neither the state nor the private sector have the courage to invest for the long term? Or do projects like the new Forth Crossing show that Scotland can – when it needs to – show as much courage as ever? Title: Scottish Shorts
Description:
From a little boy zombie who just wants to make friends, to an old woman who just wants to be left alone, a selection of exciting up-and-coming Scottish filmmakers introduce a varied cast of characters and worlds in which to immerse yourself. Find yourself transported from the Scottish coast, to a post-apocalyptic rural landscape, by way of a disastrous dinner party, and the fairy-tale world of a young girl afraid of the wolf at her door and the wheelchair by her bed. [12A]
Crowman  Duncan Nicoll/UK/2015/15 min
A dark rite of passage set in rural Scotland where survival is a struggle and contact with the locals leads only to conflict and brutality.

Dave  Garry J Marshall, Chris Watson/UK/2015/12 min  
Dave is a little boy zombie who, after a terrible disaster, is forced into an unfriendly world where he has to fight to survive.

Grimm Street  Siri Rodnes/UK/2015/17 min  
When an imaginative teenager refuses to accept her health is fading fast, she escapes into her own world, only to find a big bad wolf.

Meet Me By The Water  Raisah Ahmed/UK/2016/14 min 
In a small Scottish fishing town a young Asian woman must decide whether to leave home and family for a new life in South America.

No Place Like Home  Cat Bruce/UK/2015/13 min 
Under threat of imminent eviction from her countryside home, a self-reliant woman struggles to preserve her way of life.

The Rat King  Pavel Shepan/UK/2015/18 min
An anxious mother-to-be must confront a sinister presence in her new home and the growing cracks in her marriage.

A hostess serves her family deadly wild mushrooms. Spores is a darkly comic family drama exploring the things that poison us against each other.

Title: Chris Riddell

Teaser: Award-winning author Siobhan Dowd died in 2007, bequeathing her royalties to a trust which aims to bring the joy of reading to those who need it most. This year the Siobhan Dowd Trust Memorial Lecture is delivered by Children's Laureate Chris Riddell. A...
Description: Award-winning author Siobhan Dowd died in 2007, bequeathing her royalties to a trust which aims to bring the joy of reading to those who need it most. This year the Siobhan Dowd Trust Memorial Lecture is delivered by Children's Laureate Chris Riddell. A prolific illustrator and writer, Riddell joins us to talk about his passion for stories – both written and drawn – and the importance of giving all children access to books.

Title: Marilyn and Sinatra
Description: You know their names but you didn't know their love story... until now. See Marilyn and Sinatra days before this very special play opens in London’s West End. Exhaustively researched, it tells the little-known story of the relationship between showbiz icons Marilyn Monroe and Frank Sinatra. A two-performer show with songs, the play lasts one hour with no intermission. Presented by Sandro Monetti and Jason Haigh-Ellery in association with Lexus Scotland and The Diamond Studio. It stars Jeff Bratz as Frank, Erin Gavin, who also produces, as Marilyn and is written and directed by Sandro Monetti.
Artist: Starring Erin Gavin and Jeff Bratz

Title: Story Shop
Teaser: Immerse yourself in short stories at Story Shop, now in its 10th year, hosted by our friends the Edinburgh UNESCO City of Literature Trust. It’s free and takes place every day at 15.00 in the Spiegeltent. This is your chance to hear up-and-coming...
Description:
Immerse yourself in short stories at Story Shop, now in its 10th year, hosted by our friends the Edinburgh UNESCO City of Literature Trust. It’s free and takes place every day at 3.00pm in the Spiegeltent. This is your chance to hear up-and-coming writers living and working in Edinburgh today. You can find more about the writers and their stories at: www.cityofliterature.com
	@EdinCityofLit #StoryShop

Title: Every Brilliant Thing
Description:
The worldwide smash-hit is back. You’re six years old. Mum’s in hospital. Dad says she’s done something stupid. She finds it hard to be happy. You make a list of everything that’s brilliant about the world.

Everything worth living for.

1. Ice Cream
2. Kung Fu Movies
3. Burning Things
4. Laughing so hard you shoot milk out your nose
5. Construction cranes
6. Me

A play about depression and the lengths we go to for those we love. 

“Heart-wrenching, hilarious… possibly one of the funniest plays you will ever see” **** The Guardian
Warnings: Patrons who require wheelchair tickets must book via the Summerhall Box Office on 0131 560 1581 There are 2 wheelchair tickets plus companions per show. 24 hours notice is preferred.
Venue description: Roundabout is Paines Plough’s beautiful pop-up in-the-round theatre. It offers a unique 360 degree theatre experience with 168-seats wrapped around the stage, state-of-the-art LED lighting and surround sound. Roundabout flat packs and pops-up across the UK bringing the nation’s best playwrights and a thrilling atmosphere to audiences everywhere. "The lovliest venue at the Fringe" The List
Venue accessibility: Paines Plough are excited to be trialing closed captioning within Roundabout this year. Closed captioning will be available on tablets for some shows in Roundabout. Patrons who require a captioning tablet must notify Roundabout front of house via text/call on 07855 744164 or email office@painesplough.com. 24 hours notice is preferred as tablets are limited.  Patrons are advised to collect captioning tablets from Roundabout front of house staff 15-20 minutes before the performance. Full venue site is accessible, Lift level access to all areas, Wheelchair accessible toilet, Reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas

Title: History’s Future
Description: Visual artist Fiona Tan’s striking debut film veers between gentle playfulness to intellectual challenge as it follows a man (an impressively charismatic performance from Mark O’Halloran) who has lost his memory after an assault and attempts to piece his life back together. Tan co-wrote the script with film critic Jonathan Romney, with elusive self-discovery at the heart of its meandering story. [PG]

Title: Dusty Horne's Sound and Fury
Description: It’s 1963. The pioneer of cinematic sound, Jack Foley, has inspired a generation of great ‘foley artists’. Dusty Horne is not one of them. Nevertheless, Dusty will attempt to join the pantheon of celluloid greatness by revealing the secrets of her craft, before a live audience. Witness the hidden magic of foley. Marvel at the madcap mayhem behind famous (and infamous) films. From Hollywood classics to B-movie clangers, you’ll hear thunderclaps, gunshots, broken glass and breaking hearts, as Dusty’s spectacular live sound effects put the emotion into motion pictures. Cinema will never sound the same.
Venue description: The Pleasance Dome is at the very centre of the now famous Bristo Square, featuring the very best comedy and theatre in 5 venues all under one roof. With great bars and cafes, come soak up the legendary Pleasance atmosphere throughout the day and stay for the fun late in to the night. Open until 5am
Venue accessibility: All performance spaces are accessible. A full accessibility guide can be found at www.pleasance.co.uk. A full accessibility guide can be found at www.pleasance.co.uk. Title: Out of the Blue
Description: Embarking on their 13th run at the Edinburgh Festival Fringe, Out of the Blue will captivate you with their unbeatable mixture of vibrant vocals, outrageously unprofessional choreography and often unintentional comedy. With their recent online hits, these floppy haired Oxford undergraduates conjure up a relentless level of energy and enthusiasm that has left audiences beaming around the world. 'If you don't enjoy yourself you're officially the curmudgeon of the Millennium' (Scotsman). Out of the Blue is proud that their show is supporting Helen & Douglas House, the world's first children's hospice, based near their Oxford home.
Venue description: Assembly George Square Theatre is perfectly located next to Assembly George Square Gardens and Studios for pre or post show drinks or food. The theatre itself is a purpose built venue with comfortable modern seating for up to 500, while the The Box is an intimate 80 seat studio hosting great theatre and comedy.
Venue accessibility: Full venue site is accessible, Lift level access to all areas, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. Cobbles in the Square

Title: Jason Byrne is Propped Up
Description: False chins. Giant ducks. Mouse with a moustache. Portable igloos. Mops for legs. On his last British and Irish tour, Jason re-introduced prop comedy mixed with stand up and audience participation. They loved it. So here is a brand new show from the very experienced, very funny, very absolutely trouser-wetting, very can’t watch much more else I might die, comedian. ‘Unmissable’ (Evening Standard). ‘Watching a new Jason Byrne show is a bit like witnessing lightning in a bottle’ (Edinburgh Evening News). ‘The outright king of live comedy’ (Times).
Warnings: Adult content and strong language
Artist: Phil McIntyre Entertainments by arrangement with Lisa Thomas Management
Venue description: The magnificent venue atop the Mound is the most prestigious venue on the Fringe and hosts the finest drama, music and comedy. Entrance and box office through New College Quad off Mound Place. The venue houses three spaces; the Main Hall, Rainy Hall and Baillie Room.
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site, Some areas not reachable by lift or level access, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. Title: The Company of Wolves
Description: Twisted Tales presents an imaginative retelling of Angela Carter's The Company of Wolves. A cautionary tale for girls incorporating puppetry and physical theatre. Join the girls as they stray of the path and into the woods.
Venue description: Located right in the middle of the Mile, seconds from the Fringe stages, a real fringe hub, three theatres offer a diverse programme of new and established work, from theatre to improv, spoken word, music, comedy, monologue, sketch and spoken word, a global feast for all. Title: Big Bang Bash
Teaser: Join us for an out-of-this-world space party!
Description: Join us for an out-of-this-world space party! Sample a space-themed cocktail from the Bar at the End of the Universe then get ready for an intergalactic night out to remember. Unleash your inner astronaut as you take a spacesuit selfie, make an interstellar structure from Splatform and see whether you're fit for orbit with our challenges. Step inside our portable planetarium to discover the wonders of the solar system, watch roving scientists perform mind-boggling experiments or take to the dance floor for the space themed Science Ceilidh. There’ll also be short talks from space experts including Mars One finalist Ryan MacDonald and astrobiologist Lewis Dartnell, not to mention the chance to dance the night away to a space-tacular DJ.

Title: Dirty Glitter
Description: The award-winning Naughty Corner Productions return with Dirty Glitter. A comedy-thriller from the outrageous minds behind The Bastard Queen! and Not the Horse, this neon-noir follows Murphy and Valmont, private investigators hired to find a missing girl during the height of disco, 1979. The investigation leads them to Les Fleurs nightclub in New York, run by resident psychopath Vince Rubel. But to get to him they’ll have to go through his trusted bit-on-the-side, Minnie. Filled with the usual razor sharp wit and unbearable tension, Murphy and Valmont find themselves in a world of blood, betrayal and glitter.
Warnings: Frequent strong language, strong violence and scenes of a sexual nature.

Title: Doctor in the House
Description: Spend an intimate evening of insightful and intelligent comedy with this British doctor. After leaving England for the brighter shores of Australia, Dr Ahmed returns to share some of the comical aspects of being a modern day GP. With sections including Why I Left the NHS and The Lighter Side of Dying, this promises to be an enjoyable evening for healthcare workers and patients alike. Performing to sell-out shows down under, be sure to book early. Don't miss your appointment with this doctor, he will have you in stitches.

Title: Katherine Ryan: Work in Progress
Description: Star of Live at the Apollo, QI and The Jonathan Ross Show, the razor sharp and hilariously funny Canadian returns to the festival. Direct from a complete sell-out national tour throughout the UK and Australia, Katherine premieres her brand new work in progress show. Put this at the top of your must-see list for this year’s Fringe. ‘Young, smart and acridly funny’ (Sunday Times). ‘Thoughtful, funny and just twisted enough’ (Times). ‘Warped wit... striking presence... killer lines... calm confidence’ (Scotsman). **** (Fest). **** (Independent). **** (Chortle.co.uk).
Artist: Live Nation in association with United Agents
Venue description: Come and graze in George Square! Food, drink, two fantastic venues and of course, an upside down purple cow. If you're looking for Udderbelly or Wee Coo, this is the place to be. We also have buzzing bars open til very late!

Title: Exploring Grandma's House with Alice Melvin
Teaser: Enjoy exploring the rooms of Grandma's House with Alice Melvin as she presents her highly detailed and intricate new picture book. Inspired by her childhood visits to her own grandmother's home, this event is a real celebration of the bond between...
Description: Enjoy exploring the rooms of Grandma's House with Alice Melvin as she presents her highly detailed and intricate new picture book. Inspired by her childhood visits to her own grandmother's home, this event is a real celebration of the bond between children and their grandparents. Grab your granny and come and join the fun!

Title: The Rat Pack – Live
Description: See Frank, Sammy and Dean's world-famous recordings brought to life on stage in this sophisticated evening of razor-sharp wit and silky smooth swing. Backed by the sassy, scorching Burelli Sisters and with a full jazz orchestra, this talented cast take a trip back to glamorous Las Vegas, when the Rat Pack ruled the town. With sell-out awards and a host of multi starred reviews under its belt, this show is the ultimate Fringe swing sensation. 'Infinite amounts of cool' ***** (ThreeWeeks). **** (BroadwayBaby.com). Early booking recommended
Venue address: Saint Stephen's Stockbridge, St Stephen Street/St Vincent Place
Venue description: C scala at the majestic Saint Stephen's Stockbridge hosts some of our biggest shows in a building with an impressive history. C scala is especially suited for circus, large scale physical and musical theatre, larger music and cabaret shows and international work. C scala is part of the C venues curated programme taking place in over twenty performance spaces at multiple city-centre venues in our 26th year at the Fringe.
Venue accessibility: Great hall only accessible by two flights of stairs to upper level. Limited access to some parts of venue site, Some areas not reachable by lift or level access, No wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, On street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. Enter venue via St Vincent Place

Title: Colourful Games
Description: Games are more than just fun for babies and small children, taking up most of their time in the first years of their life. By playing, they explore and learn about themselves and the surrounding world: to sit and crawl, climb and jump, grasp and drop, catch and kick, smile and frown, share and make friends, think and enjoy. Bursting with vibrant colour and delightful surprises, this interactive performance invites its young audience to explore the world around them with the help of a dancer. Self-discovery and wonder await. A beautifully crafted immersive experience for little ones.
Venue description: ZOO's award-winning, intimate studio theatres host a feast of the best new writing, emerging dance companies, and breathtaking physical theatre from around the world. Just down the road from the Pleasance Courtyard.

Title: I Love You, You’re Perfect, Now Change
Description: ‘And the Lord God said: let there be man and woman’. And there was man and woman. And that night, man asked woman if she was busy. And woman said, thank you, she’d have to check, but she’d still like to see other people. Love may not be easy, but it has never been so hilarious. Joe DiPietro and Jimmy Roberts’ fast-paced musical comedy pays tribute to right-swipers, parents and diapers, and to those who have dared to ask: ‘Say, what are you doing Saturday night?’
Warnings: Mild sexual content/references
Venue address: St Columba's by the Castle, Johnston Terrace/Victoria Terrace
Venue description: C too, one of the first Fringe venues, features two spaces and a relaxed garden café in the heart of the city. The mainhouse is ideal for musicals, theatre, physical and family shows. The church is popular for music and spoken word. C too is part of the C venues curated programme taking place in over twenty performance spaces at multiple city-centre venues in our 26th year at the Fringe.

Title: The Concept
Description: Given the chance, what would you ask God? 'Why do I have three nipples?' Jessie is taken on a journey through time. As unfortunate circumstances occur, God just watches. Has God abandoned us? In the style of Edgar Allen Poe and Charles Dickens, The Concept will make you question the relevance of God(s) today.
Venue description: At the foot of the Royal Mile, Venue 13 has been bringing the best of emerging talent from the UK and the wider world to the Edinburgh Festival Fringe since 1996. With a real focus on theatre, but also contemporary dance and physical performance, Venue 13 prides itself on offering more than just simply fringe theatre. Audiences keep coming back for more to ‘this serene little venue’ ([i]Scotsman[/i]).
Venue accessibility: Full venue site is accessible, Lift level access to all areas, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. The pedestrian route available from the Royal Mile is wheelchair accessible

Title: Tidying Up with Emily Gravett
Teaser: Emily Gravett has twice won the prestigious Kate Greenaway Medal and it's no surprise given her vibrant drawings and charming characters. Here, she introduces her latest book Tidy, the story of Pete the badger who, in his quest to keep the forest tidy,...
Description: Emily Gravett has twice won the prestigious Kate Greenaway Medal and it's no surprise given her vibrant drawings and charming characters. Here, she introduces her latest book Tidy, the story of Pete the badger who, in his quest to keep the forest tidy, ends up almost destroying it entirely. Find out what happens when you meet this immensely talented author-illustrator.

Title: DIY Space Exploration
Teaser: Join us for an evening exploring the surprisingly reachable areas of space.
Description: A democratisation of space exploration underway! From Space X and Virgin Galactic to the Solar Impulse plane, private organisations have made many recent innovations and we’re now in an exciting era where individuals can 3D-print rocket parts and launch their own microsatellites. Join us for an evening exploring the surprisingly reachable areas of space with Dr Camilla Colombo, lecturer in spacecraft engineering at Southampton University, Tom Walkinshaw of QubeSat and Head of ESA’s Space Debris Office, Dr Holger Krag.

Title: Now We Are Sixty
Description: Maxine's turned 60. She's a bit bothered by this but mostly bewildered. Time’s speeding up so quickly that it now seems like bin day every day, and people have started to apologise if they swear in front of her. But she has started something new and is going for gold. This is Maxine's fourth Edinburgh show. She has been on BBC Radio 4 and RTE. 'Outstandingly funny' (Entertainment.ie). 'Audience loved it' (Buxton Review). 'Brilliant' (Northern Standard). 'Made me laugh a lot' (Jo Enright). 'Top 10 feminist fatales' (Chortle.co.uk). 'Her honesty worked for me' (Somerset County Gazette).
Venue description: A recent arrival to the Cowgate this is a bar, diner and nightclub with a strong Latin American flavor. With a dedicated upstairs function room for PBH Free Fringe comedy from 12noon and DJ clubnights from midnight. Over 18's only.
Venue accessibility: The venue is split over two levels, the ground floor is the main holding bar and restaurant, the performance room/stage is on the first floor level. There is wheelchair access and disability toilets in the main ground floor bar but no disabled persons access or facilities on the first floor performance areas. Title: Geoff Norcott: Conswervative
Description: A trade unionist's son who grew up on a council estate, Geoff Norcott is wondering how he ended up leaning to the right. A motley South London upbringing may be the root of his more provocative views in this brand new 'satirically incisive' (Scotsman) hour of stand-up. 'Norcott is an absolute tonic' **** (Telegraph). 'Master of anecdotal story-telling' **** (Edinburgh Festivals). 'Genuine iconoclast... more importantly he makes it funny' (Chortle.co.uk). Writing credits include Channel 4's Alternative Election, The Sarah Millican Television Programme, 8 Out of 10 Cats and The Now Show.
Artist: So Comedy by arrangement with Troika
Venue description: Situated at the heart of the festival, between George Square and Teviot Place, the Med Quad is where you can find venues Cow Barn, Ermintrude, Buttercup, Daisy and Clover, presenting theatre, musicals, comedy, cabaret and family shows early til late.

Title: Immortal
Description: Winter, 1944. Holland. Five young air bombers are trapped behind enemy lines, fighting for the life of their wounded engineer. But an unwanted visitor comes knocking. Do they cling to their comrade, or flee for their lives?
Venue description: Back after its phenomenally successful launch in 2015 with a brand new studio means Greenside @ Infirmary Street is BIGGER than ever! Three really is the magic number so say hello to the third and newest addition to the family - Greenside @ Infirmary Street!

Title: LoveHard: The House on the Hill
Description: A family, recently arrived from nearby America, are moving into a newly-acquired property in Scotland. Specifically rural Scotland. Specifically specifically remote rural Scotland. Rumours surround the mysterious mansion and its blood-drenched past, and the locals aren't keen on the new arrivals either. But all the Kings want is a nice, quiet, relatively murder-free area to settle down and forget the problems they've left behind. Will they find the eternal peace they're looking for? Will the house claim them for its own? And will remote rural Scotland ever lose its faint sheen of unnatural terror?
Venue description: A daily selection of free shows, comedy, theatre and cabaret, running as part of the Free Festival, with performances running all day from midday until midnight in this friendly venue, offering a wide range of drinks and food.

Title: Scottish Beasties with Kate McLelland
Teaser: Illustrator Kate McLelland's bestselling There Was a Wee Lassie Who Swallowed a Midgie featured a host of Scottish creatures, with a humorous twist on a much-loved rhyme. Now Kate's back with more colourful pictures, introducing wee ones to animals and...
Description: Illustrator Kate McLelland's bestselling There Was a Wee Lassie Who Swallowed a Midgie featured a host of Scottish creatures, with a humorous twist on a much-loved rhyme. Now Kate's back with more colourful pictures, introducing wee ones to animals and numbers in a uniquely Scottish way. Learn how to draw your favourite beastie in this interactive event. Tickets admit 1 child and 1 accompanying adult. Adult supervision recommended.

Title: Paul Duncan McGarrity – Ask an Archaeologist
Description: An experiment. An archaeologist sits in a room and answers your questions on any subject as honestly as possible. Could be rude, probably crude. Be prepared to talk candidly with the protection of context. 'Like a very tall, funny, excited child' (Scotsman). Photo credit comedysnapshot.
Venue description: The candle in the middle of two burning ends. A patchwork quilt of fair-trade coffees, 241 pizzas & magazines will get you through the day. It all begins to unravel again with a night-time tapestry of cocktails, craft beers and fine tunes - and a huge variety of free Fringe shows

Title: Wild about Wilder
Description: Journey through time, space and emotion in two selections from Thornton Wilder. Pullman Car Hiawatha, a one-act comedy, brings audiences to a Pullman car traveling from New York to Chicago in 1930 while it examines life and death. The Happy Journey joins a family on a drive to visit another family member… and the drama, laughter and love that takes place on the road.
Venue description: Rumoured to be the original fringe venue, this is one of the most talked about theatres in town, its unique atmosphere is known in fringe folklore. Here we present new and established work from across the globe. A full daily programme of cross-genre performance makes this wonderfully located venue a must for all. Show info. www.thespaceuk.com.

Title: Stuart MacBride
Subtitle: A Drop of the Hard Stuff
Teaser: With ten Logan McRae novels under his belt, Aberdonian crimewriter Stuart MacBride is firmly established as an international bestseller. In the Cold Dark Ground kicks off with the discovery of a maimed body in woodland not far from the Granite City, and...
Description: With ten Logan McRae novels under his belt, Aberdonian crimewriter Stuart MacBride is firmly established as an international bestseller. In the Cold Dark Ground kicks off with the discovery of a maimed body in woodland not far from the Granite City, and quickly lands McRae in an underworld trench war. Top drawer plotting and extreme brutality: this Scottish heavyweight’s on gruesomely good form.

Title: Beardyman: One Album Per Hour
Description: Total sell-out 2013, 2014 and 2015. Travelling at the speed of thought in his music production spaceship, the world-class multi award-winning musician and comedian transcends mere mimicry to produce studio-quality compositions faster than most could imagine them. The vocal shaman emits and manipulates any conceivable sound with a manic wit that will have you rocking with laughter and shaking your tail feather as a whole album is created live, based on your suggestions. 'An hour of dazzling skill... The bar for improv has been raised' **** (Chortle.co.uk). 'Breath-takingly talented' (Time Out).
Venue description: Soak up the legendary atmosphere at the Pleasance Courtyard, considered by many to be the heart of the Fringe. With every entertainment under the sun in seventeen venues, come take in a show, enjoy a drink and stay for the day. There's even the Kidzone for the little-ones! ‘The centre of the cultural universe' (Scotsman).
Venue accessibility: A full accessibility guide can be found at www.pleasance.co.uk. Title: Ada Campe in Cress!
Description: Experience Ada Campe's unique blend of comedy, magic, regret and shouting in a show that will surprise and entertain everyone – especially vegetarians. Ada Campe has delighted audiences in Stand Up for Women! at the Garrick Theatre and Wilton’s Music Hall, What The Frock! Comedy in Bristol and Femmes by the Thames at the Royal Vauxhall Tavern. She’s also very big in the shires. Verging on huge, actually. ‘Resembles an unhinged supervillain’ (Diva Magazine). ‘Extraordinary stage presence’ (John Fleming). ‘Talented and funny... Look out drag queens, the dowager duchess is in da house’ (Kate Copstick).
Venue description: Buzzing, unpretentious gay club over two levels with bars, dancefloor and regular cabaret nights. Open from 11am-3am. Every day during the fringe we host several, 5-star, PBH Free Fringe shows, bespoke cocktails and international beers. Kitchen open every day until 10pm. Children welcome before 9pm.
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site

Title: Blushed
Description: Loosely inspired by The Red Shoes: a compendium of bonkers and brilliant adult fairy tales told through tap dance. In turns anarchic, wonderful and wonky, these stories explore dated ideals through the eyes of modern-day adulthood. 'Humorous sketches, fun and frolics… Sole Rebel Tap are taking tap forward' (Rebecca Nice, TotalTheatre.org.uk). 'They've experimented with something new for tap. Title: Edinburgh Medal Address: Astronomy for a better world
Teaser: The 2016 Edinburgh Medal is jointly awarded to Kevin Govender and the International Astronomical Union (IAU), to recognise their wide reaching contribution to science
Description:
The 2016 Edinburgh Medal is jointly awarded to Kevin Govender and the International Astronomical Union (IAU), to recognise their wide reaching contribution to science. It is awarded jointly for the creation of, and practical establishment of, Astronomy for Development, which integrates the pursuit of scientific knowledge with social development for and with those most in need. The IAU is the international astronomical organisation that brings together almost 10,000 distinguished astronomers from all nations of the world. Its mission is to promote and safeguard the science of astronomy in all its aspects through international cooperation. Under the pioneering stewardship of Kevin Govender, the Office of Astronomy for Development has successfully harnessed astronomy in the service of education and capacity building in the developing world.

The Edinburgh Medal is a prestigious award given each year to men and women of science and technology whose professional achievements have made a significant contribution to the understanding and well-being of humanity.

Kevin will be appear in the Edinburgh Medal Address and will be joined by Sylvia Torres-Piembert, President of the International Astronomical Union, who will be accepting the Medal on its behalf.

The set is backed by superb musicians from the Scottish jazz scene: Fraser Urquhart (grand piano), Colin Steele (trumpet) and Jerry Forde (bass). From Cheek to Cheek and I Cover the Waterfront to Fever and Sunday Kind of Love, this show is not to be missed!
Venue: St Andrew's and St George's West, George St
Venue description: A beautiful, easily accessible 18th century New Town church, which hosts a variety of musical performances - from soloists to choirs, instrumentalists to small orchestras and bands in all musical genres: classical, folk, jazz, songs from the shows, opera, world music.  Enjoy light lunches and snacks in the Undercroft cafe, or sit and admire the newly refurbished building.

Title: Funny for a Grrrl
Description: We’ve selected the funniest women we could find at the Fringe and brought them together for an afternoon of comedy you’ll never forget! ‘An amazing evening of the most hilarious women I've seen in a very long time. When BBC producers say they can't find any funny women they obviously haven't been looking hard enough’ (Evening Herald, Dublin). ‘A fascinating range of different comedic styles. Even Christopher Hitchens would find these women funny’ (GQ). ‘Our girls are clean and won't rush you’ (Watford Gazette).

The giant 140 capacity yurt, an original tented structure from Eastern Europe is sure to surprise and delight! Food, drink, The Famous Spiegeltent and free music stage on site too.

Title: Geometric Embroidery
Teaser: Get hands-on making complex geometric shapes with a few simple steps!
Description: Find out how to make complex geometric shapes by following a few simple steps with maker and maths enthusiast Jessica Stanley. Embroider your own piece of 2D geometry to take home with you - no sewing experience needed.

Title: Along the Silk Road: Songs, Soldiers and Legends
Description: A mix of ancient music, legends and history as this troupe of 80 young performers recreate the excitement of an ancient imperial parade during the reign of Emperor Qin, almost 1,300 years ago. This snapshot of the most prosperous country on Earth at the time features dancers in traditional military costumes, stories about the legendary Eight Immortals and tales of the Silk Road. Discover traditional Chinese melodies and instruments such as the erhu, pipa and sheng.
Artist: Young Cultural Ambassadors from Affiliated Primary School of Tsinghua University
Venue description: Acoustic Music Centre @ St Bride's is approx 5 - 10 minutes' walk from the important Haymarket road and rail interchange.

Title: The Notorious Mary Bourke
Description: This is an Irish housewife's guide to life, love and hip hop. If you've ever wondered what happened when I met Tupac Shakur in Dublin, or why Jay Z is the worst thing to happen to East Coast hip hop – or how to live your life with the super confidence of Biggie Smalls – then this is the show for you. I'm an OG and I'm here to help, cause let's face it, sometimes bitches be trippin'. ‘One of the best female acts in the country’ (GQ). ‘The audience loved her’ (Independent).
Warnings: All seating is unreserved and latecomers may not be admitted.
Venue description: Stand 5 and Stand 6 are located at The Place – a luxury four-star boutique townhouse hotel, situated in a stunning A-listed Georgian terrace in the very heart of Edinburgh's New Town. Stand 5 & 6 offer comfort, space, a roof terrace bar and complimentary WiFi. The venue also boosts a stylish restaurant and opulent cocktail bar. Catch another sensational comedy line-up from The Stand family here!

Title: Michelle Brasier: Space Tortoise
Description: Michelle Brasier (Backwards Anorak’s Winter is Coming, Aunty Donna’s 1999) presents Space Tortoise. In 1968 the Soviet Union sent the first tortoise into deep space. That tortoise was my daddy. I’ll sing about it. You’re invited on the heart-warming intergalactic journey of a tortoise working in retail with big dreams and an even bigger voice. ***** (Funny Tonne, AU). 'Artfully awkward comedy… ridiculously fun' (Music, AU). 'Powerhouse vocals... utterly mesmerised from start to finish' (RipItUp.com.au).
Venue description: An exciting, vibrant, neo-gothic mini-castle housing nine performance spaces and seven bars including the exclusive roof top bar, The Loft. A must for all Fringe-goers. A massive mini-Fringe under one roof, this iconic venue has spawned the best of the best on the Fringe! All spaces, the café and all seven bars are wheelchair accessible, with the exception of the Balcony and Billiard Rooms. Tickets available 24-hours online!

Artist: George Wilson (Organ), Adam Wilson (Cello), Tom Wilson (Violin)

Title: Gospel World
Description: Cillis – short for St. Cecilia Church – Gospel Choir, directed by Scotsman Brian Hamilton, comes from just outside Munich, Bavaria. Our aim is to perform every song with the maximum possible musicality and passion. Our programme includes many old favourites – Down by the Riverside, He's Got the Whole World, When the Saints, Amazing Grace and more – in imaginative choral arrangements, together with a selection of the best contemporary gospels, sung a capella or with piano accompaniment. Come and experience this talented German choir's artistry and enthusiasm. You won't regret it – goosebumps guaranteed!
Venue description: Fringe venue number 60.

Title: Superwomen of Science – Minerva Scientifica
Description: Ada Lovelace, computing, Caroline Herschel, comets, Mary Sommerville, mathematics, Jocelyn Bell-Burnell, pulsars, Anne McLaren, genetics, Eva Crane, bees. Theatrical virtuosa, Frances M Lynch, sings spectacular stories. Music by Handel, Hildegard, Frances-Hoad, Plowman, Thompson, Whitley, Wimhurst.
Venue description: Festival Fringe productions in The Little Theatre 'beyond the treasure house of salamis, cheeses, balsamic vinegars and olive oils' ([i]Sunday Times[/i]). 'If anything makes a London-based gourmet jealous of the Scots, it is Valvona & Crolla' ([i]Financial Times[/i]).

Title: Lady Shakespeare
Description: The splendour of the Elizabethan theatre also has its shadows and mysteries. Queen Elizabeth knows them very well. She knows its ins and outs better than we think. The famous bard, known throughout history and around the world, William Shakespeare, created many relevant female characters who usually remain hidden behind the curtains. This show brings them to the fore, to the front-line of war, as characters who are prepared to discover one of the greatest secrets of our culture: the true identity of William Shakespeare.
Venue description: Paradise Green is the heart and soul of the largest arts festival in the world, presenting a wide range of top-quality performances. Title: Astonish Me! – Jeux
Description: Sergei Diaghilev's challenge to all of his collaborating artists was: ‘Astonish me!’. In May 1913, this demand brought into being two astounding works – Stravinsky's Rite of Spring and Jeux, Debussy's last orchestral masterpiece. Premiered at the Edinburgh Jazz Festival 2016, Patrick's reinterpretation of Jeux straddles jazz and contemporary music landscapes, faithfully capturing Debussy's ethereal sound world. This outstanding octet is joined by Mark Lotz on piccolo/flute and Max Grosch on violin. ‘A world-class ensemble, completely at ease with each other’ **** (BroadwayBaby.com). Commissioned by Edinburgh Jazz Festival, through the Scottish Government’s Edinburgh Festivals Expo Fund.
Venue description: This stylish basement bar is Edinburgh's coolest, multiple award-winning, year-round live music venue, with a crammed daily programme of multi-genre music and Fringe shows running all day, every day, from 13:00-05:00. As well as all the independent Fringe shows hosted by the venue, you’ll hear the bar’s own programme of excellent music, with great jazz, funk, acoustic, blues and rocky sounds – and bar service to 05:00 nightly!

Title: La Traviata
Description: Scotland's Opera Bohemia returns to the Fringe for its seventh year with one of the world’s most loved operas, La Traviata. Verdi's masterpiece tells the tale of the famous courtesan Violetta, who commits the cardinal sin of falling in love. Scottish favourite Catriona Clark and Thomas Kinch lead a star cast of some of Scotland’s finest home-grown talent, including Aaron McAuley's company debut in the role of Germont, and star of Gianni Schicchi Andrew McTaggart as Baron Douphol. Including the famous Brindisi and Sempre Libera, this intimate and gripping new production is not to be missed.
Warnings: Sung in Italian with English subtitles
Venue description: St Cuthbert's is at the very heart of Edinburgh on Lothian Road near the junction with Princes Street (opposite the Caledonian Hotel), adjacent to public transport and Castle Terrace car park. It has two superb performance spaces and fine acoustics.

Title: Simon Callow
Subtitle: Orson Welles at 100
Teaser: Not just a great actor, Simon Callow has now also shown that he is a gifted biographer. In One-Man Band, the third volume of his biography of Orson Welles, Callow skilfully charts the later years of Welles’ life, painting a vivid and often very funny...
Description: Not just a great actor, Simon Callow has now also shown that he is a gifted biographer. In One-Man Band, the third volume of his biography of Orson Welles, Callow skilfully charts the later years of Welles’ life, painting a vivid and often very funny portrait of a troubled genius enduring a cocktail of triumph and decline. Today Callow reveals an actor’s insights into a highly complex artist.

Title: Stories from Mexico and Panama
Description: With his double cultural background, storyteller Rubén Corbett treats you to stories from both Central American countries. Venture into pivotal places in world geography which have spawned huge imaginative energies. Bilingual support by storyteller Laura Escuela.

Title: Europe
Subtitle: Shifting Borders, Itinerant Lives
Teaser: In 1994, Philip Howard directed Europe at the Traverse, a breakthrough production for playwright David Greig. Howard and Greig both went on to enjoy stellar careers, and the play itself remains remarkably relevant. A response to the civil war in the...
Description: In 1994, Philip Howard directed Europe at the Traverse, a breakthrough production for playwright David Greig. Howard and Greig both went on to enjoy stellar careers, and the play itself remains remarkably relevant. A response to the civil war in the Balkans, Greig’s script features two refugees hoping to take a train. Although originally a commentary on the decline of communism, Europe still resonates powerfully today thanks to its meditation on the plight of refugees and their need to put down roots. Philip Howard returns to direct a rehearsed reading featuring nine actors for this special Book Festival event.

Title: Perhaps Hope
Description: Welcome to a brave new world of hope beyond devastation. Rockie Stone (Circa, Circus Oz) and Vincent van Berkel (Knee Deep, Circus Oz) explore the stark reality of climate change in this breathtakingly honest eco-apocalyptic circus show. Examine the humanity behind the masses and the thinly veiled beauty hiding beneath the ugliness. This humorous, delicate and tension filled work will leave you with a renewed optimism, and perhaps hope… ‘Enchanting, entrancing and at times breath holdingly, heart stoppingly brilliant’ **** (Advertiser, Adelaide). ‘Circus at its most polished and poignant’ (Theatre Press). Winner: Original New Circus, Melbourne Fringe 2015.
Venue: Underbelly’s Circus Hub on the Meadows
Venue description: Circus Hub is back on the Meadows celebrating spectacular circus. Visit Circus Hub for two dazzling circus tents – Lafayette and Beauty – and a charming bar for ticket and pass-holders.

Title: Stand Up & Slam!
Description: Stand-up comedy: poetry’s idiot relation, right? Performance poetry: comedy’s boring cousin, yes? Let's find out. Six phenomenal acts go head-to-head for your approval as poetry and comedy collide with hilarious results! Our resident team captains are joined by the most exciting comedians and poets from around the UK. 'A complete and utter winner' (TheReviewsHub.com). 'I have not laughed this hard in a very long time. Inspired' (Latest). 'Ever evolving... have multiple viewings on different days' (EdFestMag.com).
Venue: Just the Tonic at The Mash House
Venue description: Fringe Venue number 288

Title: The Great Scottish Make Off
Description: A week of arts and crafts events: an interactive art event unlike any other. Watch artists make with limited time, materials tools – the ultimate product is limited only by imagination. Each of our selected artists will get 4 hours to create a unique art piece. Each day artists will work on their creations using materials sourced from local art shops, scrap yards, donations, and sponsors. Watch for free, or participate in a variety hands-on workshops with artists that start from £5. Full programme at cthefestival.com/strands/great-scottish-make-off
Venue description: C south is a Festival oasis in the heart of the Southside, close to the Meadows, University and other venues. The unique set of indoor and outdoor performance spaces includes church, black box theatre, black box tent, found space studios, expansive gardens. C south is part of the C venues curated programme taking place in over twenty performance spaces at multiple city-centre venues in our 26th year at the Fringe.

Title: Adventures of the Singing Acupuncturist Five: Big O Conquers the FOMO – Free
Description: Spread your wings of courage and join Big O as she explores the aspects of fear. Through storytelling, songs and comedy, she provides new insights into the FOMO: fear of missing out. What’s holding you back from accomplishing your dreams? Big O provides some secret solutions for a renewed spirit. Create a shield, piercing through darkness and into the light. Nothing will get in the way of your dreams! Another world premiere, this marks her 5th Edinburgh Festival Fringe show. For more info: oliviarhee.tumblr.com.
Venue description: Situated on the bustling city centre street, at the foot of Edinburgh Castle sandwiched between the stylish West-end district and the ever popular Bruntsfield. Moriarty‘s is a place where you can relax in stylish yet homely surroundings. The carefully refurbished bar has a Sherlock Holmes theme upstairs with our focus on Craft Beers, World Lagers and Malt Whisky.

Title: Glyndebourne: Don Pasquale
Description:
Cinema screening of live performance.
One of the reasons why Donizetti's Don Pasquale is regarded as a cornerstone of the Italian comic opera tradition is because its characters are no mere commedia dell'arte stereotypes, but complex, vulnerable human beings. This is brought to the fore in Mariame Clément's sensitive and perceptive production, hailed by the Financial Times as 'a Glyndebourne classic'. Acclaimed buffo baritone Alessandro Corbelli sings the title role 'with just the right degree of lugubriousness', while Danielle de Niese, one of today's most sought-after sopranos, is an 'engaging' and 'irresistible' Norina (Telegraph).
Venue description:

Title: Fin Taylor: Whitey McWhiteface
Description: Taylor the 'filth maestro' (Time Out) takes on the ickiest thing there is! Being white. Set 'potential for backfire' to maximum. Taylor follows up last year's show Stink, which the Scotsman called 'the punchiest, densest, most wide-ranging hour of stand-up at the Fringe', with an hour that's just about one thing. 'A brilliant analysis of white privilege... masterful stand-up' (Scotsman). 'Says Honky and Cracker more than Reg D Hunter in his prime' (List). Fin has supported Doc Brown on tour, gigged with Louis CK in New York, and made multiple appearances on Josh Widdicombe's XFM show.

Title: Greater Belfast
Description: A gig like no other; these are songs for a city growing greater and greater. Little King blends poetic storytelling with powerful contemporary composition for string quartet to paint a moving portrait of a city still aching from the violence of its recent past. This is the patter and slang of Belfast, the caustic black humour of Belfast, all bent together into words and music that cut through the sleech and speak to the heart.

Directed by Lee Griffiths of Late Night Gimp Fight (Chortle Award for Best Character of Sketch Act). By Sasha Ellen and Daniel Collard. Daniel's audio play, Dark Shadows: Tainted Love was produced by Big Finish Productions. He can be seen in CBC's X Company. The competition is run by three unconventional adults who, with the children, have their own unique stories to tell. From the production team that brought you I Love You, You’re Perfect, Now Change ***** (ThePublicReviews.com), Four Wheeled Theatre presents this hilarious and heart-warming show which tackles the anxieties of being a teenager, the complexity of family, and a need to succeed. So get your thinking caps on, and remember, 'Can I have a definition please?'.

Description: Phoenix Nights meets The Sopranos. One night in London’s legendary 90s club, The Tardis. If you were there you wouldn't remember anyway… George is facing closure unless he pays the mother of all rent demands. Fortunately, The Tardis is having the party of the year tonight. Title: Celebrating Kevin Govender and the International Astronomical Union
Teaser: Come and view an exhibition celebrating the work of Kevin Govender and the International Astronomical Union.
Description: Under the pioneering stewardship of Kevin Govender, the Office of Astronomy for Development has successfully harnessed astronomy in the service of education and capacity building in the developing world. The 2016 Edinburgh Medal has jointly been awarded to the International Astronomical Union and Kevin Govender for the creation and practical establishment of Astronomy for Development, which integrates the pursuit of scientific knowledge with social development for and with those most in need. Come and view an exhibition celebrating the work of Kevin Govender and the International Astronomical Union.

Title: Vadim Levental & Agustín Fernández Mallo
Subtitle: Novels that Inspire Novelists
Teaser: Continuing our commitment to groundbreaking literature in translation, we welcome Vadim Levental, a vastly talented Russian novelist whose compelling debut, Masha Regina, centres around a woman in St Petersburg who takes the European film scene by...

One of Spain's most celebrated writers, Agustín Fernández Mallo presents the highly inventive Nocilla Dream, a daring and influential experiment which spawned the ‘Nocilla Generation’ of Spanish writers.

Title: Stand Up and Spit
Subtitle: Potent Words with Purpose
Teaser: Back in the 80s, the ranting poets ruled the alternative cabaret scene. Today we welcome the most famous of the lot, Attila the Stockbroker, still raging 35 years on. Tim Wells, who was also there with his chippy verses, has created an online history of...
Description: Back in the 80s, the ranting poets ruled the alternative cabaret scene. Today we welcome the most famous of the lot, Attila the Stockbroker, still raging 35 years on. Tim Wells, who was also there with his chippy verses, has created an online history of the scene, Stand Up and Spit. Two modern day spitters join them: Bridget Minamore and Luke Wright, who deploy poetry to kick back at the world. Expect sharp debate and snarling verse.

Title: Programme Your Own Lego Robot
Description: This practical workshop will see you use Lego software to programme a robot, You will use basic coding skills, write algorithms, learn how to debug, use variables and solve lots of problems! This workshop session is designed to be hands-on, to encourage collaborative working and to be lots of fun! You can expect: a hands-on experience; to learn how to use programming software to work individually and in small groups. This workshop is suitable for people aged 12+ and building or programming experience is not required. Find out more at www.edef.co.uk
