Title: Mitch Benn: Don't Fear the Reaper
Description: It's been a morbid year for 'the country's leading musical satirist' (Times), he's turned 46 – over the hill by anyone's standards – his personal life is in turmoil and his childhood heroes are dropping like flies. At times like these, a man feels the Reaper creeping up on him… But is death anything to fear? And is it really the end? (Yes. Yes it is, sorry!) Mitch confronts his – and your – mortality with hilarious (and tuneful) consequences. Join him! It's an hour of your life you're not getting back!
Warnings: All Seating is unreserved. Latecomers may not be admitted.
Venue description: Stand 5 and Stand 6 are located at The Place – a luxury four-star boutique townhouse hotel, situated in a stunning A-listed Georgian terrace in the very heart of Edinburgh's New Town. Stand 5 & 6 offer comfort, space, a roof terrace bar and complimentary WiFi. The venue also boosts a stylish restaurant and opulent cocktail bar. Catch another sensational comedy line-up from The Stand family here!
Venue accessibility:
Limited access to some parts of venue site, Some areas not reachable by lift or level access, No wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, On street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. Partial level access from Stand 6 to the bar and Stand 5 to the Courtyard. 
For Stand 6, the only wheelchair access is through the hotel service door on Dublin Street Lane. This is only for access downstairs – no access to the Stand 5, the hotel main bar,  lounges or terrace without having to climb stairs. For Stand 5, wheelchair access best though the main door of The Place Hotel (2 wide steps) – through the bar area - out to the courtyard (1 step from the bar door and 9 wide steps down into the courtyard). The door to stand 5 is accessible through the courtyard. Stand 5 is also accessible from Dublin Street Lane and has 12 steps with a 90 degree turn. Please make contact with the venue box office for approval. Regretfully, staff are unable to assist electric wheelchairs.

Title: Condemned
Description: New late night tour experience offering a unique insight into Edinburgh's tumultuous yet fascinating past with witches and witchcraft, telling stories of its infamous accomplices and most ardent opponents. For centuries we have been fascinated by the other side but paradoxically afraid of what may be beyond. The lives of those who have cavorted with the devil are often cut short or hidden in the shadows and mystery has engulfed their stories... until now! This dramatic interpretation will challenge perceptions and go beyond what we believe to be true. Will you dare cross the threshold and confront the unknown?
Venue description: A unique underground street buried deep beneath Edinburgh's Royal Mile frozen in time since the 17th century. In the company of a guide you can explore the site and experience what it was like to live, work and die here. An unmissable, award-winning five-star visitor attraction. Shop and cafe open daily.
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site, Some areas not reachable by lift or level access, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. The site is underground with uneven surfaces and steep inclines and steps. Wheelchair access is not possible

Title: Poisons
Teaser: Discover the poisons that were once found on pharmacy shelves and learn about their effects on the body.
Description: Paracelsus wrote, "All things are poisons, for there is nothing without poisonous qualities. It is only the dose which makes a thing poison." Many compounds we now consider to be poisons were once found on pharmacy shelves. Before the twentieth century people often got better in spite of their doctor rather than because of them. This talk examines four former medicines, their effects on the body and some killer case studies.
Genre tags: Being Human,Human Biology,Health & Diseases,History of Science

Title: Seann Walsh: One for the Road
Description: The Lie-in King returns. All-new show from the star of BBC's Live at the Apollo, E4's Virtually Famous and ITV's Play to the Whistle. 'Unquestionably the best observational comic of his generation' (Guardian).
Warnings: May contain strong language
Venue description: Soak up the legendary atmosphere at the Pleasance Courtyard, considered by many to be the heart of the Fringe. With every entertainment under the sun in seventeen venues, come take in a show, enjoy a drink and stay for the day. There's even the Kidzone for the little-ones! ‘The centre of the cultural universe' (Scotsman).
Venue accessibility: A full accessibility guide can be found at www.pleasance.co.uk. Full venue site is accessible, Lift level access to all areas, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. The Pleasance Courtyard is located uphill when accessing the venue from Cowgate. The outdoor spaces of the venue are a mix of cobblestones and tarmacked surfaces

Title: EVENT CANCELLATION - Updates From Space with Jean-Francois Clervoy
Teaser: Meet one of Europe’s most experienced space explorers to get an insight into life as an astronaut
Description:
Join one of Europe’s most decorated space explorers to get an insight into life as an astronaut. European Space Agency’s (ESA) Jean-Francois Clervoy will share his experiences and highlights of a career involving 675 hours of space flight. He will be joined by guests from the UK Space
Agency to update on Tim Peake’s Principia Mission to the International Space Station.

Jean-Francois flew three times on the Space Shuttle. His missions included repairing the Hubble space telescope and undertaking a wide range of science experiments. In his current role Jean-Francois provides support to the human spaceflight programme and closely followed
British ESA astronaut Tim Peake as he trained for his current Principia Mission. Tim blasted off from Earth to join the ISS on 15 December 2015 and the panel will be able to share the latest news on Tim’s mission as well as giving a unique viewpoint on the challenges and opportunities of
human spaceflight.

Title: Black Box Shorts 3: Rituals of Transformation and Discovery
Description:
This programme consists of five films that take quite different approaches to the theme of ritual, offering the viewer an insight into practices of physical and spiritual transformation. From the masked monkeys of Indonesia to matrilineal tribes in China and Panama, and from documentary to animation, these films bring together the strange and the familiar, the real and the surreal. They demonstrate in profound and moving ways how looking outwards towards the other involves looking inwards towards the self. [PG]
Anóme Lena Ditte Nissen/Germany, Panama, China/2015/13 min
The Masked Monkeys Anja Dornieden, Juan David González Monroy/Germany, Indonesia/2015/30 min
Noevus Samuel Yal/France/2016/8 min
A Subsequent Fulfilment of a Pre-Historic Wish Johannes Gierlinger/Austria/2015/9 min
Toré João Vieira Torres, Tanawi Xucuru Kariri/Brazil, France/2015/15 min
 
*Please note there is a strobe warning for these screenings.

Title: Snug as a Bug?
Description: Storyteller Rosie Mapplebeck lives in a nature garden where she makes new homes for tiny creatures. Share stories of her animal, bird and bee friends and make a beastie bed-box, in Leith’s renowned crofting garden, on the west side of the Links.

Title: The Stoats Loony Dook
Description: Welcome 2017 with a splash by taking part in the breath-taking Loony Dook at South Queensferry for 30 years thousands of Dookers have taken part in the annual dip in the freezing River Forth in the shadow of the world-famous Forth Bridges.
Venue accessibility: Y

Title: David Ashton
Subtitle: Murder in the Bawdy-Hoose
Teaser: Fans of David Ashton’s BBC Radio 4 drama (and his Inspector McLevy novels) will already know Jean Brash. She’s the actor-turned-writer’s counterpoint to McLevy and in Mistress of the Just Land she gets a novel that’s entirely her own. As the...
Description: Fans of David Ashton’s BBC Radio 4 drama (and his Inspector McLevy novels) will already know Jean Brash. She’s the actor-turned-writer’s counterpoint to McLevy and in Mistress of the Just Land she gets a novel that’s entirely her own. As the boss of Edinburgh’s finest brothel, she finally has a case to solve – and it’s a violent murder that’s taken place in her own house of pleasure.

Title: Aaaaargh! It's 101 Naughty Jokes in 30 Minutes – Free Show
Description: Award-winning gag merchant and UK Pun Champion 2016, Masai Graham delivers over 100 naughty jokes in just half an hour. Expect puns, one-liners and wordplay in this 3.3 laughs per minute bonanza. ‘Annoyingly good' (Gary Delaney, Mock the Week). ‘Flashes of proper genius’ (Chortle.co.uk). Dave's top 10 jokes of the Edinburgh Festival Fringe 2014 and 2015.
Venue description: An Irish bar with a difference.... we're actually Irish! Located just off Edinburgh's famous Grassmarket, Dropkick Murphy's gives you a real experience of what an Irish bar is meant to be. Live music at night, showing major sports on our big screens, and all out great craic assured - and we have free shows here through the Fringe from midday to 10pm, with the bar open until very late afterwards!
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site, Some areas not reachable by lift or level access, No wheelchair accessible toilet

Title: Blank
Description: Known for plays without directors, sets and rehearsals, the acclaimed Iranian playwright Nassim Soleimanpour takes it to extremes in his new play Blank. Each night the gap riddled script is to be completed by a new performer and a live audience. The play becomes a story machine to share the life story of the playwright, the performer and a random audience member. Blank celebrates the communal and elusive nature of theatre as audience members shout, laugh, gasp and collaborate to write the evening’s story, a story that will never be told in the same way ever again.
Venue description: Uniquely within Edinburgh's former Royal (Dick) Veterinary College, Summerhall presents high quality, engaging, challenging and exhilarating theatre, music, dance, visual arts for people of all ages. Our busy bar restaurant and cafe offers a wonderful selection of food and drink; the courtyard an epicentre of al fresco bars and street food. Not all of our shows are listed here. The entire programme of performance and visual arts is at www.summerhall.co.uk
Venue accessibility:
We are committed to making your visit to Summerhall an enjoyable experience and we are working to make our venue as accessible as possible. The building is B-listed and is over one hundred years old and not all of our spaces are fully accessible. 

Our step free access is through the side entrance on Summerhall Square. The Royal Dick Bar and Restaurant is situated to your right as you come in (with a ramp at the rear of the bar) and there is a ramp directly ahead of you that leads to the Reception, Box Office, Shop and Café.
We have lift access to some of the First Floor spaces. Further information about individual spaces and shows can be obtained from the Box Office. If you would like more information about the accessibility of particular shows, or if you wish to arrange a familiarisation tour of the venue prior to the festival, please do not hesitate to contact us by phone on 0845 874 3000 or by email on info@summerhall.co.uk

Our staff are here to help and if there is anything you need assistance with please do not hesitate to ask.

http://www.summerhall.co.uk/about/accessibility/. Limited access to some parts of venue site, Some areas not reachable by lift or level access, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, On street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. Ramp access is at the side of the venue on Summerhall Square.

Code: Second Sight: Seeing in Highland Tradition
Title: Second Sight: Seeing in Highland Tradition
Description: Storyteller and tradition bearer George Macpherson of Glendale in Skye explores the phenomena of super-sensory “seeing” in the Gaelic traditions of the Highlands and Islands. Are they connected with older Druidic beliefs and if so, how has it been expressed in more recent times? George’s new book, The Old Grey Magician, digs into related unique material surviving in oral culture.

Title: Janet Ellis & Lorna Gibb
Subtitle: Dangerous Heroines
Teaser: Two debut novels whose lead characters will entrance, unnerve and delight. Evoking the blood, filth and beauty of Georgian London, Janet Ellis’ The Butcher’s Hook introduces us to young Anne Jaccob who embarks on a passionate love affair with...
Description: Two debut novels whose lead characters will entrance, unnerve and delight. Evoking the blood, filth and beauty of Georgian London, Janet Ellis’ The Butcher’s Hook introduces us to young Anne Jaccob who embarks on a passionate love affair with shocking consequences. In A Ghost’s Story, Lorna Gibb tells the story of Katie King's life and afterlife. From Victorian Scotland to the present day, she haunts all she meets. Chaired by Jenny Brown.

Title: The Tempest: A New Kind of Wonder
Description: The Royal Shakespeare Company and Intel are collaborating to use the latest digital technology to bring to life Shakespeare’s The Tempest for a new generation. Along with a demonstration of motion capture technology by The Imaginarium Studios, the panel will discuss the innovation and experimentation involved in creating the supernatural elements of the play onstage.
Artist: In collaboration with Intel and in association with The Imaginarium
Venue description:
The iconic Assembly Rooms building is at the heart of Edinburgh's New Town. In 2016 the Assembly Rooms play host venue to the inaugural Edinburgh Digital Entertainment Festival which will be showcasing
the best recordings of live arts events in a world class Cinema as well as presenting the best in new technological developments across the sector through a series of stands, talks, workshops and live presentations.
Venue accessibility: Full venue site is accessible, Lift level access to all areas, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, On street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas

Title: #TheSoloFilter: Researching Re-authorship
Description: Part of the Fringe Central Events Programme, for Fringe participants. Ever left a performance discussing what you would have done differently? #TheSoloFilter is an opportunity to remake a performance into the piece you wish you had seen. Since 2013, #TheSoloFilter has grown as a model of creative development, audience engagement and challenging the way we discuss performance. But what is the benefit of exercising your opinions? Emma Jayne Park will present the research, its background and illustrate #TheSoloFilter in action.
Warnings: You may be asked to show your Fringe Participant pass on entry.
Venue description: Fringe Central is a resource developed specifically for Fringe participants. A hub for professional and creative development opportunities and home to our Arts Industry, Media and Venues and Companies offices, you will find support and advice as well as a programme of over 100 free events all designed to help you make the most out of your Fringe experience.
Venue accessibility: Full venue site is accessible, Lift level access to all areas, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, On street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas

Title: Cinderella
Description: Cinderella wants a night at the ball, Buttons wants Cinderella to notice him and the Ugly Sisters want Cinderella to just stay in her cupboard! Welcome our Fairy Godmother and hey presto we have a magical pantomime at Paradise Green! Come along with us to the ball, and see whether Cinderella will live happily ever after with Prince Charming. Or will the Ugly Sisters’ cabaret act just blow him away? Jam-packed with catchy tunes and corny jokes, thigh-slapping fun for all the family! A must watch!
Venue description: Paradise Green is the heart and soul of the largest arts festival in the world, presenting a wide range of top-quality performances. Visit our beautiful and friendly venue, relax with a drink from our snack bar before your performance and soak up the true atmosphere of the Fringe.
Venue accessibility: Full venue site is accessible, Lift level access to all areas, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas

Title: Sticky Notes
Description: Scottish actress Rose Leslie (Game of Thrones) shines in this impressive comedy/drama, as a struggling dancer trying to hit the big-time in Los Angeles. She gives it all up to care for her ill father Jack (Ray Liotta) in Florida but when the chance of a lifetime comes up she feels she cannot pass up the opportunity. This attractively staged film dwells on the tough – and often tender and funny – nature of father/daughter relationships, with a strong cast also featuring Justin Bartha and Gina Rodriguez. [12A]

Title: Claude Bourbon: Medieval and Spanish Blues – Guitar and Songs
Description: Not a same ol' same ol' gig! Ready for a unique and talented take on a wide range of musical traditions? Bourbon is known throughout Europe and America for amazing guitar performances that take blues, Spanish, Middle-Eastern, and Russian styling into uncharted territories. Experience an evening of exploration in the unique ambiance of the Thumb! 'Never heard anyone get that much beautiful sound out of a J-45' (Bob, Tucson). 'A breathtaking acoustic fusion of blues, jazz, folk, classical and Spanish guitar from a stunning guitar virtuoso.' (Altadena News, USA). www.claudebourbon.org
Venue description: Acoustic Music Centre @ St Bride's is approx 5 - 10 minutes' walk from the important Haymarket road and rail interchange.
Venue accessibility: Induction loop in Big Room and in venue box office but not in Back Room. Limited access to some parts of venue site, Some areas not reachable by lift or level access, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, On street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. Very close to several bus routes

Title: Made in Cumbria
Description: Jane Postlethwaite brings her debut solo show, Made in Cumbria, to the Edinburgh Fringe, where she will introduce you to a selection of dark female characters who will welcome you into their unique world. Jane Postlethwaite is a Funny Women finalist 2015 and Brighton Comedy Festival Squawker Award finalist 2015. ‘Surprisingly dark Cumbrian observational commentary’ (Latest 7). ‘Bloody brilliant. Loneliness and breakdown has never been funnier!’ (Julian Caddy, managing director at Brighton Fringe). ‘Fascinating and compelling. A wonderfully entertaining experience’ (FringeReview.co.uk).
Venue description: Step away from the herd and enjoy the best programme at the Festival in this haven of calm and comfort just along from the Cowgate. Featuring shows of all genres from around the world, a trendy bar, posh loos and ... glorious air-conditioning.
Venue accessibility: Full venue site is accessible, Lift level access to all areas, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, On street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas

Title: Concert in the Gardens
Description:
Welcome the New Year in spectacular style with a sound and visual feast from the world class singer songwriter Paolo Nutini! Ring in the New Year to the sounds of Paolo and bask in the glow of our spectacular fireworks display from Edinburgh Castle, this truly is the best view in the house! 

Tickets General Release: 30th September 2016 at 10am

Previous headliners include Biffy Clyro, Pet Shop Boys, Lily Allen, Primal Scream, Kasabian, and Blondie.
Venue accessibility: Y

Title: Viva
Description: The colourful and vivid community of Havana’s drag clubs is the striking heart of Irish director Paddy Breathnach’s acclaimed film, which stars Hector Median as willowy teenager and would-be drag artist Jesus who attempts to build a relationship with his former boxer father Angel (Jorge Perugorria), freshly released from prison and finding it rather hard to deal with his son’s world. A deliciously atmospheric film, beautifully cast and brimming with emotion. [12A]

Title: Glasgow Girls
Description: Cora Bissett and David Greig's life-affirming, song filled Scottish drama, based on the true story of seven feisty teenagers whose lives change forever when their school friend and her asylum-seeking family are forcibly taken from their home to be deported. They are galvanised to fight for her life, taking on the government and succeeding where others failed, capturing the imagination of the media and inspiring a whole community to unite behind its residents. Smash-hit 2012. 'The most politically engaged and enraged British musical since Blood Brothers' ***** (Express). 'True raw power' **** (Metro). 'Awe inspiring' (Time Out). www.madeinscotlandshowcase.com.
Warnings: Strobe lighting. Strong language.
Artist: Pachamama Productions, National Theatre of Scotland and Regular Music
Venue description: The magnificent venue atop the Mound is the most prestigious venue on the Fringe and hosts the finest drama, music and comedy. Entrance and box office through New College Quad off Mound Place. The venue houses three spaces; the Main Hall, Rainy Hall and Baillie Room.
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site, Some areas not reachable by lift or level access, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. Assembly Hall is on Mound Place up a steep hill. Box Office and Bar has step free access, but there is a large steep flight of steps up to the venues from this entrance. Baillie Room is not accessible, but the Main Hall and Rainy Hall have wheelchair access via a rear entrance on Lawn Market - please arrange access in advance and arrive a full 30 minutes before show time if wheelchair or step free access to either Main Hall or Rainy Hall is required. Call 07864639321 for assistant venue

Title: Mike Newall: High on Gravy
Description: From male grooming to rodents, Mike has it all covered in this eclectic hour of stand-up comedy. Join Mike as he gives you an off-kilter perspective on his world. Please note that this show does not contain gravy. ‘Well-crafted jokes, great call-backs and a wonderfully dry delivery’ (ThreeWeeks). ‘There’s something strangely elegiac about these modest little insights into his life that make them more than just average observational comedy... Impressive stuff’ (Chortle.co.uk).
Warnings: Buy a ticket in advance to guarantee entry or Pay What You Want at the venue.
Venue: Just the Tonic at The Mash House
Venue description: Fringe Venue number 288

Title: Puzzle
Description: How does the world look to a small child? Is it round or angular, yellow or blue? Or maybe oblong, green, hollow and soft? Renowned Lithuanian choreographer Birute Baneviciute pieces together a puzzle from these coloured shapes in an absorbing performance exploring a child’s developmental stages. Dancers crawl, bounce, walk and run as they traverse a delightful world filled with vibrant costumes and gorgeous scenery which is assembled into an array of familiar forms, from geometric shapes to fruit and flowers. Accompanied by music composed especially for little ones, this is a gentle and joyous dance performance for babies.
Venue description: ZOO's award-winning, intimate studio theatres host a feast of the best new writing, emerging dance companies, and breathtaking physical theatre from around the world. Just down the road from the Pleasance Courtyard.
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site, Some areas not reachable by lift or level access, No wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, On street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas

Title: The Mathematics of Why I Don't Have a Boyfriend
Teaser: An introduction to randomness of romance, using statistics, signal processing and the novels of Jane Austen.
Description: Are you single? Losing hope that you will ever find ‘The One? Wondering about the true purpose of Venn Diagrams? Dr Trina Dinnis gives an introduction to mathematical modelling and how this relates to the real world, using league tables, communication theory, and the novels of Jane Austen.

Title: Gavin Francis on The Man Who Mistook His Wife for a Hat
Subtitle: Reading Workshop
Teaser: Award-winning author and GP Gavin Francis explores The Man Who Mistook His Wife for a Hat by neurologist Oliver Sacks. This fascinating work describes the case histories of people struggling against incredible adversity, enabling us to enter the world...
Description: Award-winning author and GP Gavin Francis explores The Man Who Mistook His Wife for a Hat by neurologist Oliver Sacks. This fascinating work describes the case histories of people struggling against incredible adversity, enabling us to enter the world of the neurologically impaired. Expect an open discussion from the start: you can either read the book ahead of the event or be inspired to pick it up afterwards.

Title: After the Higgs Boson - What's next?
Teaser: Enter the Cosmic Ray Doorway to discover the world of particle physics
Description: Enter the Cosmic Ray Doorway to discover the world of particle physics and how we can explore the building blocks of the whole universe. Drive a particle accelerator, watch cosmic rays glide through our cloud chamber, and discover why the Higgs Boson is so important.

Title: Liars' Club
Description: This successful London club night comes to Edinburgh. Join hosts Lou Sanders and Vanessa Hammick (from Hello) with drop-ins from the UK’s finest improvisers including Cariad Lloyd, Paul Foxcroft, Pippa Evans, Rachel Parris and Graham Dickson. Every show is different. Come and see what all the fuss is about. Reviews of performers include: ***** (Times). ‘Refreshingly different’ **** (Fest). ‘Very, very funny... Sanders nails it’ **** (Time Out). **** (Independent). ‘Free in more ways than one’ (BroadwayBaby.com). **** (Guardian). ‘Hello Impro are completely unique and always hilarious’ (Cariad Lloyd, Peep Show).
Venue description: A daily selection of free shows, comedy, theatre and cabaret, running as part of the Free Festival, with performances running all day from midday until midnight in this friendly venue, offering a wide range of drinks and food.
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site, Some areas not reachable by lift or level access, No wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking

Title: Drawn to the Light: LED Sketching
Teaser: Science meets art in this fun workshop.
Description: Join in on this hands-on workshop, for all ages and artistic abilities, that brings the worlds of science and art together. Photography is one of the best examples of where science and art merge and this workshop with Dr Kathryn Harkup will teach you how to paint, sketch and doodle with light to create beautiful images, using long exposure photography and a bit of science along the way.

Title: Novel Experiments in Living
Description: Novel Experiments in Living follows some characters in a script, as they discover, to various extents, that they’re characters in a script. It’s a love story, it’s a social commentary, it’s a coming-of-age tale. (It’s pretentious, it’s confusing, it screams student theatre). It’s a play that writes itself. (It’s a play that critiques itself). Loose the plot with this mind-bending new comedy. (Nah don’t bother, I hear Alistair McGowan's at the Fringe this year…)
Venue description: The festivals smartest multi-space venue, located right in the hub of the festival, the ultimate powerhouse of live performance. Here we offer a pulsating programme of cross genre performance art. The festivals largest programme of new writing, children's, classical, dance, physical, monologues, poetry and comedy. All under one roof in one spectacular venue. For more information: www.thespaceuk.com.
Venue accessibility: Ramps to venue box office, and three ground floor theatres, lift to Grand Theatre. Full venue site is accessible, Lift level access to all areas, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, On street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas

Title: At the Fringe of Reason: Skeptics In The Pub
Teaser: A line-up of talks related to science, reason and critical thinking
Description: Edinburgh Skeptics head back to the pub for a series of events during Science Festival 2016. Join them as they investigate a selection of topics relating to science, reason and critical thinking including GMOs, genders, materials of tomorrow, psychic cons, syphilis, the biology of crime, big data and big brother and happiness. See edskeptics.co.uk for full programme information.

Title: I Love You / It's Over
Description: Palms sweating. Heart racing. Smiling like an idiot. It's love isn't it? (Or is it just a chemical reaction?). A darkly humorous exploration of what love really means to us all and why we long to chase after those three little words. A contemporary verbatim theatre piece with emerging artist Mairi Davidson in collaboration with Tiny Fragments Theatre.
Artist: Mairi Davidson / Tiny Fragments / YACNE Fife Youth Arts
Venue description: The Edinburgh Academy is centrally located in the New Town, with ample off-street parking and refreshments are available 30 minutes before every performance. The venue has several spaces including its Performing Arts Centre and Science Lecture Theatre.
Venue accessibility: Full venue site is accessible, Some areas not reachable by lift or level access, Wheelchair accessible toilet, Reserved accessible parking, On street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas

Title: Not Quite Write
Description: We always strive for those eureka moments, the top 1% of ideas, but what about the other 99%? Rubbish right? Wrong. Not Quite Write prides itself on the 99%. All that glistens isn't gold, but it’s sure worth trying to make a cheap joke out of. Join Oxford student comics Low Hanging Fruit as they take a deconstructed look at the sketch writing process, imagining a fictional writers’ office which throws quality control out the window and stages the lot: the good, the bad, and the not quite right.
Venue description: This intimate space hosts an array of new and established work. Well known for producing that little nugget on the fringe. Located seconds from the Royal Mile with bar and cafe facilities. Very well known for new and emerging work and a strong reputation with well heeled theatre goers. For show information: www.thespaceuk.com.
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site, Some areas not reachable by lift or level access, Wheelchair accessible toilet, Reserved accessible parking, On street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas

Title: Dreams and Nightmares
Description: Auld Reekie, the Athens of the North. Our city and our people weave two tales. Edinburgh has seen centuries of ambition and glory alongside riot and ruin. We’ll show you closes and courtyards to share tales where dreams were made, and nightmares unfolded. Organised by Mercat Tours.

Title: Godspell
Description: Borderline Confrontational is a group of students and graduates from the Birmingham School of Acting. A talented international cast brings a devised version of Godspell, Stephen Schwartz’s musicalised telling of parables from the Gospel of Matthew, mixing folk rock with storytelling.
Venue description: Rumoured to be the original fringe venue, this is one of the most talked about theatres in town, its unique atmosphere is known in fringe folklore. Here we present new and established work from across the globe. A full daily programme of cross-genre performance makes this wonderfully located venue a must for all. Show info. www.thespaceuk.com.
Venue accessibility: Full venue site is accessible, Lift level access to all areas, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, On street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas

Title: Remembering Chet
Description: Most Chet Baker tributes celebrate the trumpet-playing of the man but rarely showcase his vocal talent too. 27 years after his passing, three of Scotland's finest musicians join forces to bring his music to life. Trumpet maestro Colin Steele, the sublime piano accompaniment of Euan Stevenson and the smooth vocals of Iain Ewing combine to produce something truly magical. Well respected in their own right, expect something different as this trio join forces. Transport yourself back in time to a smoky jazz joint for some beautifully laid-back West Coast jazz.
Artist: Remembering Chet featuring Iain Ewing, Colin Steele and Euan Stevenson.
Venue description: This stylish basement bar is Edinburgh's coolest, multiple award-winning, year-round live music venue, with a crammed daily programme of multi-genre music and Fringe shows running all day, every day, from 13:00-05:00. As well as all the independent Fringe shows hosted by the venue, you’ll hear the bar’s own programme of excellent music, with great jazz, funk, acoustic, blues and rocky sounds – and bar service to 05:00 nightly!
Venue accessibility: Access to the basement venue is by two flights of stairs down from street level, there is space for a chairlift nor disabled toilets. Limited access to some parts of venue site, Some areas not reachable by lift or level access, No wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, On street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. Access to the basement venue is by two flights of stairs down from street level, there is space for a chairlift, nor disabled toilets

Title: Worbey and Farrell's Rhapsody
Description: In this brand new show following sell-outs in 2013, 2014 and 2015, the internationally acclaimed duo bring their unique touch to the world's greatest music. Expect exhilarating rhapsodies, beguiling boogie-woogies and sensational piano-playing. From Liszt to Jools Holland, from Queen to Gershwin, the ingenuity of these amazing musicians makes you laugh one moment and takes your breath away the next. Prepare to be moved, delighted and utterly gobsmacked. 'Extremely virtuosic and beyond dazzling' (Sean Rafferty, BBC Radio 3). ***** (Scotsman). ***** (Herald). ***** (ThreeWeeks). ***** (Edinburgh Evening News). ***** (BroadwayBaby.com).
Venue description: Assembly George Square Theatre is perfectly located next to Assembly George Square Gardens and Studios for pre or post show drinks or food. The theatre itself is a purpose built venue with comfortable modern seating for up to 500, while the The Box is an intimate 80 seat studio hosting great theatre and comedy.

Title: Guillermo Erades & Hamid Ismailov
Subtitle: The End of the Soviet Union
Teaser: The crazy early years of post-Soviet Russia are handled with great originality in Guillermo Erades’ novel Back to Moscow, set at the turn of the millennium against a backdrop of conflict in Chechnya. Hamid Ismailov’s The Underground goes back...
Description: The crazy early years of post-Soviet Russia are handled with great originality in Guillermo Erades’ novel Back to Moscow, set at the turn of the millennium against a backdrop of conflict in Chechnya. Hamid Ismailov’s The Underground goes back further, to before and after the USSR collapsed. Multifaceted and subtle, it’s partly a nod to Moscow’s grand underground system, but mainly a tapestry of ideas about an entire epoch.

Title: The Eclectic Guitar of Tony Mitchell
Description: Following his two very successful previous shows, Mitchell returns with another programme of solos, including his own compositions and songs in various styles. A review of Tony's 2014 Fringe show said: ‘Mitchell's relaxed style was very assured and truly eclectic covering folk, blues, classical, jazz etc’ (ThreeWeeks). Mitchell is also guitarist with Brack'n'File.
Venue description: Acoustic Music Centre @ St Bride's is approx 5 - 10 minutes' walk from the important Haymarket road and rail interchange.

Very close to several bus routes

Title: You Wouldn't Want to Be in the Great Fire of London!
Description: You Wouldn't Want to Be in the Great Fire of London is a 45 minute, 100 miles per hour show for kids! Two storytellers will transport the children back to 1666 smoggy, grotty London, where the most famous fire in history began! Come with us on an adventure ride of the imagination, come laugh with us, sing with us and help us save London! This production is adapted from the children's book You Wouldn't Want to Be in the Great Fire of London published by The Salariya Book Company.
Venue description: The Sir Arthur Conan Doyle Centre is situated on Palmerston Place, just a stone throw away from Haymarket Station. Set in a beautiful Victorian Townhouse, the Centre boasts rich historical features and was created to provide for the physical, emotional and spiritual well-being of society and community needs in Edinburgh.

Amongst the animated jewels vying for your vote to be crowned the 27th McLaren Award Winner, we have prophetic characters delving into the future, an adaptation of a short story by Jack London, the tenderness of love inferred through potted plants, and the nature of reality torn apart in a way only animation can do. Title: Tom Bullough & Anjali Joseph
Subtitle: Landscapes and Lives
Teaser: Literary prize judges, take note. Here are two luminous, lyrical novels which reveal deep truths about globalisation and a changing world. Tom Bullough’s Addlands is the stunning saga of a family living in the Welsh Borders, while Anjali Joseph’s...
Description: Literary prize judges, take note. Here are two luminous, lyrical novels which reveal deep truths about globalisation and a changing world. Tom Bullough’s Addlands is the stunning saga of a family living in the Welsh Borders, while Anjali Joseph’s The Living tells the story of two lives: a young woman working in an English shoe factory, and an older man in a western Indian town. Chaired by Daniel Hahn.

Title: Black
Description: A stylish and brutal story of forbidden love, the impressively staged Black is driven by a mesmerising lead performance from newcomer Martha Canga Antonio as 15 year-old Mavela, whose love for the member of a rival gang sees her life descend into violence. The film offers a tough glimpse into the dark side of Brussels, which has seen an increase in the number and brutality of teen gangs. Beautifully shot in widescreen, it is an unflinching but compelling drama. [18]

Title: Unbound
Subtitle: The Flint & Pitch Revue
Teaser: All-round literary powerhouse Jenny Lindsay launches her latest venture, Flint & Pitch, which continues the cabaret style of Rally & Broad presenting the best of Scotland-based spoken word, music and live lit. The first line-up is packed with readings...
Description: All-round literary powerhouse Jenny Lindsay launches her latest venture, Flint & Pitch, which continues the cabaret style of Rally & Broad presenting the best of Scotland-based spoken word, music and live lit. The first line-up is packed with readings from Hannah McGill, performances from Dave Hook, Katie Ailes and Sam Small, plus music from Roseanne Reid and Pronto Mama.  Over 18s only.

Title: Nick Cope's Family Songbook
Description: Nick's family performances are legendary! He has a fanatical army of little and not so little fans from all over the world. If you haven't heard his songs or seen his shows before come and find out what you're missing. 'A brilliant show' ***** (TheEdinburghReporter.co.uk). With songs about dogs eating soap and dragons called Keith. 'Even the shyest of kids will warm to his unpretentious style' **** (Fest). 'Nick puts the audience first, and deserves a much, much bigger one. If that audience could be you, go and see him' **** (BroadwayBaby.com).
Venue description: An exciting, vibrant, neo-gothic mini-castle housing nine performance spaces and seven bars including the exclusive roof top bar, The Loft. A must for all Fringe-goers. A massive mini-Fringe under one roof, this iconic venue has spawned the best of the best on the Fringe! All spaces, the café and all seven bars are wheelchair accessible, with the exception of the Balcony and Billiard Rooms. Tickets available 24-hours online!

Title: The Haggis Horns
Description: The Haggis Horns are a seven-piece live funk extravaganza combining heavy breakbeat funk, soul, hip-hop and afrobeat with the virtuosity of trained jazz musicians. The members of The Haggis Horns have performed and recorded with the likes of Jamiroquai, John Legend and The Roots, Amy Winehouse, Corinne Bailey Rae, Take That, Mark Ronson, Martha Reeves, Roots Manuva, Lou Donaldson, Elbow, Nightmares On Wax, Dennis Coffey, Adele, Finley Quaye, Robbie Williams, Morcheeba, Duran Duran, The Cinematic Orchestra, Lisa Stansfield, Kano, Estelle, Lily Allen, KT Tunstall and Snowboy, to name a few!
Venue description: This venue is in a fantastic location just off George Street. It has an impressive, large internal area with table seating for 220 and a VIP area. Table service meals and a cocktail bar will be available during the show.

Title: Care Takers
Description: ‘Those who care, aren’t the ones who stay.’ Ms Lawson, a new teacher at Newall South High School, believes Jamie Harrow is being bullied because he’s gay. She wants to help but a bigger bully in the form of Deputy Head, Mrs Rutter, stands in her way. Winner of a Stage Edinburgh Award 2016 for excellence. ‘Pure theatre at its best!’ *****(Broadwaybaby.com). ‘Tight and powerful... hits home with a punch’ *****(WhatsOnStage.com). ‘A great piece of writing... fiery and quick. Go see it’ ***** (RemoteGoat.com) ‘Insightful, provocative and plausible’ (Manchester Evening News).
Venue description: C, our multiplex main venue, is a powerhouse of outstanding international performance - a happening Festival hub hosting everything from Bardic Breakfasts to late night cabaret. Four larger-size theatres, bar and events space. C is part of the C venues curated programme taking place in over twenty performance spaces at multiple city-centre venues in our 26th year at the Fringe.

Title: Fingertips
Description: ‘Everything you thought you knew is now basically obsolete.’ A brave and dynamic piece of new writing. From the critically acclaimed team behind 1984 and The Winterling, Fingertips is a play about life as a twentysomething, struggling to find your place in a virtual world. Inspired by interviews with real people, the play explores what sex, love and identity mean to this lost generation, desperate for independence but scared to grow up. Real people, real relationships, real life.
Warnings: Explicit language, sexual references.
Venue description: C nova, our popular seven-storey multiplex, is an unrivalled city centre hub. Features intimate studio theatres and fantastic found spaces. C nova's spaces are ideal for smaller-scale theatre, physical theatre, cabaret and comedy. C nova also houses installation spaces and immersive environments. C nova is part of the C venues curated programme taking place in over twenty performance spaces at multiple city-centre venues in our 26th year at the Fringe.

Title: Kevin Barry
Subtitle: John Lennon’s Bad Trip
Teaser: Kevin Barry’s Beatlebone recently won the £10,000 Goldsmiths Prize for ‘fiction at its most novel’. The phrase seems apt: even though this is a story built from familiar elements – an imagined John Lennon, post-Beatles in 1978, trying to pay a...
Description: Kevin Barry’s Beatlebone recently won the £10,000 Goldsmiths Prize for ‘fiction at its most novel’. The phrase seems apt: even though this is a story built from familiar elements – an imagined John Lennon, post-Beatles in 1978, trying to pay a visit to an isle off the coast of Ireland that the real-life Lennon bought in the 60s – Barry has produced a tour de force that’s funny, raw and dazzlingly novel.

Title: Paul Foot: 'Tis a Pity She's a Piglet
Description: This year Professor Ketchup and his camembert piglet join forces as Paul tackles the big issues such as terrorism. Plus, Ant and Dec, immigration, X factor and breakfast. 'Sublime, original and brilliant' (Independent). 'Surreal, unique and over all too quickly, he's the only Paul Foot available at the Fringe' **** (EdFestMag.com). 'Utterly outlandish, but beneath layers of absurdity is Foot's sharp eye for satire' **** (Time Out). 'He's a comedy whirlwind from the school of Spike Milligan... it's risky to call someone unique, but Foot is certainly pretty close' (ThreeWeeks).
Venue description: Now in its 17th year, Underbelly Cowgate is home to some of the best talent and the best bars you can find at the Fringe. Complete with a Cow Cafe (serving up coffee, snacks and free late-night entertainment), three licensed bars and seven vivacious venues open til 5am.

Title: Best of Scottish Comedian of the Year
Description: **** (Scotsman). ***** (BroadwayBaby.com). Ten sell-out years. Biggest selling showcase of multi award-winning Scottish comedy talent at the Fringe. Featuring previous SCOTY finalists and winners. 'Rarely can a non-sponsored event have featured quite so many mentions of Greggs the bakers' **** (Scotsman). 'SCOTY does attract some major talent' (Skinny). 'No one can deny the sense of excitement and occasion that this annual event now generates' (Scotsman). Title: Mercy and the Wild Sea
Description: A sensational, original rock-opera experience set in the 34th century, this show brings together live rock music, dramatic performance and a spectacular movie created by award-winning BetterFeelingFilms. Set in the beautiful cut-throat galaxy of the online game Elite:Dangerous, we follow the journey of disgraced Commander Mercy, vocalist Corinne Lucy, ‘sounds like the love child of Joni Mitchell and Karen Carpenter’ (Robert Rosenberg, Trinifold). Brian Portsmouth (whose stage roles have included Alan Turing at the Haymarket), portrays Alexander Selcraig, long-retired Federation Intelligence Officer on an extraordinary personal mission: 100 years later... Is it too late?
Venue description: Paradise Green is the heart and soul of the largest arts festival in the world, presenting a wide range of top-quality performances. Visit our beautiful and friendly venue, relax with a drink from our snack bar before your performance and soak up the true atmosphere of the Fringe.

Title: The McLaureen's Tale
Description: Christine Khandjian presents a Celtic musical inspired by Irish migration. Come hear Sally’s story, crossing the ocean for a second chance! Singer/songwriter: C Khandjian. Director: Colton Pometta. With video projections. Book: Guy/C Khandjian, adapted by D Graves.
Venue description: Spotlites is one of the leading venues at Edfringe, with seven unique, beautiful theatres established at the heart of the Festival. Our central, easy to find venue, on George Street, presents an outstanding programme of international companies, interactive children's theatre, drama workshops, innovative plays, musicals, dance, music, magic, poetry, comedy and cabaret. Spotlites has a reputation for quality five and four star sell-outs, clean facilities and caring, helpful staff.

There are lifts throughout the venue to all the spaces

Title: Maureen Langan: Daughter of a Garbage Man
Description: In Daughter of a Garbage Man, Maureen addresses our Kardashian culture, where making a sex tape and oiling-up your ass leads to fame and fortune. Maureen’s Irish mother and sanitation worker father told her to work hard, get educated, and life would reward her. But is that true? With laugh-aloud insight, Maureen taps into the hearts and frustrations of hard-working people everywhere who wonder if they were raised wrong. Maureen is an American broadcaster and stand-up comic. She is proud to debut her solo show at the 2016 Edinburgh Festival Fringe. www.MaureenLangan.com
Warnings:
All seating is unreserved. Late comers may not be
admitted.
Venue description: Stand 5 and Stand 6 are located at The Place – a luxury four-star boutique townhouse hotel, situated in a stunning A-listed Georgian terrace in the very heart of Edinburgh's New Town. Stand 5 & 6 offer comfort, space, a roof terrace bar and complimentary WiFi. The venue also boosts a stylish restaurant and opulent cocktail bar. Catch another sensational comedy line-up from The Stand family here!

Title: Echoes from the Past
Description: On The Runn's youth performance group present a look back at their work over the last five years incorporating contemporary, jazz and lyrical dance performances. A young dynamic group of dancers who perform with energy, emotion and intensity. For more information visit www.fifeyoutharts.com.

Title: Rob Deering's Beat This
Description: The live music-based game show and late-night Fringe favourite from 'brilliant musical comedian' (Time Out) Rob Deering returns. 'Employing live music mash-ups and megamixes (not enough of them nowadays) and music trivia, nimble-fingered Deering pits comedians and audience against each other' (Comedy Central). The festival's not the festival without Beat This, the perfect end – middle, if you're that badass – to your evening. New show with four top-notch guests every time. Previous guests include Alan Davies, Gary Delaney, Nick Helm, Miles Hunt, Sarah Millican, Andi Osho, Frank Skinner and Josh Widdicombe.

Title: Men With Coconuts
Description: Last year’s Top Free Show on the Fringe (Daily Record) is back for a limited run only! Improvised comedy games and sketches culminating in an entirely improvised musical. This show combines improvised sketches and stories, accompanied by a pianist, to create a packed and entertaining hour. The experienced cast of actors work together to discover the comedy in scenes suggested and inspired by audience members. Men With Coconuts are comedians, actors and musicians of international acclaim now at home in Edinburgh. ‘Skilful and hysterical!’ (Jo Caulfield). 'Hilarious!' **** (EdFringeReview.com).
Venue description: The Scottish Storytelling Centre is the world's first purpose-built centre for storytelling, right on the Royal Mile. The award-winning Netherbow Theatre and Storytelling Court spaces host live storytelling, traditional arts, literature, theatre, children's and visual arts events. A warm welcome for families. Book online, over the phone and in person for tickets.

Title: John Hands
Subtitle: Where is the Human Race Heading?
Teaser: The Book Festival has always enjoyed asking big questions. And they don’t come much bigger than those posed by John Hands in Cosmosapiens, an astonishing new survey of scientific understanding and its limits. With the breadth of Bill Bryson, the...
Description: The Book Festival has always enjoyed asking big questions. And they don’t come much bigger than those posed by John Hands in Cosmosapiens, an astonishing new survey of scientific understanding and its limits. With the breadth of Bill Bryson, the exploratory powers of Stephen Hawking and the controversial bent of Richard Dawkins, Hands' decade-long study challenges our understanding of human evolution. Chaired by James Runcie.

Title: Sick (Bolesno)
Description: At the age of 16, Ana’s parents locked her up in a psychiatric hospital in a bid to “cure her of homosexuality”. After five years during which she endured a harsh regime trapped in a high security ward, Ana was physically freed; but were the residual emotional scars irretrievably deep? Hell-bent on revenge and fuelled by anger and hatred, she finds herself in a new relationship, but will her inability to escape the past deny her a chance of happiness? [12A]

Title: Game For the Next Generation (Advanced)
Description: Do you love gaming? Here is an opportunity for you to design and build your very own game for the next generation. Using basic coding build a game concept that you think would sell! You can expect: a hands-on experience; to learn how to build and programme your own virtual world; learn to use Kodu software; support and guidance to use technology to make a 3D computer game. This workshop is suitable for people aged 9+ and prior experience in using Kodu is not required. Adults welcome! More info at www.edef.co.uk
Warnings: suitable for people aged 9+
Venue description:
The iconic Assembly Rooms building is at the heart of Edinburgh's New Town. In 2016 the Assembly Rooms play host venue to the inaugural Edinburgh Digital Entertainment Festival which will be showcasing
the best recordings of live arts events in a world class Cinema as well as presenting the best in new technological developments across the sector through a series of stands, talks, workshops and live presentations.

Title: Kamila Shamsie on Kim
Subtitle: Reading Workshop
Teaser: Pakistani novelist Kamila Shamsie explores the highly controversial Kim by Rudyard Kipling. Providing a detailed portrait of the people and culture of late 19th century India, this absorbing novel offers an insight into political, religious and social...
Description: Pakistani novelist Kamila Shamsie explores the highly controversial Kim by Rudyard Kipling. Providing a detailed portrait of the people and culture of late 19th century India, this absorbing novel offers an insight into political, religious and social tensions. Expect an open discussion from the start: you can either read the book ahead of the event, or be inspired to pick it up afterwards.

Title: Gut Feeling
Teaser: A panel event exploring our complex relationship with the bacteria in our gut
Description: Discover the important role your gut plays in your overall health. Prof Adam Hart, author of The Life of Poo, will chair this fascinating panel event, supported by the British Society for Immunology, featuring immunologist Prof Fiona Powrie FRS and microbiologist Dr Lindsay Hall. You’ll be introduced to bacterial biology and the immune system, followed by a discussion on the latest research connecting gut bacteria with inflammatory bowel disease, Crohn's disease, asthma, eczema and even mental health. There will be a chance to ask your own question and an opportunity to interact with a demonstration wall, led by Prof Powrie, after the event.

Title: Make a Monster
Teaser: Learn about biodiversity by designing a monster!
Description: Meet some of the strangest animals that exist on our planet and learn how biodiversity and adaptation help them to survive. Inspired by these weird creatures, you’ll design and make your very own monster from recycled materials. We'll also help you to capture a photograph of your monster in its natural habitat using our custom Monster Photobooth!

Title: Rob Auton: The Sleep Show
Description: This show is about sleep. It is suitable for those who have slept. Following on from 2012's The Yellow Show, 2013's The Sky Show, 2014's The Face Show, 2015's The Water Show, award-winning writer and performer Rob Auton returns with 2016's The Sleep Show. ‘Just sad’ (Vanessa Feltz). ‘We need him’ (Scotsman). ‘Entirely compelling to watch’ (Daniel Kitson). ‘A genuine original. Poetical, philosophical, humane, completely charming and funny to boot.’ (Guardian). ‘Like watching a kid caught in the stage lights of his first Nativity’ (Venue.co.uk).
Venue description: Roundabout is Paines Plough’s beautiful pop-up in-the-round theatre. It offers a unique 360 degree theatre experience with 168-seats wrapped around the stage, state-of-the-art LED lighting and surround sound. Roundabout flat packs and pops-up across the UK bringing the nation’s best playwrights and a thrilling atmosphere to audiences everywhere. "The lovliest venue at the Fringe" The List
Venue accessibility: Paines Plough are excited to be trialing closed captioning within Roundabout this year. Closed captioning will be available on tablets for some shows in Roundabout. Patrons who require a captioning tablet must notify Roundabout front of house via text/call on 07855 744164 or email office@painesplough.com. 24 hours notice is preferred as tablets are limited.  Patrons are advised to collect captioning tablets from Roundabout front of house staff 15-20 minutes before the performance. Title: Kiri Pritchard-McLean: Hysterical Woman
Description: Chortle Award-nominated comedian Kiri Pritchard McLean performs her inadvisably ambitious debut hour, tackling genetics, gender and being a comedian who happens to be a woman. Also, she sticks her white, middle class nose into racial inequality. (I know, it has nothing to do with her, but she won't be told.) Join her for an hour of whipsmart stand-up that's as funny as it is clever – or turn up to see if she commits an accidental hate crime. 'One to look out for' (Leicester Mercury). Tour support: Justin Moorhouse. Writer/director Gein's Family.
Venue description: Soak up the legendary atmosphere at the Pleasance Courtyard, considered by many to be the heart of the Fringe. With every entertainment under the sun in seventeen venues, come take in a show, enjoy a drink and stay for the day. There's even the Kidzone for the little-ones! ‘The centre of the cultural universe' (Scotsman).

Title: Camille O'Sullivan: The Carny Dream
Description: 'Queen of the Fringe' (BBC) premieres new show: Dark, light, dreams, circus. Singing Cave, Bowie, Brel, Arcade Fire, Radiohead. Chameleon like, her five-star sell-out performances include Sydney Opera House, Royal Festival Hall, La Clique, Roundhouse, Later with Jools Holland (BBC) and a Herald Angel award for her RSC solo performance, Lucrece. Sexy, fierce and mesmerizing, Camille transforms each song into an intense, emotional experience. Expect joy and pure passion. 'A major star' ***** (Scotsman). 'Masterclass in living a lyric – mesmerising' ***** (Mail on Sunday). 'Exceptional voice' ***** (Time Out). 'Hypnotic' ***** (Independent).

Title: Team Viking

A debut show by James Rowland. For Previous Work: 'Magnificently clever' (Guardian). ‘The most dramatic Hamlet… dripping with sweat and rubbing his chest in pain, he yells whilst gurgling milk’ (Daily Mail). ‘Slightly odd' (Sunday Times).

Title: The Rights of The Machine
Teaser: Should we give robots the same rights as humans? Explore the issues in this lively panel discussion.
Description: In 2015, two chimpanzees in New York were granted ‘legal person status’ by a court ruling. This action has potentially groundbreaking implications in the field of medical ethics. Do intelligent robotic systems deserve civil rights? Or even human rights? Join Dr Peter Asaro, philosopher of science, technology and media, Kathleen Richardson from the Campaign Against Sex Robots, and Dr Patricia Vargas, Roboethicist and Director of the Robotics Laboratory, as they explore the rights of the machine.

Description:

Our mortal bodies are bombarded by risk and our minds plagued by the pressures of progress. Have we become too fragile to evolve? A programme of short films followed by live discussion with specially invited guests.

From 1999-2011 Ken Russell invented and propelled his Garagiste movement, creating home-produced comic-tragic surreal auteur films on a shoestring. These music hall meets punk, pre-Raphaelite meets postmodern short films include Fall of the Louse of Usher, Lion’s Mouth, Revenge of the Elephant Man, Mystery of Mata Hari, Charlotte Bronte, Goodship Venus, his last, Boudica Bites Back, alongside others that have not been seen since 1965.
Warnings: The films are short, from 20 to 45 to 71 minutes and a few have a little surreal nudity but no sex.

Title: Mozart's Requiem by Candlelight
Description: Described as the sublimest achievement that the modern period has contributed to the church, there can be few more befitting settings in which to experience the heart-wrenching beauty of Mozart’s Requiem than by candlelight in the historic St Giles' Cathedral. The story of its creation (as sensationalised by the Oscar-winning Amadeus) is as intriguing as this, his final masterpiece, is enigmatic. The National Youth Choir of Scotland reprises its critically acclaimed performance of this dark yet resplendent choral work for the first time since the BBC Proms in 2014.
Venue description: Founded in the 1120s, St Giles' was the church of John Knox during the Reformation and is renowned for its stained glass, Rieger organ and beautiful Thistle Chapel. Open daily. Title: Jenny Downham: Unspeakable Truths
Teaser: Jenny Downham's first book, the multi award-winning Before I Die, became an international bestseller and spawned the major Hollywood movie Now is Good, starring Dakota Fanning. Now Jenny returns to explore issues of identity and unspeakable truths in...

Come along to find out more about this tender, funny, life-affirming piece of storytelling.

Title: Missed Connections
Description: The unwritten rule of the London Underground: never speak to anyone! Thousands of strangers, hundreds of journeys and countless fleeting interactions. Avoiding glances, defending personal space and dodging as many armpits as possible. It’s just another Saturday night on the tube. Across the city and across train lines, three chance encounters lead to unexpected revelations in this new short play by Rachel Jarmy. From the writer of Cubicle Four and I’ll Be Seeing You comes an everyday tale of life on the underground, and what happens when you break the unwritten rule.

C nova is part of the C venues curated programme taking place in over twenty performance spaces at multiple city-centre venues in our 26th year at the Fringe.

Teaser: Join us in raising a glass to the literally and figuratively) to the wonderful art and science of wine making
Description: ‘In vino veritas, in aqua sanitas’ – ‘in wine there is truth, in water there is health’; a great hypothesis with which to start our exploration of the world of wine! This event will raise a glass (literally and figuratively) to the wonderful art and science of wine making and challenge some common assumptions: Does expensive wine taste better? Will we ever see vineyards in Scotland? Is there a difference between corked bottles and screw tops?

Title: Alistair Moffat
Subtitle: Scotland’s Moment in the Sun

Description: While Edinburgh in August is passionate about exploring the ‘international’ across its festivals, there is always a vital place for delving deep into the heart of Scotland. And that’s what Alistair Moffat will be doing when he discusses his Scotland: A History from Earliest Times which looks at the major battles as well as exploring the ordinary people who have shaped this land from Ice Age to IndyRef. Chaired by Ruth Wishart.

Title: Kirsty Lusk & Willy Maley
Subtitle: Scotland and the Easter Rising
Teaser: 100 years on, the 1916 Rising remains a defining moment in Irish history. It's also of immense importance for Scotland, and for Irish people living in Scotland. In a major new volume, Scotland and the Easter Rising, Professor of Renaissance Studies at...
Description: 100 years on, the 1916 Rising remains a defining moment in Irish history. It's also of immense importance for Scotland, and for Irish people living in Scotland. In a major new volume, Scotland and the Easter Rising, Professor of Renaissance Studies at Glasgow University Willy Maley and researcher Kirsty Lusk bring together a powerful mix of fresh perspectives on the topic. Chaired by Jane Fowler.

Title: Aurora Revelation Exhibition by TK Chan

She is the co-founder of BLINK Gallery Hong Kong. This exhibition showcases her landscape oil paintings and original series Aurora Revelation by applying scientific knowledge to the creative arts. TK is calling for solidarity around concerns about global warming and asking people to join together to protect our mother earth in harmony. This series is inspired by the mysteriously beautiful but volatile Aurora Borealis.

After a spilt cup of tea causes their mime time machine to explode, two mimes become trapped above the fourth dimension, existing everywhere and everywhen as their consciousness is stretched thin over the vastness of the universe. These two brave mimes, who don't really like each other, will travel from the end to the beginning of time itself in a desperate attempt to find meaning in an infinite existence. But it's mostly jokes about time travel.

Title: The science of panda breeding
Teaser: Find out why it’s so hard to breed these giant bears
Description: Pandas are threatened by extinction in their native region of China so it’s ever more important that captive breeding programmes exist. RZSS Edinburgh Zoo has the UK’s only giant pandas – Tian Tian and Yang Guang – but to date a panda cub has remained elusive. Join Director of Giant Pandas Iain Valentine, alongside RZSS Edinburgh’s in-house expert panda keepers, vets and external partners for a discussion on the science behind panda breeding.

Praise for Annie's previous work: ‘Shiningly original narrative… moving and macabre’ **** (List). ‘Untamed, brilliant writing… A one-woman rollercoaster ride’ **** (Fest). ‘Impressively original… hovers around the sublime’ **** (BroadwayBaby.com).

Our staff are here to help and if there is anything you need assistance with please do not hesitate to ask.

I put the toilet seat down in public toilets just in case a woman goes into the gents by mistake. I write please in Google searches. When I’m pretending to be a car, I let people cross. But a twisted darkness inspires my thoughts. It is that which I must share with you. Star of Intensive Carey, BBC Radio 4. ‘Anecdotally debauched’ **** (Herald). ‘Supremely crafted comedy’ **** (List). ***** (Edinburgh Evening News).**** (Chortle.co.uk) **** (Scotsman).

Title: How We Lost It
Description: How We Lost It is a piece about who we are now, where we’ve come from and asks what we’ve lost (and gained) in between. A coming of age story that sees us come to terms with the fact that our prince charming might look a little different to the fairy tale – but hey, we don’t need saving anyway. We weave together our own stories about youth, love, sex and growing up, inviting the audience into our narrative and seducing them to revisit theirs. This is one lip-smacking, seam-splitting show, not to be missed.

The clock ticks, the afternoon gets hotter, the princess goes ballistic and the Skype calls grow more desperate. Come and watch our heroes – if you can figure out who they are – it’s going to be a right royal screw up!

With Amsterdam, Milord, La Vie en Rose and other French classics. ‘A bravura display of amazing colour and dynamic range’ (Edmonton Journal). ‘Gall has an astounding voice that leaves audiences breathless’ (Vue Magazine). ‘A beautifully rendered and loving homage’ (CBC.ca). ***** (Winnipeg Free Press).

But first he needs to contact Oscar-winning Matthew McConaughey and Labour Party-leading Jeremy Corbyn. It's a long story... A true, enlightening, politically crusading, surreal, physically madcap, sincere story. With jokes. 'Obvious talent' (Chortle.co.uk). 'Clever and funny' (Al Murray).

Scientist and performer Dr Niamh Shaw has dreamed of space travel from the age of eight. Title: Shorts 4: Other Planes
Description:
Traversing a winding pathway that leads the senses through a luminous immersion into colour, light, movement and sound, this selection explores the process of seeing and perceiving as a powerful multi-sensory experience.   Tearing at the boundaries of the visual language of cinema, these works weave into being a dazzling spectrum of evocative images, drifting through hazy corridors of memory, examining the ambiguous relationship between what we see and how we recall it, and exploring performance as a medium for channeling resistance and rebellion. [12A]
Anna, Pina, Teresa  Cynthia Madansky/Italy/2015/7 min
Refracting historical narratives through movement and engaging dance as a form of resistance, Madansky ingeniously reappropriates the three key movements from Pina's death scene in Rossellini's Roma Città Aperta.

Expression of the Sightless Jessica Sarah Rinland/UK/2016/7 min
An observational mapping of a trio of sculpted figures by a blind man; his sensorial explorations form a paean to tactility and the manifold ways of 'seeing' and perceiving.

Fire, Water, Air (Feu, Eau, Air) Anne Murat, David Bart/France/2016/15 min
Vivid, optic portrait of an artist whose textile and sculptural work elegantly merges traditional Japanese artisanal techniques with natural, environmental processes.

The Frame Lars Koens, Demelza Kooij/UK/2016/7 min
Imploring us to look beyond conventional visual grammar, Kooij and Koens meditate upon the parameters of the cinematic form, expanding the confines of the compositional frame.

Ghost Copy Christiana Perschon/Austria/2016/2 min
Repurposed found footage sets into motion a regenerative process whereby the disembodied visual voices of the past reach from within the film's frames, into the present.

Remembering the Pentagons Azadeh Navai/USA, Iran/2015/23 min
Navai evokes the formative memories of her Iranian childhood, weaving together an opulent patchwork of emotionally resonant 16mm film through which we journey through the sensory and synaesthetic.

A Thing Among Things Giovanni Giaretta/Netherlands/2015/7 min
The ambiguity of memories and the subjective nature of perception are examined in this enigmatic audiovisual work.

Title: The Living Room
Description: The Living Room takes us home, to a place in which we welcome another. By starting from this fundamental action that can take place in a living room, we enter an investigation into how the potentialities of performance craft can both enrich and be enriched by daily interpersonal relations and realities. How can our room come alive? Within our meeting a performative event unfolds, structured and precise, a living stream of actions based on work with songs of tradition, as well as texts exploring what it takes to awaken face to ourselves, the other, and the world.

In the duo section, Gordon Ferries will be joined by special guest artist, Stephen Morrison. Both players will perform on period instruments. 'Ferries' playing is subtle, rich and probing' (Independent).

Title: Dermatological Distractors
Teaser: Join us for a hands-on workshop exploring how art and science can help us to manage the symptoms and side-effects of eczema.
Description: In the UK, one in five children and one in twelve adults suffer from the skin condition, eczema. Symptoms of inflammation and itchy skin are commonplace amongst it's victims and can have a profound impact on how people lead their lives. In this hands-on workshop, join Trevor Gordon to explore how art and science can help people who have an urge to itch. Use dental alginate to take casts of your fingers, make patterns and mould small sculptures, explore textures and shapes to make small one-off distractors that you can pop in your pocket and keep, and learn how to effectively manage this condition in this artistic, dermatological masterclass.

Through laughter and tears, Kirk finds a way to come to peace with his son’s limitations and seeks to encourage others going through their own challenges.

Title: Future Realities: Exploring Augmented and Mixed Reality
Description: Pokemon Go has taken over and soon it will be commonplace to create and interact with holograms that blend into our surroundings. Unlike the simulated vistas in virtual reality, augmented reality and mixed reality allow the physical world to become interactive and digitally manipulable. While AR is augmenting virtual objects into the real world, MR allows us to navigate our existing landscape using virtual objects, enhancing the environment with digital content. This panel focuses on where AR and MR will take us and how they will revolutionise how we work and play.

Title: Traces
Description: Everything leaves a trace in this world. What would you find if you could go back and trace yours?  Think of all the lines and patterns, sounds and echoes we have made... these are the traces we leave behind and the traces we follow. Our lives leave imprints all around us - in the sand, on surfaces and on scraps of paper - to let others know where we have been. Our traces gently guide others in their first steps.  Traces take us on a very special and lyrical journey with stunning live musical accompaniment featuring the sounds of the echo of our voices. A visual and aural landscape is created allowing us time to contemplate how our lives are interlinked. Beginning and ending in our foyer creative play space, stay around afterwards to interact with the performers.

Title: Emballage
Description: Emballage refers to Tadeusz Kantor’s concept of wrapping, a utilitarian action taken from the most mundane reality of everyday life. This outcome of an imaginative reworking of the Richard Demarco Archive is supported by Leeds Beckett University’s PhD research programme. The piece is informed by the work of Joseph Beuys, Marina Abramovic, Rose Finn-Kelcey and Bobby Baker, while Shakespeare’s Macbeth and the autobiographical, archival narratives of the performers and the audience participants are explored. Audience members are encouraged to participate in the performance-installation, to navigate the spaces as they wish and to share memories from their subjective archives.
Artist: Leeds Beckett University, Richard Demarco Archive and Aletia Upstairs

Over a period of four years, Ben Rawlence explored this extraordinary 'temporary' city, getting close to the realities of life for its inhabitants. City of Thorns takes us beyond the shock headlines, offering testament to the frailty and resilience of humanity.

Title: As You Like It
Description: As You Like It is one of Shakespeare’s late plays, which celebrates love in the real world and views freedom in a vulnerable place, exposing the naked nature of desire and love and discovering human nature through the love between men and women, palace life and the Adam forest. This Chinese shadow play’s stage design is elegant and sumptuous, and its artistic value lies not only its beauty but in the development of new technology – new materials and modern design have created a new form of stage art.

Description: For Richard Barnett, surgery is an art as much as a science. Crucial Interventions is his breathtaking exploration of medicine in the 19th century, a period that saw a complete transformation of the practice and reputation of surgery. Drawing on rare surgical textbooks, he captures the beauty and detail that went into the illustrations and paintings crucial to enabling medical progress to be documented. Chaired by Sheena McDonald.

Title: Why Do Guitars Taste of Hops?
Teaser: An interactive show that’s part neuroscience, part memoir and part comedy – with plenty of beer!
Description: Award-winning beer writer and passionate music fan Pete Brown began pairing his favourite beers and tracks for fun, but a few years ago he discovered scientific principles behind the matches. Since then he’s been on a journey of discovery, investigating how our senses enhance, complement and sometimes confuse each other. Join him for an interactive show that’s part-neuroscience, part-memoir and part-comedy, with real-time scientific experiments; with real-time scientific experiments and some fine beer tasting.

Title: The Ruff Guide to Shakespeare
Description: Commemorating the 400th anniversary of his death, Ruff Guide tells the tale of William Shakespeare (well, what we know of him!) Seven actors from Bristol Old Vic Theatre School will take you on a journey through his life, his plays and the Elizabethan stage! So, expect silly songs, daft dance routines and some of his most famous speeches as you learn about the greatest playwright of all time!

Everyone else will have to make do with just laughing occasionally like a normal person.

This visual haiku draws on ideas from Japanese Butoh, Zen sages, and John Cage, with a gentle hint of mime and humour. A quietly understated insight into the daydreaming mind of a Zen fool, Baka. ‘Surprisingly touching... blissfully calm’ (Scotsman). ‘Movement beautifully blends with meditation in this memorably tranquil work... quietly satisfying’ (Stage). ‘A delightful, pleasing contrast to the frenzy of the Fringe’ (Skinny).

Venue description: Uniquely within Edinburgh's former Royal (Dick) Veterinary College, Summerhall presents high quality, engaging, challenging and exhilarating theatre, music, dance, visual arts for people of all ages. Our staff are here to help and if there is anything you need assistance with please do not hesitate to ask.

http://www.summerhall.co.uk/about/accessibility/. For who knows better than a child what a performance for children should be like?  However things are not so straightforward; the boys want monsters, blood and violence while the girls want pretty dresses and pretty dancing.  What results is hilarious and captivating with genuine moments of beauty.

It is a rich piece of history told through the eyes of brother and sister, Annika and Pepicek as they journey into town to buy milk for their sick mother. Along the way they encounter the mean organ-grinder Brundibar. They make friends with a cat, dog and sparrow, who help them gather the children of the village to help them defeat the tyrant.

Venue description:
Built in 1994, the impressive glass facade imposes a sense of occasion as you enter the sleek and contemporary foyer spaces. Enjoy a drink in our spacious bars and take in the inspiring views across to Arthur's Seat - but don't let the modern entrance fool you - the traditional 1915-seat auditorium, with its sumptuous decor and lavish fittings, has all the grandeur and splendour you need for a truly special theatrical experience.
Designed as Scotland's premier dance and opera house in 1994, the stage is the largest in Scotland, providing the perfect platform for world-class contemporary dance and ballet, and excellent acoustics make it a number one venue for opera, musicals and concerts. The Festival Theatre continues to provide the best programme of dance and opera in the country, as well as a variety of world-class productions across all artforms. Home to the International Festival in the summer, and Christmas shows in winter, you'll find unmissable entertainment here all year round.
The Festival Theatre is by no means short of history either - and we've got the ghost stories to prove it! Standing on Edinburgh's longest continuous theatre site, and previously Edinburgh's beloved Empire Palace Theatre, over a century of famous acts have graced the stage - from Laurel and Hardy and Judy Garland to David Bowie and John Cleese. A tragic fire on stage in 1911 led to one of the most interesting stories in Edinburgh's history - join one of our backstage tours for a real insight into the fascinating past of this historic venue.
